TUAN-U-01-01.label: Hexagram 01 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-01-01.original: 大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。雲行雨施，品物流形，大明終始，六位時成。 時乘六龍以御天，乾道變化，各正性命，保合大和，乃利貞。 首出庶物，萬國咸寧。
TUAN-U-01-01.translation: Qian describes the vast creative force from which all things begin. Clouds move, rain falls, and living things take shape. The six lines unfold in their proper times, like six dragons carrying the movement of heaven. As this creative way changes, each being develops its own nature and finds harmony with the whole. When this leading force works rightly, the world can live in peace.

TUAN-U-02-01.label: Hexagram 02 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-02-01.original: 至哉坤元，萬物資生，乃順承天。坤厚載物，德合无疆；含弘光大，品物咸亨。牝馬地類，行地无疆，柔順利貞。 君子攸行，先迷失道，後順得常。 西南得朋，乃與類行，東北喪朋，乃終有慶。安貞之吉，應地无疆。
TUAN-U-02-01.translation: Kun describes the deep, receptive power through which all things are born and sustained. Earth follows heaven, carries everything, and supports life without limit. Its model is the mare: gentle, steady, and able to travel far. If a person tries to lead without understanding the way, they become lost. If they follow what is right, they regain a stable course. Finding companions in the southwest and letting go of them in the northeast both fit the situation. Quiet steadiness brings good fortune because it follows the boundless character of earth.

TUAN-U-03-01.label: Hexagram 03 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-03-01.original: 屯，剛柔始交而難生，動乎險中，大亨貞。雷雨之動滿盈，天造草昧，宜建侯而不寧。
TUAN-U-03-01.translation: Zhun shows firm and yielding forces meeting for the first time, so difficulty naturally appears. Movement begins inside danger, yet real progress is possible when people remain steady and act at the right time. Thunder and rain fill the world while everything is still confused and unsettled. Leaders and helpers should be appointed, but no one should pretend that order has already been secured.

TUAN-U-04-01.label: Hexagram 04 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-04-01.original: 蒙，山下有險，險而止，蒙。蒙亨，以亨行，時中也。匪我求童蒙，童蒙求我，志應也。初筮告，以剛中也。再三瀆，瀆則不告，瀆蒙也。蒙以養正，聖功也。
TUAN-U-04-01.translation: Meng describes inexperience and confusion: danger lies below the mountain, and movement comes to a stop. Progress is possible when teaching is given at the right time. The teacher does not chase after the inexperienced student; the student must sincerely ask to learn. A first honest question deserves an answer. Repeated careless questioning shows disrespect, so no further answer is given. Guiding beginners toward what is right is the work of a sage.

TUAN-U-05-01.label: Hexagram 05 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-05-01.original: 需，須也，險在前也；剛健而不陷，其義不困窮矣。需，有孚，光亨，貞吉，位乎天位，以正中也。利涉大川，往有功也。
TUAN-U-05-01.translation: Xu means waiting because danger lies ahead. The inner strength of the hexagram is firm, but it does not rush into danger, so it avoids being trapped. Sincerity brings clarity and success, and steadiness brings good fortune, because the fifth line is central, correct, and in the place of leadership. Crossing the great river is beneficial when the time is right because well-timed action can accomplish real work.

TUAN-U-06-01.label: Hexagram 06 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-06-01.original: 訟，上剛下險，險而健，訟。訟，有孚，窒，惕，中吉，剛來而得中也。終凶，訟不可成也。利見大人，尚中正也。不利涉大川，入于淵也。
TUAN-U-06-01.translation: Song means conflict. Strength is above and danger is below, showing how determination can turn into dispute when risk is present. Even when a claim is sincere, it may still meet resistance. Staying alert and stopping before the conflict goes too far brings good fortune; pushing the dispute to the bitter end brings misfortune. It is helpful to seek a fair and mature judge, but it is not a good time to take on a major undertaking.

TUAN-U-07-01.label: Hexagram 07 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-07-01.original: 師，眾也。貞，正也。能以眾正，可以王矣。剛中而應，行險而順，以此毒天下，而民從之，吉又何咎矣。
TUAN-U-07-01.translation: Shi means an organized group or army. Steadfastness here means keeping the group directed toward what is right. A capable leader who can guide many people with discipline may take on great responsibility. The firm central line receives support, showing leadership that earns cooperation. Acting in danger while remaining responsive to the people can bring good fortune, but the burden and hardship involved should never be taken lightly.

TUAN-U-08-01.label: Hexagram 08 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-08-01.original: 比，吉也。比，輔也，下順從也。原筮，元永貞，无咎，以剛中也。不寧方來，上下應也。後夫凶，其道窮也。
TUAN-U-08-01.translation: Bi means joining with and supporting one another, so it can bring good fortune. Those below willingly gather around a firm and central leader. The relationship remains sound only if that leader has lasting integrity and stays steady. People who feel unsettled will come seeking connection because the upper and lower parts respond to each other. Whoever arrives too late misses the proper time for joining and meets misfortune.

TUAN-U-09-01.label: Hexagram 09 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-09-01.original: 小畜，柔得位而上下應之，曰小畜。健而巽，剛中而志行，乃亨。密雲不雨，尚往也。自我西郊，施未行也。
TUAN-U-09-01.translation: Xiao Xu describes a small amount of restraint and accumulation. One yielding line holds its proper place, and the lines above and below respond to it. Firm strength rises but is temporarily held back. Inner strength is joined with outward gentleness, allowing the plan to move forward. Dense clouds without rain show that conditions are gathering but are not yet ready to release their full result.

TUAN-U-10-01.label: Hexagram 10 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-10-01.original: 履，柔履剛也。說而應乎乾，是以履虎尾，不咥人，亨。剛中正，履帝位而不疚，光明也。
TUAN-U-10-01.translation: Lu means walking carefully. A yielding line steps on firm strength, like treading on a tiger's tail, yet avoids being bitten because it responds with openness and respect. The firm central line holds the position of leadership without guilt. The brightness of the hexagram shows that people must recognize differences in rank and responsibility and act with proper conduct.

TUAN-U-11-01.label: Hexagram 11 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-11-01.original: 泰，小往大來，吉亨。則是天地交而萬物通也，上下交而其志同也。內陽而外陰，內健而外順，內君子而外小人，君子道長，小人道消也。
TUAN-U-11-01.translation: Its main message is this: tai means that the small departs and the great approaches, bringing good fortune and progress. Heaven and earth interact, so all things communicate and develop. Those above and below connect and share a common purpose. Yang is within and yin is outside; strength is within and receptiveness is outside; noble people advance while lesser people withdraw. The way of the noble person grows, and the way of the lesser person declines.

TUAN-U-12-01.label: Hexagram 12 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-12-01.original: 否之匪人，不利君子貞，大往小來。則是天地不交而萬物不通也，上下不交而天下无邦也。內陰而外陽，內柔而外剛，內小人而外君子，小人道長，君子道消也。
TUAN-U-12-01.translation: The hexagram explains the situation this way: pi describes a failure of people to understand and unite with one another. This does not favor the noble person’s steadfast course: the great departs and the small approaches. Heaven and earth do not interact, so all things are blocked. Those above and below do not communicate, so society loses order. Yin, weakness, and lesser people are within; yang, strength, and noble people are outside. The way of lesser people grows while the way of noble people declines.

TUAN-U-13-01.label: Hexagram 13 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-13-01.original: 同人，柔得位得中，而應乎乾，曰同人。同人曰，同人于野，亨。利涉大川，乾行也。文明以健，中正而應，君子正也。唯君子為能通天下之志。
TUAN-U-13-01.translation: In Tong Ren the weak line has the place of influence, the central place, and responds to the corresponding line in Qian above; therefore comes its name of Tong Ren or Union of men. Tong Ren says: The language, Tong Ren appears here as we find it in the remote districts of the country, indicating progress and success, and that it is favorable to cross the great stream, is moulded by its containing the strength symbolled in Qian. Then we have the trigram indicating elegance and intelligence, supported by that indicating strength; with the line in the central, and its correct, position, and responding to the corresponding line above: all representing the correct course of the noble person. It is only the noble person who can comprehend and affect the minds of all in the world.

TUAN-U-14-01.label: Hexagram 14 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-14-01.original: 大有，柔得尊位，大中而上下應之，曰大有。其德剛健而文明，應乎天而時行，是以元亨。
TUAN-U-14-01.translation: In Da You the weak line has the place of honour, is clearly central, and the strong lines above and below respond to it. Hence comes its name of Da You Having what is Great. The attributes of its component trigrams are strength and vigour with elegance and brightness. The ruling line in it responds to the ruling line in the symbol of heaven, and consequently its action is all at the proper times. In this way it is said to indicate great progress and success.

TUAN-U-15-01.label: Hexagram 15 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-15-01.original: 謙，亨，天道下濟而光明，地道卑而上行。天道虧盈而益謙，地道變盈而流謙，鬼神害盈而福謙，人道惡盈而好謙。謙尊而光，卑而不可逾，君子之終也。
TUAN-U-15-01.translation: Qian indicates progress and success. It is the way of heaven to send down its beneficial influences below, where they are brilliantly displayed. It is the way of earth, lying low, to send its influences upwards and there to act. It is the way of heaven to diminish the full and augment the humble. It is the way of earth to overthrow the full and replenish the humble. Spiritual Beings inflict serious trouble on the full and bless the humble. It is the way of men to hate the full and love the humble. Humility in a position of honour makes that still more brilliant; and in a low position men will not seek to pass beyond it. Therefore it is that the noble person will have a good issue to their undertakings.

TUAN-U-16-01.label: Hexagram 16 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-16-01.original: 豫，剛應而志行，順以動，豫。豫，順以動，故天地如之，而況建侯行師乎？天地以順動，故日月不過，而四時不忒；聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服。豫之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-U-16-01.translation: The hexagram explains the situation this way: yu arises when the firm line receives a response and its purpose can be carried out: receptiveness works through movement. Heaven and earth also move through this kind of harmony; how much more important is it when appointing leaders or mobilizing an army. Because nature moves in accord with order, the sun, moon, and seasons do not lose their timing. When sages act in accord with order, punishments are just and the people accept them. The timing and meaning of Yu are important.

TUAN-U-17-01.label: Hexagram 17 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-17-01.original: 隨，剛來而下柔，動而說，隨。大亨貞，无咎，而天下隨時，隨之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-U-17-01.translation: Its main message is this: sui means following. The firm trigram places itself below the yielding one, while movement joins with joy. Great progress is possible through steadfastness, with no blame. The world follows what is appropriate to the time. The timing and meaning of following are therefore important.

TUAN-U-18-01.label: Hexagram 18 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-18-01.original: 蠱，剛上而柔下，巽而止，蠱。蠱，元亨，而天下治也。利涉大川，往有事也。先甲三日，後甲三日，終則有始，天行也。
TUAN-U-18-01.translation: In Ku we have the strong trigram above, and the weak one below; we have below pliancy, and above stopping: these give the idea of K u a Troublous Condition of affairs verging to ruin. Ku indicates great progress and success: through the course shown in it, everyone in the world, this will bring good order. This will bring advantage in crossing the oreat stream: the person who advances will encounter the business to be done. The person should weigh well, however, the events of three days before the turning-point, and those to be done three days after it: the end of confusion is the beginning of order; such is the procedure of Heaven.

TUAN-U-19-01.label: Hexagram 19 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-19-01.original: 臨，剛浸而長。說而順，剛中而應，大亨以正，天之道也。至于八月有凶，消不久也。
TUAN-U-19-01.translation: In Lin the strong lines gradually increasing and advancing. The lower trigram is the symbol of being pleased, and the upper of being compliant. The strong line is in the central position, and is properly responded to. There is great progress and success, along with steadfastness: this is the way of Heaven. In the eighth month this brings misfortune: the advancing power will decay after no long time.

TUAN-U-20-01.label: Hexagram 20 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-20-01.original: 大觀在上，順而巽，中正以觀天下。觀，盥而不荐，有孚顒若，下觀而化也。觀天之神道，而四時不忒，聖人以神道設教，而天下服矣。
TUAN-U-20-01.translation: The great Manifester occupies an upper place in the figure, which consists of (the trigrams Kwan shows its subject like a worshipper who has washed their hands, but not yet presented their offerings; with sincerity and an appearance of dignity commanding reverent regard: all beneath look to them and are transformed. When we contemplate the spirit-like way of Heaven, how the four seasons proceed without error. The sages, following this image spirit-like way, laid down their instructions, and everyone in the world yield submission to them.

TUAN-U-21-01.label: Hexagram 21 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-21-01.original: 頤中有物，曰噬嗑，噬嗑而亨。剛柔分，動而明，雷電合而章。柔得中而上行，雖不當位，利用獄也。
TUAN-U-21-01.translation: The hexagram explains the situation this way: the existence of something between the jaws gives rise to the name Shih Ho Union by means of biting through the intervening article. The Union by means of biting through the intervening article indicates the progress denoted by the hexagram.

TUAN-U-22-01.label: Hexagram 22 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-22-01.original: 賁，亨；柔來而文剛，故亨。分剛上而文柔，故小利有攸往。剛柔交錯，天文也；文明以止，人文也。觀乎天文，以察時變；觀乎人文，以化成天下。
TUAN-U-22-01.translation: Its main message is this: bi means adornment. A yielding line comes to decorate firmness, allowing progress; a firm line rises to decorate what is yielding, so only small advances are favorable. The interweaving of firm and yielding forms the patterns of heaven. Clarity joined with restraint forms human culture. By observing heavenly patterns, we recognize seasonal change; by observing human culture, we educate and transform society.

TUAN-U-23-01.label: Hexagram 23 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-23-01.original: 剝，剝也，柔變剛也。不利有攸往，小人長也。順而止之，觀象也。君子尚消息盈虛，天行也。
TUAN-U-23-01.translation: The hexagram explains the situation this way: bo means stripping away: yielding lines are replacing the firm lines. Going forward is not favorable because the influence of lesser people is growing. Receptiveness joined with stopping shows that the noble person should understand the image and stop. The noble person values the cycles of decrease and increase, fullness and emptiness, which follow the movement of heaven.

TUAN-U-24-01.label: Hexagram 24 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-24-01.original: 復亨；剛反，動而以順行，是以出入无疾，朋來无咎。反復其道，七日來復，天行也。利有攸往，剛長也。復其見天地之心乎？
TUAN-U-24-01.translation: Fu indicates the progress of what it means: it is the coming back of what is intended by the undivided line. Its subjects actions show movement directed by accordance with natural order. Hence the person finds no one to distress them in their exits and entrances, and friends come to them, and no error is committed. The person will return and repeat their proper course; in seven days comes their return: such is the movement of the heavenly revolution. This will bring advantage in whatever direction movement is made: the strong lines are growing and increasing. Do we not see in Fu the mind of heaven and earth?

TUAN-U-25-01.label: Hexagram 25 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-25-01.original: 无妄，剛自外來，而為主於內。動而健，剛中而應，大亨以正，天之命也。其匪正有眚，不利有攸往。无妄之往，何之矣？ 天命不佑，行矣哉？
TUAN-U-25-01.translation: The hexagram explains the situation this way: in Wu Wang, a firm line comes from outside and becomes the leading force within. Movement joins with strength, and the central firm line receives a response. This is why great progress depends on acting correctly and in accord with Heaven. If the conduct is not right, trouble follows and it is not favorable to proceed. Without innocence and Heaven’s mandate, where could one rightly go?

TUAN-U-26-01.label: Hexagram 26 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-26-01.original: 大畜，剛健篤實輝光，日新其德，剛上而尚賢。能止健，大正也。不家食吉，養賢也。利涉大川，應乎天也。
TUAN-U-26-01.translation: In the trigrams composing Da Xu we have the attributes of the greatest strength and of substantial solidity, which emit a brilliant light; and indicate a daily renewal of their virtue by the person represented by it. The strong line is in the highest place, and suggests the value set on talents and virtue; there is power in the upper trigram to keep the strongest in restraint: all this shows the great correctness required in the hexagram. The good fortune attached to the subjects not seeking to enjoy their revenues in their own family shows how talents and virtue are nourished. It is favorable to cross the great stream: the fifth line, representing the ruler, is responded to by the second, the central line of Qian, representing Heaven.

TUAN-U-27-01.label: Hexagram 27 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-27-01.original: 頤貞吉，養正則吉也。觀頤，觀其所養也；自求口實，觀其自養也。天地養萬物，聖人養賢，以及萬民；頤之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-U-27-01.translation: 1 indicates that with steadfastness this brings good fortune: when the nourishing is correct, this brings good fortune. We must look at what we are seeking to nourish: we must look at those whom we wish to nourish. We must by the exercise of our thoughts seek the proper aliment: we must look to our own nourishing of ourselves. Heaven and earth nourish all things. The sages nourish men of talents and virtue, by them to reach to the myriads of the people. Great is the work intended by this nourishing in its time!

TUAN-U-28-01.label: Hexagram 28 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-28-01.original: 大過，大者過也。棟橈，本末弱也。剛過而中，巽而說行，利有攸往，乃亨。大過之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-U-28-01.translation: Its main message is this: da Guo means that the firm lines are in excess. The supporting beam bends because both ends are weak. Although firmness is excessive, the central lines remain balanced. Gentleness and joy support action, so it is favorable to go forward and progress is possible. The demands of this exceptional time are great.

TUAN-U-29-01.label: Hexagram 29 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-29-01.original: 習坎，重險也。水流而不盈，行險而不失其信。維心亨，乃以剛中也。行有尚，往有功也。天險不可升也，地險山川丘陵也，王公設險以守其國，坎之時用大矣哉！
TUAN-U-29-01.translation: Kan repeated shows us one defile succeeding another. This is the nature of water; it flows on, without accumulating its volume so as to overflow; it pursues its way through a dangerous defile, without losing its true nature. That the mind is penetrating is shown by the strong line in the centre. That action following this image will be of high value tells us that advance will be followed by achievement. The dangerous height of heaven cannot be ascended; the difficult places of the earth are moun tains, rivers, hills, and mounds. Kings and princes arrange, by means of such strengths, to maintain their territories. Great indeed is the use of what is here taught about seasons of danger.

TUAN-U-30-01.label: Hexagram 30 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-U-30-01.original: 離，麗也；日月麗乎天，百谷草木麗乎土，重明以麗乎正，乃化成天下。柔麗乎中正，故亨；是以畜牝牛吉也。
TUAN-U-30-01.translation: The hexagram explains the situation this way: li means being attached to. The sun and moon have their place in the sky. All the grains, grass, and trees have their place on the earth. The double brightness of the two trigrams adheres to what is correct, and the result is the transforming and perfecting all in the world. The weak second line occupies the middle and correct position, and gives the indication of a free and successful course; and, moreover, nourishing docility like that of the cow will lead to good fortune.

TUAN-L-31-01.label: Hexagram 31 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-31-01.original: 咸，感也。柔上而剛下，二氣感應以相與，止而說，男下女，是以亨利貞，取女吉也。天地感而萬物化生，聖人感人心而天下和平；觀其所感，而天地萬物之情可見矣！
TUAN-L-31-01.translation: Xian means mutual influence. The yielding trigram is above and the firm trigram below; the two respond to each other and unite. Stillness joins with joy, and the man places themself below the woman. Therefore progress and steadfastness are favorable, and marriage brings good fortune. Heaven and earth influence each other and all things are born. Sages influence human hearts and bring peace. By observing what things respond to, we can understand their nature.

TUAN-L-32-01.label: Hexagram 32 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-32-01.original: 恆，久也。剛上而柔下，雷風相與，巽而動，剛柔皆應，恆。恆亨无咎，利貞；久于其道也，天地之道，恆久而不已也。利有攸往，終則有始也。日月得天，而能久照，四時變化，而能久成，聖人久于其道，而天下化成；觀其所恆，而天地萬物之情可見矣！
TUAN-L-32-01.translation: Hang means long continuance. The strong trigram is above, and the weak one below; they are the symbols of thunder and wind, When the text says that Hang indicates progress and no error in what it means; but the advantage will come from being steadfast and right, this indicates that there must be long continuance in its way of operation. The way of heaven and earth is to be long continued in their operation without stopping. When the text says that Movement in any direction whatever will be beneficial, this implies that when the moving power is spent, it will begin again. The sun and moon, realising in themselves the course of Heaven, can perpetuate their shining. The four seasons, by their changing and transforming, can perpetuate their production of things. The sages persevere long in their course, and all in the world are transformed and perfect. When we look at what they continue doing long, the natural tendencies of heaven, earth, and all things can be seen.

TUAN-L-33-01.label: Hexagram 33 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-33-01.original: 遯亨，遯而亨也。剛當位而應，與時行也。小利貞，浸而長也。遯之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-L-33-01.translation: The hexagram explains the situation this way: dun brings progress through timely retreat. The firm line occupies the proper position and receives a response, so action follows the time. Limited persistence remains favorable because the influence of lesser people is gradually growing. The timing and meaning of retreat are important.

TUAN-L-34-01.label: Hexagram 34 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-34-01.original: 大壯，大者壯也。剛以動，故壯。大壯利貞；大者正也。正大而天地之情可見矣！
TUAN-L-34-01.translation: Its main message is this: da Zhuang means great strength. Strength acts through movement, creating power. Steadfastness is favorable because true greatness must also be correct. When greatness and correctness are united, the character of heaven and earth becomes visible.

TUAN-L-35-01.label: Hexagram 35 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-35-01.original: 晉，進也。明出地上，順而麗乎大明，柔進而上行。是以康侯用錫馬蕃庶，晝日三接也。
TUAN-L-35-01.translation: The hexagram explains the situation this way: jin means advancing. Light rises above the earth; receptiveness follows and attaches to great brightness, while a yielding line advances upward. This is why the secure prince receives many horses and is granted three audiences in one day.

TUAN-L-36-01.label: Hexagram 36 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-36-01.original: 明入地中，明夷。內文明而外柔順，以蒙大難，文王以之。利艱貞，晦其明也，內難而能正其志，箕子以之。
TUAN-L-36-01.translation: The symbol of the Earth and that of Brightness entering into the midst of it give the idea of Ming I Brightness wounded or obscured. The inner trigram means being accomplished and bright; the outer, being pliant and submissive. The case of kinoWan was that of one who with these qualities was yet involved in great difficulties. It is favorable to realise the difficulty of the position, and maintain steadfastness: that is, the individual concerned should obscure their brightness. The case of the count of Ki was that of one who, amidst the difficulties of their House, was able therefore to maintain their aim and mind correct.

TUAN-L-37-01.label: Hexagram 37 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-37-01.original: 家人，女正位乎內，男正位乎外，男女正，天地之大義也。家人有嚴君焉，父母之謂也。父父，子子，兄兄，弟弟，夫夫，婦婦，而家道正；正家而天下定矣。
TUAN-L-37-01.translation: In Jia Ren the wife has her correct place in the inner trigram, and the man their correct place in the outer. That man and woman occupy their correct places is the great righteousness shown in the relation and positions of heaven and earth. In Jia Ren we have the idea of an authoritative ruler; that, namely, represented by the parental authority. Let the father be indeed father, and the son son; let the elder brother be indeed elder brother, and the younger brother younger brother; let the husband be indeed husband, and the wife wife: then will the family be in its normal state. Bring the family to that state, and everyone in the world will be established.

TUAN-L-38-01.label: Hexagram 38 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-38-01.original: 睽，火動而上，澤動而下；二女同居，其志不同行；說而麗乎明，柔進而上行，得中而應乎剛；是以小事吉。天地睽，而其事同也；男女睽，而其志通也；萬物睽，而其事類也；睽之時用大矣哉！
TUAN-L-38-01.translation: Its main message is this: kui means opposition. Fire moves upward while the lake moves downward; two women live together but pursue different aims. Yet joy attaches to clarity, and the advancing yielding line is central and responds to firmness. Therefore small matters bring good fortune. Heaven and earth differ but carry out a common work; men and women differ but can share a purpose; all things differ but belong to related kinds. The use of opposition is important.

TUAN-L-39-01.label: Hexagram 39 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-39-01.original: 蹇，難也，險在前也。見險而能止，知矣哉！蹇利西南，往得中也；不利東北，其道窮也。利見大人，往有功也。當位貞吉，以正邦也。蹇之時用大矣哉！
TUAN-L-39-01.translation: Jian means difficulty. There is the trigram expressive of danger in front. When one, seeing the danger, can arrest their steps in accordance with the significance of the lower trigram, is the person not wise? The language of Jian, that advantage will be found in the south-west, refers to the strong fifth line advanced and in the central place. That this will bring no advantage in the north-east, indicates that the way of dealing with the Jian state is exhausted. That it is favorable to see the great person, indicates that advance will lead to achievement. That the places of the different lines after the first are those appropriate to them indicates steadfastness and good fortune, with which the regions of the kingdom are brought to their normal state. Great indeed is the work to be done in the time of Jian!

TUAN-L-40-01.label: Hexagram 40 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-40-01.original: 解，險以動，動而免乎險，解。解利西南，往得眾也。其來復吉，乃得中也。有攸往夙吉，往有功也。天地解，而雷雨作，雷雨作，而百果草木皆甲坼，解之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-L-40-01.translation: In Jie we have the trigram expressive of danger going on to that expressive of movement. By movement there is an escape from the danger: this is the meaning of Jie. In the state shown by Jie, advantage will be found in the south-west: the movement therefore indicated will win all. That this brings good fortune in coming back to the old conditions shows that such action is that of the due medium. That if some operations be necessary, this brings good fortune in the early conducting of them shows that such operations will be successful. When heaven and earth are freed from the grasp of winter, we have thunder and rain. When these come, the buds of the plants and trees that produce the various fruits begin to burst. Great indeed are the phenomena in the time shown by Jie.

TUAN-L-41-01.label: Hexagram 41 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-41-01.original: 損，損下益上，其道上行。損而有孚，元吉，无咎，可貞，利有攸往。曷之用？二簋可用享；二簋應有時。損剛益柔有時，損益盈虛，與時偕行。
TUAN-L-41-01.translation: In Sun the lower trigram diminished, and the upper added to. But the method of action implied in this operates also above or, mounts upwards also and operates. If there be sincerity in this method of diminution, this will bring great good fortune; freedom from error; steadfast conduct that can be maintained; and advantage in every movement that will be made. In what will this sincerity in the exercise of Sun be employed? Even in sacrifice, two baskets of grain, though there be nothing else, may be presented: for these two baskets there ought to be the fitting time. There is a time when the strong should be diminished, and the weak should be strengthened. Diminution and increase, overflowing and emptiness: these take place in harmony with the conditions of the time.

TUAN-L-42-01.label: Hexagram 42 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-42-01.original: 益，損上益下，民說无疆，自上下下，其道大光。利有攸往，中正有慶。利涉大川，木道乃行。益動而巽，日進无疆。天施地生，其益无方。凡益之道，與時偕行。
TUAN-L-42-01.translation: The hexagram explains the situation this way: yi means reducing what is above in order to increase what is below. The people rejoice without limit, and those above place themselves at the service of those below. Going forward is favorable because the central and correct path brings blessing. Crossing the great river is favorable, like wood moving over water. Movement joined with gentleness produces daily progress. Heaven gives and earth gives birth, so growth has no fixed limit. Increase must always fit the needs of the time.

TUAN-L-43-01.label: Hexagram 43 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-43-01.original: 夬，決也，剛決柔也。健而說，決而和，揚于王庭，柔乘五剛也。孚號有厲，其危乃光也。告自邑，不利即戎，所尚乃窮也。利有攸往，剛長乃終也。
TUAN-L-43-01.translation: Its main message is this: guai is the symbol of displacing or removing. in the figure the strong lines displacing the weak. We have in it the attributes of strength and complacency. There is displacement, but harmony continues. The exhibition of the criminals guilt in the royal courtyard is suggested by the one weak line mounted on the five strong lines.

TUAN-L-44-01.label: Hexagram 44 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-44-01.original: 姤，遇也，柔遇剛也。勿用取女，不可與長也。天地相遇，品物咸章也。剛遇中正，天下大行也。姤之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-L-44-01.translation: Gou has the significance of unexpectedly coming on. in it the weak line coming unexpectedly on the strong one's. It will not be good to marry such a female: one so symbolised should not be long associated with. Heaven and earth meeting together as here represented, all the variety of natural things become fully displayed. When a strong line finds itself in the central and correct position, good government will greatly prevail all in the world. Great indeed is the significance of what has to be done at the time shown by Gou!

TUAN-L-45-01.label: Hexagram 45 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-45-01.original: 萃，聚也；順以說，剛中而應，故聚也。王假有廟，致孝享也。利見大人亨，聚以正也。用大牲吉，利有攸往，順天命也。觀其所聚，而天地萬物之情可見矣。
TUAN-L-45-01.translation: Its main message is this: cui means gathering. Receptiveness joins with joy, and the central firm line receives a response, so people gather. The king approaches the ancestral temple to express devotion through offerings. It is favorable to meet a great person because the gathering is guided by what is right. A great offering and forward action are favorable when they follow Heaven’s order. By observing gatherings, we can understand the tendencies of heaven, earth, and all things.

TUAN-L-46-01.label: Hexagram 46 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-46-01.original: 柔以時升，巽而順，剛中而應，是以大亨。用見大人，勿恤；有慶也。南征吉，志行也。
TUAN-L-46-01.translation: We find the weak line, as it finds the opportunity, ascending upwards. We have the attribute of flexibility and that of obedience; we have the strong line below and its proper correlate above: these things indicate that this will bring great progress and success.

TUAN-L-47-01.label: Hexagram 47 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-47-01.original: 困，剛掩也。險以說，困而不失其所，亨；其唯君子乎？ 貞大人吉，以剛中也。有言不信，尚口乃窮也。
TUAN-L-47-01.translation: Kun shows firm lines covered by yielding one's. Danger is joined with joy. The noble person can remain true to the proper course even under pressure, and therefore can still make progress. Steadfastness brings good fortune to the great person because the firm line is central. Mere words are not trusted; relying on speech alone leads to exhaustion.

TUAN-L-48-01.label: Hexagram 48 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-48-01.original: 巽乎水而上水，井；井養而不窮也。改邑不改井，乃以剛中也。汔至亦未繘井，未有功也。羸其瓶，是以凶也。
TUAN-L-48-01.translation: We have the symbol of wood in the water and the raising of the water; which gives us the idea of a well. A well supplies nourishment and is not itself exhausted. The site of a town may be changed, while the fashion of its wells undergoes no change: this is shown by the central position of the strong lines in the second and fifth places.

TUAN-L-49-01.label: Hexagram 49 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-49-01.original: 革，水火相息，二女同居，其志不相得，曰革。巳日乃孚；革而信也。文明以說，大亨以正，革而當，其悔乃亡。天地革而四時成，湯武革命，順乎天而應乎人，革之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-L-49-01.translation: Its main message is this: ge means change. Water and fire oppose each other, and two women live together without sharing the same purpose. Change is trusted only after it has been completed. Clarity joined with joy brings great progress through correctness; when change fits the time, regret disappears. Heaven and earth change and the four seasons are completed. Tang and Wu changed dynasties in accord with Heaven and in response to the people. The timing of change is crucial.

TUAN-L-50-01.label: Hexagram 50 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-50-01.original: 鼎，象也。以木巽火，亨飪也。聖人亨以享上帝，而大亨以養聖賢。巽而耳目聰明，柔進而上行，得中而應乎剛，是以元亨。
TUAN-L-50-01.translation: Its main message is this: ding presents the image of a cauldron. Wood enters the fire so that food can be cooked. The sages used cooking to present offerings to the highest power and to nourish worthy and capable people. Gentleness below and clear perception above allow the yielding line to rise, take the central place, and respond to the firm line. This is why the hexagram promises great success.

TUAN-L-51-01.label: Hexagram 51 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-51-01.original: 震，亨。震來虩虩，恐致福也。笑言啞啞，后有則也。震驚百里，驚遠而懼邇也。出可以守宗廟社稷，以為祭主也。
TUAN-L-51-01.translation: The hexagram explains the situation this way: zhen indicates movement and development. The shock first brings fear, and that fear can lead to good fortune by making a person careful. Laughter afterward shows that order has been restored. The shock is heard for a hundred miles: it alarms those far away and warns those nearby. The person who remains composed can protect the ancestral temple and serve as leader of the rites.

TUAN-L-52-01.label: Hexagram 52 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-52-01.original: 艮，止也。時止則止，時行則行，動靜不失其時，其道光明。艮其止，止其所也。上下敵應，不相與也。是以不獲其身，行其庭不見其人，无咎也。
TUAN-L-52-01.translation: Its main message is this: gen means stopping. Stop when the time calls for stopping, and act when the time calls for action. When movement and stillness both fit the time, the way becomes clear. To keep the back still means stopping in the proper place. The upper and lower lines oppose rather than support one another. Therefore one does not become absorbed in the self; one may walk through the courtyard without being distracted by other people. There is no blame.

TUAN-L-53-01.label: Hexagram 53 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-53-01.original: 漸之進也，女歸吉也。進得位，往有功也。進以正，可以正邦也。其位剛，得中也。止而巽，動不窮也。
TUAN-L-53-01.translation: The advance shown by Jian is like the marrying of a young lady which is attended by good fortune. The lines as they advance get into their correct places: this indicates the achievements of a progress. Among the places of the hexagram the strong undivided line in the centre. In the attributes of restfulness and flexible penetration we have the assurance of an onward movement that is inexhaustible.

TUAN-L-54-01.label: Hexagram 54 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-54-01.original: 歸妹，天地之大義也。天地不交，而萬物不興，歸妹人之終始也。說以動，所歸妹也。征凶，位不當也。无攸利，柔乘剛也。
TUAN-L-54-01.translation: By Gui Mei the marrying away of a younger sister the great and righteous relation between heaven and earth is suggested to us. If heaven and earth were to have no intercommunication, things would not grow and flourish as they do. The marriage of a younger sister is the end of her young womanhood and the beginning of her motherhood. We have in the hexagram the desire of Any action will be misfortune: the places of the lines are not those appropriate to them.

TUAN-L-55-01.label: Hexagram 55 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-55-01.original: 豐，大也。明以動，故豐。王假之，尚大也。勿憂宜日中，宜照天下也。日中則昃，月盈則食，天地盈虛，與時消息，而況于人乎？況于鬼神乎？
TUAN-L-55-01.translation: Feng means abundance. Clarity joined with movement creates abundance. The king reaches this state because the person values greatness. Do not worry; be like the sun at noon and let the light reach everyone. Yet the sun begins to decline at noon, and the full moon begins to wane. Heaven and earth move between fullness and emptiness with the seasons; human affairs change even more. The timing of abundance is therefore very important.

TUAN-L-56-01.label: Hexagram 56 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-56-01.original: 旅，小亨，柔得中乎外，而順乎剛，止而麗乎明，是以小亨，旅貞吉也。旅之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-L-56-01.translation: Its main message is this: lu indicates that there may be some small attainment and progress: the weak line occupies the central place in the outer trigram, and is obedient to the strong lines on either side of it. We have also the attributes of quiet resting closely attached to intelligence (in the com Great is the time and great is the right course to be taken as indicated in Lu!

TUAN-L-57-01.label: Hexagram 57 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-57-01.original: 重巽以申命，剛巽乎中正而志行。柔皆順乎剛，是以小亨，利有攸往，利見大人。
TUAN-L-57-01.translation: The double Sun shows how, following this example, governmental orders are reiterated. that the strong fifth line has penetrated into the central and correct place, and the will of its subject is being carried into effect; also the weak first and fourth lines both obedient to the strong lines above them. It is therefore said, c This will bring some little attainment and progress. This will bring advantage in movement onward in whatever direction. It will be beneficial also to see the great person.

TUAN-L-58-01.label: Hexagram 58 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-58-01.original: 兌，說也。剛中而柔外，說以利貞，是以順乎天，而應乎人。說以先民，民忘其勞；說以犯難，民忘其死；說之大，民勸矣哉！
TUAN-L-58-01.translation: Its main message is this: dui means joy. Firmness is central and yielding lines are outside. Joy is beneficial when joined with steadfastness, because it then accords with Heaven and responds to people. When joy leads the people, they forget their labor; when it helps them face danger, they forget the fear of death. Properly used, the power of joy encourages people.

TUAN-L-59-01.label: Hexagram 59 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-59-01.original: 渙，亨。剛來而不窮，柔得位乎外而上同。王假有廟，王乃在中也。利涉大川，乘木有功也。
TUAN-L-59-01.translation: Huan indicates that this will bring progress and success: the strong line in the second place of the lower trigram, and not suffering any extinction there; and also the weak line occupying its place in the outer trigram, and uniting its action with that of the line above. The king goes to their ancestral temple: the kings mind is without any deflection. It is favorable to cross the great stream: the person represented by the hexagram rides in a vessel of wood over water, and will do so with success.

TUAN-L-60-01.label: Hexagram 60 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-60-01.original: 節，亨，剛柔分，而剛得中。苦節不可貞，其道窮也。說以行險，當位以節，中正以通。天地節而四時成，節以制度，不傷財，不害民。
TUAN-L-60-01.translation: The hexagram explains the situation this way: jie means limitation and order. Firm and yielding lines are divided, while the firm lines hold central positions, so progress is possible. Bitter and oppressive limits cannot last because their way becomes exhausted. Joy moves through danger, and proper position creates suitable limits; centrality and correctness keep communication open. Heaven and earth have limits, and the four seasons are formed. Good institutions protect resources without harming the people.

TUAN-L-61-01.label: Hexagram 61 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-61-01.original: 中孚，柔在內而剛得中。說而巽，孚，乃化邦也。豚魚吉，信及豚魚也。利涉大川，乘木舟虛也。中孚以利貞，乃應乎天也。
TUAN-L-61-01.translation: In Zhong Fu we have the two weak lines in the innermost part of the figure, and strong lines occupying the central places in the trigrams. We have the attributes of joy and flexible penetration. Sincerity therefore symbolled will transform a country. Pigs and fish are moved, and this brings good fortune: sincerity reaches to and affects even pigs and fishes. In the exercise of the virtue denoted by Acting Fu, the text says that this will bring advantage in being; steadfast and right: in that virtue indeed we have the response of man to Heaven.

TUAN-L-62-01.label: Hexagram 62 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-62-01.original: 小過，小者過而亨也。過以利貞，與時行也。柔得中，是以小事吉也。剛失位而不中，是以不可大事也。有飛鳥之象焉，有飛鳥遺之音，不宜上宜下，大吉；上逆而下順也。
TUAN-L-62-01.translation: In Xiao Guo the small lines exceeding the others, and giving the intimation of progress and attainment. Such exceeding, in order to its being beneficial, must be associated with steadfast conduct: that is, it must take place only according to the requirements of the time. The weak lines are in the central places, and therefore the text says that what the name means may be done in small affairs, and this brings good fortune. Of the strong lines one is not in its proper place, and the other is not central, therefore the text says that what the name means should not be done in great affairs. In the hexagram we have the symbol of a bird on the wing, and of the notes that come down from such a bird, for which it is better to descend than to ascend, thereby leading to great good fortune: to ascend is contrary to what is reasonable in the case, while to descend is natural and right.

TUAN-L-63-01.label: Hexagram 63 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-63-01.original: 既濟，亨，小者亨也。利貞，剛柔正而位當也。初吉，柔得中也。終止則亂，其道窮也。
TUAN-L-63-01.translation: Ji Ji indicates progress and success: in small matters, that is, this will bring that progress and success. This will bring advantage in being steadfast and right: the strong and weak lines are correctly arranged, each in its appropriate place. There has been good fortune in the beginning: the weak second line is in the centre. In the end there is a cessation of effort, and disorder arises: the course that led to rule and order is now exhausted.

TUAN-L-64-01.label: Hexagram 64 Tuan Commentary
TUAN-L-64-01.original: 未濟，亨；柔得中也。小狐汔濟，未出中也。濡其尾，无攸利；不續終也。雖不當位，剛柔應也。
TUAN-L-64-01.translation: The hexagram explains the situation this way: wei Ji promises progress because the yielding fifth line holds the central position. The young fox has almost crossed, but has not yet escaped danger. Wetting its tail brings no advantage because the crossing cannot be completed. Although the lines are not in their proper positions, the firm and yielding lines still respond to one another.

XIANG-U-01-01.label: Hexagram 01 Great Image
XIANG-U-01-01.original: 天行健，君子以自強不息。
XIANG-U-01-01.translation: Heaven, in its motion, gives the idea of strength. The noble person, following this image, nerves themself to ceaseless activity.

XIANG-U-01-02.label: Hexagram 01 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-01-02.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the dragon lies hid in the deep; it is not the time for active doing: this appears from the strong and undivided lines being in the lowest place.

XIANG-U-01-03.label: Hexagram 01 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-01-03.translation: This line or image shows that the dragon appears in the field: the diffusion of virtuous influence has been wide.

XIANG-U-01-04.label: Hexagram 01 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-01-04.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: active and vigilant all the day: this refers to the treading of the proper path over and over again.

XIANG-U-01-05.label: Hexagram 01 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-01-05.translation: The person seems to be leaping up, but is still in the deep: if the person advance, there is no blame.

XIANG-U-01-06.label: Hexagram 01 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-01-06.translation: The dragon is on the wing in the sky: the great person rouses themself to their work.

XIANG-U-01-07.label: Hexagram 01 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-01-07.translation: The dragon exceeds the proper limits; this will bring cause for regret: a state of fulness, that is, should not be indulged in long.

XIANG-U-01-08.label: Hexagram 01 Line Image 7
XIANG-U-01-08.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the same undivided line is used in all the places of this hexagram, but the attribute of heaven thereby denoted should not always take the foremost place.

XIANG-U-02-01.label: Hexagram 02 Great Image
XIANG-U-02-01.original: 地勢坤，君子以厚德載物。
XIANG-U-02-01.translation: The capacity and sustaining power of the earth is what is denoted by Kun. The noble person, following this image, with their large virtue supports men and things.

XIANG-U-02-02.label: Hexagram 02 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-02-02.original: 履霜堅冰，陰始凝也。馴致其道，至堅冰也。
XIANG-U-02-02.translation: The person is treading on hoarfrost; the strong ice will come by and by: the cold air has begun to take form. Allow it to go on quietly according to its nature, and the hoarfrost will come to strong ice.

XIANG-U-02-03.label: Hexagram 02 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-02-03.original: 六二之動，直以方也。不習无不利，地道光也。
XIANG-U-02-03.translation: The movement shown by the second yielding line, is from the straight line to the square. Its operation, without repeated effort, in every way beneficial, shows the brilliant result of the way of earth.

XIANG-U-02-04.label: Hexagram 02 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-02-04.original: 含章可貞，以時發也。或從王事，知光大也。
XIANG-U-02-04.translation: The person keeps their excellence under restraint, but firmly maintains it: at the proper time the person will manifest it. The person may have occasion to engage in the kings service: great is the glory of their wisdom.

XIANG-U-02-05.label: Hexagram 02 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-02-05.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: a sack tied up; there is no blame: this shows how, through carefulness, no injury will be received.

XIANG-U-02-06.label: Hexagram 02 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-02-06.translation: The yellow lower-garment; this will bring great good fortune: this follows from that ornamental colours being in the right and central place.

XIANG-U-02-07.label: Hexagram 02 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-02-07.translation: The dragons fight in the wild: the onward course shown by Kun is pursued to extremity.

XIANG-U-02-08.label: Hexagram 02 Line Image 7
XIANG-U-02-08.translation: The lines are all weak and divided, as appears from the use of the number six: but those who are therefore represented becoming perpetually steadfast and principled, there will thereby be a great consummation.

XIANG-U-03-01.label: Hexagram 03 Great Image
XIANG-U-03-01.translation: The trigram representing clouds and that representing thunder form Zhun. The noble person, following this image, adjusts their measures of government as in sorting the threads of the warp and woof.

XIANG-U-03-02.label: Hexagram 03 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-03-02.original: 雖磐桓，志行正也。以貴下賤，大得民也。
XIANG-U-03-02.translation: Although there is a difficulty in advancing, the mind of the person represented by the line is set on doing what is correct. While noble, the person humbles themself to the mean, and clearly gains the people.

XIANG-U-03-03.label: Hexagram 03 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-03-03.original: 六二之難，乘剛也。十年乃字，反常也。
XIANG-U-03-03.translation: The difficulty to the person represented by the second yielding line, arises from its place over the undivided line below it. The union and children after ten years shows things resuming their regular course.

XIANG-U-03-04.label: Hexagram 03 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-03-04.original: 即鹿无虞，以從禽也。君子舍之，往吝窮也。
XIANG-U-03-04.translation: One pursues the deer without the guidance of the forester: the person does so in their eagerness to follow the game. The noble person gives up the chase, knowing that if the person go forward the person will regret it: the person would be reduced to extremity.

XIANG-U-03-05.label: Hexagram 03 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-03-05.translation: This line or image shows that going forward after such a search for a helper shows intelligence.

XIANG-U-03-06.label: Hexagram 03 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-03-06.translation: Difficulty is experienced by the person represented by the fifth line in bestowing their rich favours: the extent to which they reach will not yet be conspicuous.

XIANG-U-03-07.label: Hexagram 03 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-03-07.translation: The person weeps tears of blood in streams: how can the state therefore emblemed continue long?

XIANG-U-04-01.label: Hexagram 04 Great Image
XIANG-U-04-01.original: 山下出泉，蒙；君子以果行育德。
XIANG-U-04-01.translation: The trigram representing a mountain, and beneath it that for a spring issuing forth form Mang. The noble person, following this image, strives to be resolute in their conduct and nourishes their virtue.

XIANG-U-04-02.label: Hexagram 04 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-04-02.translation: This line or image shows that it is favorable to use punishment: the object being to bring under the influence of correcting law.

XIANG-U-04-03.label: Hexagram 04 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-04-03.translation: A son able to sustain the burden of their family: as appears from the reciprocation between this strong line and the weak fifth line.

XIANG-U-04-04.label: Hexagram 04 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-04-04.translation: This line or image shows that a woman such as is here represented should not be taken in marriage: her conduct is not agreeable to what is right.

XIANG-U-04-05.label: Hexagram 04 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-04-05.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the regret arising from ignorance bound in chains is due to the special distance of the person represented by this line from the solidity shown in lines 2 and 6.

XIANG-U-04-06.label: Hexagram 04 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-04-06.translation: The good fortune belonging to the simple lad without experience comes from their docility going on to humility.

XIANG-U-04-07.label: Hexagram 04 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-04-07.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: advantage will come from warding off injury: the person represented by this line above and the ignorant below, all do and are done to in accordance with their nature.

XIANG-U-05-01.label: Hexagram 05 Great Image
XIANG-U-05-01.original: 雲上於天，需；君子以飲食宴樂。
XIANG-U-05-01.translation: The trigram for clouds ascending over that for the sky forms Xu. The noble person, following this image, eats and drinks, feasts and enjoys themself as if there were nothing else to employ them.

XIANG-U-05-02.label: Hexagram 05 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-05-02.original: 需于郊，不犯難行也。利用恆，无咎，未失常也。
XIANG-U-05-02.translation: The person is waiting in the distant border: the person makes no movement to encounter rashly the difficulties of the situation. It will be beneficial for them constantly to maintain the purpose therefore shown, in which case there is no blame: the person will not fail to pursue that regular course.

XIANG-U-05-03.label: Hexagram 05 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-05-03.original: 需于沙，衍在中也。雖小有言，以終吉也。
XIANG-U-05-03.translation: The person is waiting on the sand: the person occupies their position in the centre with a generous forbearance. Though the person suffer the small injury of being spoken against, the person will bring things to a good issue.

XIANG-U-05-04.label: Hexagram 05 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-05-04.original: 需于泥，災在外也。自我致寇，敬慎不敗也。
XIANG-U-05-04.translation: The person is waiting in the mud: serious trouble is close at hand, and as it were in the outer trigram. The person themself invites the approach of injury: if the person be reverent and careful, the person will not be worsted.

XIANG-U-05-05.label: Hexagram 05 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-05-05.translation: The person is waiting in the place of blood: the person accommodates themself to the circumstances of the time, and hearkens to its requirements.

XIANG-U-05-06.label: Hexagram 05 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-05-06.translation: The appliances of a feast, and the good fortune through being steadfast and right, are indicated, by the position in the central and correct place.

XIANG-U-05-07.label: Hexagram 05 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-05-07.original: 不速之客來，敬之終吉。雖不當位，未大失也。
XIANG-U-05-07.translation: Guests come unurged to give their help, and if the person represented by the line receive them respectfully, this brings good fortune in the end: though the occupant and the place are not suited to each other, there has been no great failure in what has been done.

XIANG-U-06-01.label: Hexagram 06 Great Image
XIANG-U-06-01.original: 天與水違行，訟；君子以作事謀始。
XIANG-U-06-01.translation: The trigram representing heaven and that representing water, moving away from each other, form Song. The noble person, following this image, in the transaction of affairs takes good counsel about their first steps.

XIANG-U-06-02.label: Hexagram 06 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-06-02.original: 不永所事，訟不可長也。雖小有言，其辯明也。
XIANG-U-06-02.translation: The person does not perpetuate the matter about which the contention is: contention should not be prolonged. Although the person may suffer the small injury of being spoken against, their argument is clear.

XIANG-U-06-03.label: Hexagram 06 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-06-03.original: 不克訟，歸逋竄也。自下訟上，患至掇也。
XIANG-U-06-03.translation: The person is unequal to the contention; the person retires and keeps concealed, stealthily withdrawing from it: for them from their lower place to contend with the stronger one above, would be to invite serious trouble, as if the person brought it with their hand to themself.

XIANG-U-06-04.label: Hexagram 06 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-06-04.translation: The person confines themself to the support assigned to them of old: therefore following those above them, the person will have good fortune.

XIANG-U-06-05.label: Hexagram 06 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-06-05.translation: The person returns to the study of Heavens ordinances, changes their wish to contend, and rests in being steadfast and right: the person does not fail in doing what is right.

XIANG-U-06-06.label: Hexagram 06 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-06-06.translation: The person contends; and with great fortune: this is shown by their holding the due mean and being in the correct place.

XIANG-U-06-07.label: Hexagram 06 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-06-07.translation: The person receives the robe through their contention: but still the person is not deserving of respect.

XIANG-U-07-01.label: Hexagram 07 Great Image
XIANG-U-07-01.original: 地中有水，師；君子以容民畜衆。
XIANG-U-07-01.translation: The trigram representing the earth and in the midst of it that representing water, form Shi. The noble person, following this image, nourishes and educates the people, and collects from among them the multitudes of the hosts.

XIANG-U-07-02.label: Hexagram 07 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-07-02.translation: The host goes forth according to the rules for such a movement: if those rules be not observed, this brings misfortune.

XIANG-U-07-03.label: Hexagram 07 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-07-03.original: 在師中吉，承天寵也。王三錫命，懷萬邦也。
XIANG-U-07-03.translation: The person is in the midst of the host, and this brings good fortune: the person has received the favour of Heaven. The king has thrice conveyed to them the orders of their favour: the king cherishes the myriad regions in their heart.

XIANG-U-07-04.label: Hexagram 07 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-07-04.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the host with the possibility of its having many idle leaders: great will be its want of success.

XIANG-U-07-05.label: Hexagram 07 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-07-05.translation: This line or image shows that the host is in retreat; but there is no error: there has been no failure in the regular course.

XIANG-U-07-06.label: Hexagram 07 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-07-06.original: 長子帥師，以中行也。弟子輿尸，使不當也。
XIANG-U-07-06.translation: The oldest son leads the host: its movements are directed by them in accordance with their position in the centre. Younger men idly occupy their positions: the employment of such men is improper.

XIANG-U-07-07.label: Hexagram 07 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-07-07.original: 大君有命，以正功也。小人勿用，必亂邦也。
XIANG-U-07-07.translation: The great ruler delivers their charges: thereby the person rightly apportions merit. Small men should not be employed: they are sure to throw the states into confusion.

XIANG-U-08-01.label: Hexagram 08 Great Image
XIANG-U-08-01.original: 地上有水，比；先王以建萬國，親諸侯。
XIANG-U-08-01.translation: The trigram representing the earth, and over it that representing water, form Bi. The ancient kings, following this image, established the various states and maintained an affectionate relation to their princes.

XIANG-U-08-02.label: Hexagram 08 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-08-02.translation: From the seeking union with its object shown in the first yielding line, this will bring other advantages.

XIANG-U-08-03.label: Hexagram 08 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-08-03.translation: The movement towards union and attachment proceeds from the inward mind: the party concerned does not fail in what is proper to themself.

XIANG-U-08-04.label: Hexagram 08 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-08-04.translation: This line or image shows that union is sought with such as ought not to be associated with: but will not injury be the result?

XIANG-U-08-05.label: Hexagram 08 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-08-05.translation: Union is sought by the party intended here with one beyond themself, and in this case with a worthy object: the person is following the ruler above them.

XIANG-U-08-06.label: Hexagram 08 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-08-06.original: 顯比之吉，位正中也。舍逆取順，失前禽也。邑人不誡，上使中也。
XIANG-U-08-06.translation: The good fortune belonging to the most illustrious instance of seeking union and attachment appears in the correct and central position of the fifth firm line.

XIANG-U-08-07.label: Hexagram 08 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-08-07.translation: The person seeks union and attachment without taking the first step to such an end: there is no possibility of a good issue.

XIANG-U-09-01.label: Hexagram 09 Great Image
XIANG-U-09-01.original: 風行天上，小畜，君子以懿文德。
XIANG-U-09-01.translation: The trigram representing the sky, and that representing wind moving above it, form Xiao Xu. The noble person, following this image, adorns the outward manifestation of their virtue.

XIANG-U-09-02.label: Hexagram 09 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-09-02.translation: The person returns and pursues their own path: it is right that there should be good fortune.

XIANG-U-09-03.label: Hexagram 09 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-09-03.translation: By the attraction of the person represented by the former line the person returns to its own course, and is in the central place: neither will the person err in what is due from them.

XIANG-U-09-04.label: Hexagram 09 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-09-04.translation: Husband and wife look on each other with averted eyes: the person represented by line three is like a husband who cannot maintain correctly their relations with their wife.

XIANG-U-09-05.label: Hexagram 09 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-09-05.translation: The person is possessed of sincerity; their ground for apprehension is dismissed: the subjects of the lines above agree in aim with them.

XIANG-U-09-06.label: Hexagram 09 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-09-06.translation: The person is possessed of sincerity, and draws others to unite with them: the person does not use only their own rich resources.

XIANG-U-09-07.label: Hexagram 09 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-09-07.original: 既雨既處，德積載也。君子征凶，有所疑也。
XIANG-U-09-07.translation: The rain has fallen and the onward progress is stayed: the power denoted in the figure has accumulated to the full. If the noble person prosecute their measures, this brings misfortune: the person will find themself obstructed.

XIANG-U-10-01.label: Hexagram 10 Great Image
XIANG-U-10-01.original: 上天下澤，履；君子以辨上下，定民志。
XIANG-U-10-01.translation: The trigram representing the sky above, and below it that representing the waters of a marsh, form Li. The noble person, following this image, discriminates between high and low, and gives settlement to the aims of the people.

XIANG-U-10-02.label: Hexagram 10 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-10-02.translation: The person treads their accustomed path and goes forward: singly and exclusively the person carries out their long-cherished wishes.

XIANG-U-10-03.label: Hexagram 10 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-10-03.translation: A quiet and solitary man, to whom, being steadfast and right, this brings good fortune: holding the due mean, the person will not allow themself to be thrown into disorder.

XIANG-U-10-04.label: Hexagram 10 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-10-04.original: 眇能視，不足以有明也。跛能履，不足以與行也。咥人之凶，位不當也。武人為于大君，志剛也。
XIANG-U-10-04.translation: A one-eyed man who thinks that the person can see: the person is not fit to see clearly. A lame man who thinks that the person can tread well: one cannot walk along with them. The ill fortune of being bitten arises from the place not being the proper one for them. A mere bravo acting the part of a great ruler: this is because of their aims being too violent.

XIANG-U-10-05.label: Hexagram 10 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-10-05.translation: The person becomes full of cautious caution, and in the end this brings good fortune: their aim takes effect.

XIANG-U-10-06.label: Hexagram 10 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-10-06.translation: The person treads resolutely; and though the person be steadfast and right, there is danger: this is due to their being in the position that is correct and appropriate to them.

XIANG-U-10-07.label: Hexagram 10 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-10-07.translation: This will bring great good fortune, and that in the occupancy of the topmost line: this is great matter for congratulation.

XIANG-U-11-01.label: Hexagram 11 Great Image
XIANG-U-11-01.original: 天地交，泰；后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。
XIANG-U-11-01.translation: The trigrams for heaven and earth in communication together form Tai. The sage sovereign, in harmony with this, fashions and completes their regulations after the courses of heaven and earth, and assists the application of the adaptations furnished by them,; in order to benefit the people.

XIANG-U-11-02.label: Hexagram 11 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-11-02.translation: The good fortune of advance, as suggested by the emblem of the grass pulled up, arises from the will of the party intended being set on what is external to themself.

XIANG-U-11-03.label: Hexagram 11 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-11-03.original: 包荒，得尚于中行，以光大也。
XIANG-U-11-03.translation: The person bears with the uncultivated, and proves themself acting in accordance with the due mean: for their intelligence is bright and their capacity is great.

XIANG-U-11-04.label: Hexagram 11 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-11-04.translation: There is no going away so that there will not be a return refers to this as the point where the interaction of heaven and earth takes place.

XIANG-U-11-05.label: Hexagram 11 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-11-05.original: 翩翩不富，皆失實也。不戒以孚，中心願也。
XIANG-U-11-05.translation: The person comes fluttering down, not relying on their own rich resources: both the person and their neighbours are out of their real place where they are. They have not received warning, but come in the sincerity of their hearts: this is what they have desired in the core of their hearts.

XIANG-U-11-06.label: Hexagram 11 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-11-06.translation: By such a course there is happiness, and this will bring great good fortune: the person represented by the line employs the virtue proper to their central position to carry their wishes into effect.

XIANG-U-11-07.label: Hexagram 11 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-11-07.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the city wall returned back into the moat shows how the governmental orders have long been in disorder.

XIANG-U-12-01.label: Hexagram 12 Great Image
XIANG-U-12-01.original: 天地不交，否；君子以儉德辟難，不可榮以祿。
XIANG-U-12-01.translation: The trigrams of heaven and earth, not in intercommunication, form Bi. The noble person, following this image, restrains the manifestation of) their virtue, and avoids the calamities that threaten them. There is no opportunity of conferring on them the glory of official reward.

XIANG-U-12-02.label: Hexagram 12 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-12-02.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the good fortune through firm goodness, suggested by the pulling up of the grass, arises from the will of the parties intended being bent on serving the ruler.

XIANG-U-12-03.label: Hexagram 12 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-12-03.translation: The person of mature character, comporting themself as the distress and obstruction require, will have success: the person does not allow themself to be disordered by the herd of lesser people.

XIANG-U-12-04.label: Hexagram 12 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-12-04.translation: That their shame is folded in their breast is because of the inappropriateness of their position.

XIANG-U-12-05.label: Hexagram 12 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-12-05.translation: The person acts in accordance with the ordination of Heaven, and commits no error: the purpose of their mind can be carried into effect.

XIANG-U-12-06.label: Hexagram 12 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-12-06.translation: The good fortune of the great person arises from the correctness of their position.

XIANG-U-12-07.label: Hexagram 12 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-12-07.translation: This line or image shows that the distress and obstruction having reached its end, it is overthrown and removed: how could it be prolonged?

XIANG-U-13-01.label: Hexagram 13 Great Image
XIANG-U-13-01.original: 天與火，同人；君子以類族辨物。
XIANG-U-13-01.translation: The trigrams for heaven and fire form Tong Ren. The noble person, following this image, distinguishes things according to their kinds and classes.

XIANG-U-13-02.label: Hexagram 13 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-13-02.translation: The representative of the union of men is just issuing from their gate: who will blame them?

XIANG-U-13-03.label: Hexagram 13 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-13-03.translation: The representative of the union of men appears in relation with their kindred: that is the path to regret.

XIANG-U-13-04.label: Hexagram 13 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-13-04.original: 伏戎于莽，敵剛也。三歲不興，安行也。
XIANG-U-13-04.translation: The person hides their arms in the thick grass: because of the strength of their opponent. For three years the person makes no demonstration: how can the person do anything?

XIANG-U-13-05.label: Hexagram 13 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-13-05.original: 乘其墉，義弗克也，其吉，則困而反則也。
XIANG-U-13-05.translation: The person climbs onto the city wall but cannot rightly continue the attack. Their good fortune comes from recognizing the difficulty and returning to proper conduct.

XIANG-U-13-06.label: Hexagram 13 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-13-06.original: 同人之先，以中直也。大師相遇，言相克也。
XIANG-U-13-06.translation: The first action of the representative of the union of men here described arises from their central position and straightforward character. The meeting secured by their great host indicates that the opponents of it have been overcome.

XIANG-U-13-07.label: Hexagram 13 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-13-07.translation: The representative of the union of men appears in the suburbs: their object has not yet been attained.

XIANG-U-14-01.label: Hexagram 14 Great Image
XIANG-U-14-01.original: 火在天上，大有；君子以遏惡揚善，順天休命。
XIANG-U-14-01.translation: The trigram for heaven and that of fire above it form Ta Yd. The noble person, following this image, represses what is misfortune and gives distinction to what is good, in sympathy with the excellent Heaven-conferred nature.

XIANG-U-14-02.label: Hexagram 14 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-14-02.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: this first line, undivided, of Da You shows no approach to what is injurious.

XIANG-U-14-03.label: Hexagram 14 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-14-03.translation: A large wagon with its load refers to the virtue accumulated in the person represented by the line, so that the person will suffer no loss in the conduct of affairs.

XIANG-U-14-04.label: Hexagram 14 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-14-04.original: 公用亨于天子，小人害也。
XIANG-U-14-04.translation: A feudal prince presents their offerings to the son of Heaven: a petty person in such a position does themself harm.

XIANG-U-14-05.label: Hexagram 14 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-14-05.translation: H e keeps their great resources under restraint: their wisdom discriminates clearly what the person ought to do.

XIANG-U-14-06.label: Hexagram 14 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-14-06.original: 厥孚交如，信以發志也。威如之吉，易而无備也。
XIANG-U-14-06.translation: Their sincerity is reciprocated by all the others: their sincerity serves to stir and call out what is in their minds. The good fortune springing from a display of proper majesty shows how they might otherwise feel too easy, and make no preparation to serve them.

XIANG-U-14-07.label: Hexagram 14 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-14-07.translation: This line or image shows that the good fortune attached to the topmost line of Da You arises from the help of Heaven.

XIANG-U-15-01.label: Hexagram 15 Great Image
XIANG-U-15-01.original: 地中有山，謙；君子以裒多益寡，稱物平施。
XIANG-U-15-01.translation: The trigram for the earth and that of a mountain in the midst of it form Qian. The noble person, following this image, diminishes what is excessive in themself, and increases where there is any defect, bringing about an equality, accordine to the nature of the case, in their treatment of themself and others.

XIANG-U-15-02.label: Hexagram 15 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-15-02.translation: The noble person who adds humility to humility is one who nourishes their virtue in lowliness.

XIANG-U-15-03.label: Hexagram 15 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-15-03.translation: The good fortune consequent on being steadfast and right, where the humility has made itself recognised, is because of the possessors having the virtue in the core of their heart.

XIANG-U-15-04.label: Hexagram 15 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-15-04.translation: The noble person of acknowledged merit, and yet humble: the myriads of the people will submit to them.

XIANG-U-15-05.label: Hexagram 15 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-15-05.translation: One, whose action would be in every way beneficial, stirs up their humility the more: but in doing so the person does not act contrary to the proper rule.

XIANG-U-15-06.label: Hexagram 15 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-15-06.translation: The person may beneficially use the force of arms: correcting, that is, those who do not submit.

XIANG-U-15-07.label: Hexagram 15 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-15-07.original: 鳴謙，志未得也。可用行師，征邑國也。
XIANG-U-15-07.translation: Their humility has made itself recognised: but all their aims have not yet been attained. The person may employ the force of arms, but only in correcting their own towns and state.

XIANG-U-16-01.label: Hexagram 16 Great Image
XIANG-U-16-01.original: 雷出地奮，豫。先王以作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。
XIANG-U-16-01.translation: The trigrams for the earth and thunder issuing from it with its crashing noise form Yu. The ancient kings, following this image, composed their music and did honour to virtue, presenting it especially and most clearly to God, when they associated with Them at the service their highest ancestor and their father.

XIANG-U-16-02.label: Hexagram 16 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-16-02.translation: The subject of the first line proclaims their pleasure and satisfaction: this brings misfortune; their wishes have been satisfied to overflowing.

XIANG-U-16-03.label: Hexagram 16 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-16-03.translation: The person sees a thing without waiting till it has come to pass; with their steadfastness this brings good fortune: this is shown by the central and correct position of the line.

XIANG-U-16-04.label: Hexagram 16 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-16-04.translation: The person looks up for favours, while the person indulges the feeling of satisfaction; this will bring cause for regret: this is shown by the position not being the appropriate one.

XIANG-U-16-05.label: Hexagram 16 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-16-05.translation: From them the harmony and satisfaction come; great is the success which the person obtains: their aims take effect on a grand scale.

XIANG-U-16-06.label: Hexagram 16 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-16-06.original: 六五貞疾，乘剛也。恆不死，中未亡也。
XIANG-U-16-06.translation: The subject of the fifth line has a chronic complaint: this is shown by their being mounted on the strong line. The person still lives on without dying: the person is in the central position, and its memories of the past have not yet perished.

XIANG-U-16-07.label: Hexagram 16 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-16-07.translation: This line or image shows that with darkened mind devoted to the harmony and satisfaction of the time, as shown in the topmost line: how can one in such a condition continue long?

XIANG-U-17-01.label: Hexagram 17 Great Image
XIANG-U-17-01.original: 澤中有雷，隨；君子以嚮晦入宴息。
XIANG-U-17-01.translation: The trig-ram for the waters of a marsh and that for thunder hidden in the midst of it form Sui. The noble person following this image, when it is getting towards dark, enters their house and rests.

XIANG-U-17-02.label: Hexagram 17 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-17-02.original: 官有渝，從正吉也。出門交有功，不失也。
XIANG-U-17-02.translation: The person is changing the object of their pursuit: but if the person follow what is correct, this brings good fortune. The person goes beyond their own gate to find associates: the person will not fail in the method the person pursues.

XIANG-U-17-03.label: Hexagram 17 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-17-03.translation: The person cleaves to the little boy: the person cannot be with the two at the same time.

XIANG-U-17-04.label: Hexagram 17 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-17-04.translation: The person cleaves to the man of age and experience: by the decision of their will, the person abandons the youth below.

XIANG-U-17-05.label: Hexagram 17 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-17-05.original: 隨有獲，其義凶也。有孚在道，明功也。
XIANG-U-17-05.translation: The person is followed and obtains adherents: according to the idea of the hexagram, this is misfortune. The person is sincere in their course: showing their intelligence, and leading to achievement.

XIANG-U-17-06.label: Hexagram 17 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-17-06.translation: The person is sincere in fostering what is excellent: their position is correct and in the centre.

XIANG-U-17-07.label: Hexagram 17 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-17-07.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the sincerity is firmly held and clung to, as shown in the topmost line: the idea of the hexagram has reached its extreme development.

XIANG-U-18-01.label: Hexagram 18 Great Image
XIANG-U-18-01.original: 山下有風，蠱；君子以振民育德。
XIANG-U-18-01.translation: The trigram for a mountain, and below it that for wind, form Ku. The noble person, following this image, addresses themself to help the people and nourish their own virtue.

XIANG-U-18-02.label: Hexagram 18 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-18-02.translation: The person deals with the troubles caused by their father: the person feels that the person has entered into the work of their father.

XIANG-U-18-03.label: Hexagram 18 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-18-03.translation: The person deals with the troubles caused by their mother: the person holds to the course of the due mean.

XIANG-U-18-04.label: Hexagram 18 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-18-04.translation: The person deals with the troubles caused by their father: in the end there is no blame.

XIANG-U-18-05.label: Hexagram 18 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-18-05.translation: The person views indulgently the troubles caused by their father: if the person go forward, the person will not succeed.

XIANG-U-18-06.label: Hexagram 18 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-18-06.translation: The person deals with the troubles caused by their father, and obtains praise: the person is responded to by the person represented by line two with all their virtue.

XIANG-U-18-07.label: Hexagram 18 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-18-07.translation: The person does not serve either king or feudal lord: but their aim may be a model to others.

XIANG-U-19-01.label: Hexagram 19 Great Image
XIANG-U-19-01.original: 澤上有地，臨；君子以教思无窮，容保民无疆。
XIANG-U-19-01.translation: The trigram for the waters of a marsh and that for the earth above it form Lin. The noble person, following this image, has their purposes of instruction that are inexhaustible, and nourishes and supports the people without limit.

XIANG-U-19-02.label: Hexagram 19 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-19-02.translation: The good fortune through the steadfastness of the person represented by the first line advancing in company with the person represented by the second is due to their will being set on doing what is right.

XIANG-U-19-03.label: Hexagram 19 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-19-03.original: 咸臨，吉无不利；未順命也。
XIANG-U-19-03.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the good fortune and every possible advantage attending the advance of the person represented by the second line, in company with the person represented by the first, arises from the fact that those to whom the advance is made are not yet obedient to the ordinances of Heaven.

XIANG-U-19-04.label: Hexagram 19 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-19-04.original: 甘臨，位不當也。既憂之，咎不長也。
XIANG-U-19-04.translation: The person shows themself well pleased to advance: their position is not that appropriate to them. If the person become anxious, however, about their action, their error will not be continued.

XIANG-U-19-05.label: Hexagram 19 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-19-05.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the freedom from error consequent on the advance in the highest mode is due to the various appropriateness of the position.

XIANG-U-19-06.label: Hexagram 19 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-19-06.translation: This line or image shows that what befits the great ruler means the pursuing the course of the due mean.

XIANG-U-19-07.label: Hexagram 19 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-19-07.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the good fortune consequent on the advance of honesty and generosity is due to the will of the person represented by the line being set on the subjects of the first two lines of the inner trigram.

XIANG-U-20-01.label: Hexagram 20 Great Image
XIANG-U-20-01.original: 風行地上，觀；先王以省方，觀民設教。
XIANG-U-20-01.translation: The trigram representing the earth, and that for wind moving above it, form Kwan. The ancient kings, following this image, examined the different regions of the kingdom, to see the ways of the people, and set forth their instructions.

XIANG-U-20-02.label: Hexagram 20 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-20-02.translation: The looking of a lad shown by the first yielding line, indicates the way of the inferior people.

XIANG-U-20-03.label: Hexagram 20 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-20-03.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the steadfastness of a woman, in peeping out from a door is also a thing to be ashamed of in a noble person.

XIANG-U-20-04.label: Hexagram 20 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-20-04.translation: The person looks at the course of their own life, to advance or recede accordingly: the person will not err in the path to be pursued.

XIANG-U-20-05.label: Hexagram 20 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-20-05.translation: The person contemplates the glory of the kingdom: ttherefore arises the wish to be a guest at court.

XIANG-U-20-06.label: Hexagram 20 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-20-06.translation: The person contemplates their own life-course: the person should for this purpose contemplate the condition of the people.

XIANG-U-20-07.label: Hexagram 20 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-20-07.translation: The person contemplates their own character: the person cannot even yet let their mind be at rest.

XIANG-U-21-01.label: Hexagram 21 Great Image
XIANG-U-21-01.original: 雷電噬嗑；先王以明罰敕法。
XIANG-U-21-01.translation: The trigrams representing thunder and lightning form Shih Ho. The ancient kings, following this image, framed their penalties with intelligence, and promulgated their laws.

XIANG-U-21-02.label: Hexagram 21 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-21-02.translation: Their feet are in the stocks, and the person is deprived of their toes: there is no walking to do misfortune.

XIANG-U-21-03.label: Hexagram 21 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-21-03.translation: This line or image shows that biting through soft flesh until the nose is covered shows that the yielding line is riding above a firm line.

XIANG-U-21-04.label: Hexagram 21 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-21-04.translation: The person meets with what is disagreeable and hurtful: their position is not the proper one for them.

XIANG-U-21-05.label: Hexagram 21 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-21-05.translation: It is favorable to them to realise the difficulty of their task and be firm, in which case this brings good fortune: their light has not yet been sufficiently displayed.

XIANG-U-21-06.label: Hexagram 21 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-21-06.translation: Let them be steadfast and right, realising the danger of their position, and there is no blame: the person will possess every quality appropriate to their position and task.

XIANG-U-21-07.label: Hexagram 21 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-21-07.translation: The person wears the cangue and is deprived of their ears: the person hears, but will not understand.

XIANG-U-22-01.label: Hexagram 22 Great Image
XIANG-U-22-01.original: 山下有火，賁；君子以明庶政，无敢折獄。
XIANG-U-22-01.translation: The trigram representing a mountain and that for fire under it form Bi. The noble person, following this image, throws a brilliancy around their various processes of government, but does not dare in a similar way to decide cases of criminal litigation.
