XIANG-U-22-02.label: Hexagram 22 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-22-02.translation: This line or image shows that there is no walking: that is, the person represented by the line will not dare to offend any more.

XIANG-U-22-03.label: Hexagram 22 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-22-03.translation: Their beard is adorned because it rises together with the person above it.

XIANG-U-22-04.label: Hexagram 22 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-22-04.translation: The good fortune consequent on their ever maintaining steadfastness is due to this,; that to the end no one will insult them.

XIANG-U-22-05.label: Hexagram 22 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-22-05.original: 六四，當位疑也。匪寇婚媾，終无尤也。
XIANG-U-22-05.translation: The place occupied by the fourth yielding line, affords ground for doubt as to its subject; but as the person represented by the third pursues not as a robber, but as intent on a matrimonial alliance, the person will in the end have no grudge against them.

XIANG-U-22-06.label: Hexagram 22 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-22-06.translation: The good fortune falling to the fifth yielding line, affords occasion for joy.

XIANG-U-22-07.label: Hexagram 22 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-22-07.translation: The freedom from error attached to the person represented by the topmost line, with no ornament but the simple white, shows how the person has attained their aim.

XIANG-U-23-01.label: Hexagram 23 Great Image
XIANG-U-23-01.original: 山附地上，剝；上以厚下，安宅。
XIANG-U-23-01.translation: The trigrams representing the earth, and above it that for a mountain, which adheres to the earth, form Po. Superiors, following this image, seek to strengthen those below them, to secure the peace and stability of their own position.

XIANG-U-23-02.label: Hexagram 23 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-23-02.translation: The person overthrows the couch by injuring its legs: therefore the person commences their work of ruin with what is lowest in the noble person.

XIANG-U-23-03.label: Hexagram 23 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-23-03.translation: The person destroys the couch by injuring its frame: the noble person has as yet no associates.

XIANG-U-23-04.label: Hexagram 23 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-23-04.translation: That there is no blame on the part of this one among the overthrowers arises from the difference between them and the others above and below.

XIANG-U-23-05.label: Hexagram 23 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-23-05.translation: The person has overthrown the couch, and proceeds to injure the skin of them who lies on it: serious trouble is very near at hand.

XIANG-U-23-06.label: Hexagram 23 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-23-06.translation: The person obtains for them the favour that lights on the inmates of the palace: in the end this will bring no grudge against them.

XIANG-U-23-07.label: Hexagram 23 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-23-07.original: 君子得輿，民所載也。小人剝廬，終不可用也。
XIANG-U-23-07.translation: The noble person finds themself in a carriage: the person is carried along by the people. The lesser people by their course overthrow their own dwellings: they can never again be of use to them.

XIANG-U-24-01.label: Hexagram 24 Great Image
XIANG-U-24-01.original: 雷在地中，復；先王以至日閉關，商旅不行，后不省方。
XIANG-U-24-01.translation: The trigram representing the earth and that for thunder in the midst of it form Fu. The ancient kings, following this image, on the day of the winter solstice, shut the gates of the passes from one state to another, so that the travelling merchants could not then pursue their journeys, nor the princes go on with the inspection of their states.

XIANG-U-24-02.label: Hexagram 24 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-24-02.translation: This line or image shows that returning from an error of no great extent is the prelude to the cultivation of the person.

XIANG-U-24-03.label: Hexagram 24 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-24-03.translation: The good fortune attendant on the admirable return of the person represented by the second line is due to their condescension to the virtuous subject of the line below.

XIANG-U-24-04.label: Hexagram 24 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-24-04.translation: Notwithstanding the dangerous position of them who has made many returns, there is no blame through their aiming after righteousness.

XIANG-U-24-05.label: Hexagram 24 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-24-05.translation: The person moves right in the centre among those represented by the other divided lines, and yet returns alone: their object is to pursue the proper path.

XIANG-U-24-06.label: Hexagram 24 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-24-06.translation: The noble return, giving no ground for repentance, is due to the person represented by the line striving to perfect themself in accordance with their central position.

XIANG-U-24-07.label: Hexagram 24 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-24-07.translation: The misfortune consequent on being all astray on the person represented by returning is because the course pursued is contrary to the proper course for a ruler.

XIANG-U-25-01.label: Hexagram 25 Great Image
XIANG-U-25-01.original: 天下雷行，物與无妄；先王以茂對時，育萬物。
XIANG-U-25-01.translation: The thunder rolls all in the world, and to everything there is given its nature, free from all insincerity. The ancient kings, following this image, made their regulations in complete accordance with the seasons, thereby nourishing all things.

XIANG-U-25-02.label: Hexagram 25 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-25-02.translation: When the person who is free from insincerity makes any movement, the person will get what the person desires.

XIANG-U-25-03.label: Hexagram 25 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-25-03.translation: The person reaps without having ploughed: the thought of riches to be got had not risen in their mind.

XIANG-U-25-04.label: Hexagram 25 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-25-04.translation: The passer-by gets the ox: this proves a serious trouble to the people of the neighbourhood.

XIANG-U-25-05.label: Hexagram 25 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-25-05.translation: If the person can remain steadfast and right there is no blame: the person firmly holds fast their correctness.

XIANG-U-25-06.label: Hexagram 25 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-25-06.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: medicine in the case of one who is free from insincerity!; it should not be tried at all.

XIANG-U-25-07.label: Hexagram 25 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-25-07.translation: The action in this case of one who is free from insincerity will occasion the serious trouble arisinofrom action when the time for it is exhausted.

XIANG-U-26-01.label: Hexagram 26 Great Image
XIANG-U-26-01.original: 天在山中，大畜；君子以多識前言往行，以畜其德。
XIANG-U-26-01.translation: The trigram representing a mountain, and in the midst of it that representing heaven, form Ta Khu.. The noble person, following this image, stores largely in their memory the words and deeds of former men, to subserve the accumulation of their virtue.

XIANG-U-26-02.label: Hexagram 26 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-26-02.translation: The person is in a position of danger; it will be beneficial for them to stop their advance: the person should not rashly expose themself to serious trouble.

XIANG-U-26-03.label: Hexagram 26 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-26-03.translation: The person is as a carriage from which the strap under it has been removed: being in the central position, the person will incur no blame.

XIANG-U-26-04.label: Hexagram 26 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-26-04.translation: This will bring advantage in whatever direction the person may advance: the person represented by the topmost line is of the same mind with them.

XIANG-U-26-05.label: Hexagram 26 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-26-05.translation: The great good fortune shown by the fourth yielding line, shows that there is occasion for joy.

XIANG-U-26-06.label: Hexagram 26 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-26-06.translation: The good fortune shown by the fifth yielding line, shows that there is occasion for congratulation.

XIANG-U-26-07.label: Hexagram 26 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-26-07.translation: In command of the firmament of heaven: the way is clearly open for movement.

XIANG-U-27-01.label: Hexagram 27 Great Image
XIANG-U-27-01.original: 山下有雷，頤；君子以慎言語，節飲食。
XIANG-U-27-01.translation: The trigram representing a mountain and under it that for thunder form I. The noble person, following this image, enjoins watchfulness over our words, and the temperate regulation of our eating and drinking.

XIANG-U-27-02.label: Hexagram 27 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-27-02.translation: You look at me till your lower jaw hangs down: the person represented by the line is therefore shown unfit to be thought noble.

XIANG-U-27-03.label: Hexagram 27 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-27-03.translation: The misfortune of advance by the person represented by the second yielding line, is because of their leaving in their movements their proper associates.

XIANG-U-27-04.label: Hexagram 27 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-27-04.translation: For ten years let them not take any action: their course is greatly opposed to what is right.

XIANG-U-27-05.label: Hexagram 27 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-27-05.translation: This line or image shows that the good fortune attached to looking downwards for the power to nourish, shows how brilliant will be the diffusion of that power from the person represented by the lines superior position.

XIANG-U-27-06.label: Hexagram 27 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-27-06.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the good fortune from abiding in firmness is due to the docility of the person represented by the line in following the person represented by the line above.

XIANG-U-27-07.label: Hexagram 27 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-27-07.translation: The good fortune, notwithstanding the danger of their position, of them from whom comes the nourishing, affords great cause for congratulation.

XIANG-U-28-01.label: Hexagram 28 Great Image
XIANG-U-28-01.original: 澤滅木，大過。君子以獨立不懼，遯世无悶。
XIANG-U-28-01.translation: The trigram representing trees hidden beneath that for the waters of a marsh forms T a. Kwo. The noble person, following this image, stands up alone and has no fear, and keeps retired from the world without regret.

XIANG-U-28-02.label: Hexagram 28 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-28-02.translation: The person places mats of the white ma.3 grass under things set on the ground: the person feels their weakness and their being in the lowest place, and uses extraordinary care.

XIANG-U-28-03.label: Hexagram 28 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-28-03.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: an old husband and a young wife: such association is extraordinary.

XIANG-U-28-04.label: Hexagram 28 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-28-04.original: 棟橈之凶，不可以有輔也。
XIANG-U-28-04.translation: c The misfortune connected with the beam that is weak arises from this, that no help can be given to the condition therefore represented.

XIANG-U-28-05.label: Hexagram 28 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-28-05.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the good fortune connected with the beam curving upwards arises from this, that it does not bend towards what is below.

XIANG-U-28-06.label: Hexagram 28 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-28-06.original: 枯楊生華，何可久也。老婦士夫，亦可丑也。
XIANG-U-28-06.translation: This line or image shows that a decayed willow produces flowers: but how can this secure its long continuance? An old wife and a young husband: this also is a thing to be ashamed of.

XIANG-U-28-07.label: Hexagram 28 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-28-07.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: evil follows wading with extraordinary boldness through the stream: but the act affords no ground for blame.

XIANG-U-29-01.label: Hexagram 29 Great Image
XIANG-U-29-01.original: 水洊至，習坎；君子以常德行，習教事。
XIANG-U-29-01.translation: The representation of water flowing on continuously forms the repeated Kan. The noble person, following this image, maintains constantly the virtue of their heart and the integrity of their conduct, and practises the business of instruction.

XIANG-U-29-02.label: Hexagram 29 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-29-02.translation: Tn the double defile, the person enters a cavern within it: the person has missed their proper way, and this brings misfortune.

XIANG-U-29-03.label: Hexagram 29 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-29-03.translation: The person will get a little of the deliverance that the person seeks: the person will not yet escape from their environed position.

XIANG-U-29-04.label: Hexagram 29 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-29-04.translation: Whether the person comes or goes, the person is confronted by a defile: the person will never in such circumstances achieve any success.

XIANG-U-29-05.label: Hexagram 29 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-29-05.translation: This line or image shows that nothing but a bottle of spirits and a subsidiary basket of rice: these describe the meeting at this point of those who are represented by the strong and weak lines.

XIANG-U-29-06.label: Hexagram 29 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-29-06.translation: The water in the defile is not full so as to flow away: the virtue shown by the central situation is not yet sufficiently great.

XIANG-U-29-07.label: Hexagram 29 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-29-07.translation: The sixth line, divided, shows its subject missing their proper course: this brings misfortune for three years.

XIANG-U-30-01.label: Hexagram 30 Great Image
XIANG-U-30-01.original: 明兩作離，大人以繼明照于四方。
XIANG-U-30-01.translation: The trigram for brightness, repeated, forms Li. The person of mature character, following this image, cultivates more and more their brilliant virtue, and diffuses its brightness over the four quarters of the land.

XIANG-U-30-02.label: Hexagram 30 Line Image 1
XIANG-U-30-02.translation: The reverent attention directed to their confused steps is the way by which error is avoided.

XIANG-U-30-03.label: Hexagram 30 Line Image 2
XIANG-U-30-03.translation: The great good fortune from the person represented by the second line occupying their place in yellow is because of their holding the course of the due mean.

XIANG-U-30-04.label: Hexagram 30 Line Image 3
XIANG-U-30-04.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: a position like that of the declining sun: how can it continue long?

XIANG-U-30-05.label: Hexagram 30 Line Image 4
XIANG-U-30-05.translation: How abrupt is the manner of their coming!; none can bear with them.

XIANG-U-30-06.label: Hexagram 30 Line Image 5
XIANG-U-30-06.translation: The good fortune attached to the fifth yielding line, is due to its occupying the place of a king or a prince.

XIANG-U-30-07.label: Hexagram 30 Line Image 6
XIANG-U-30-07.translation: The king employs them in their punitive expeditions: the object is to bring the regions to a correct state.

XIANG-L-31-01.label: Hexagram 31 Great Image
XIANG-L-31-01.original: 山上有澤，咸；君子以虛受人。
XIANG-L-31-01.translation: The trigram representing a mountain and above it that for the waters of a marsh form Xian. The noble person, following this image, keeps their mind free from pre-occupation, and open to receive the influences of others.

XIANG-L-31-02.label: Hexagram 31 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-31-02.translation: The person moves their great toe: their mind is set on what is beyond themself.

XIANG-L-31-03.label: Hexagram 31 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-31-03.translation: Though there would be misfortune; yet, if the person abide quiet in their place, this brings good fortune: through compliance with the circumstances of their condition and place this will bring no injury.

XIANG-L-31-04.label: Hexagram 31 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-31-04.original: 咸其股，亦不處也。志在隨人，所執下也。
XIANG-L-31-04.translation: The person moves their thighs: the person still does not want to rest in their place. Their will is set on following others: what the person holds in their grasp is low.

XIANG-L-31-05.label: Hexagram 31 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-31-05.original: 貞吉悔亡，未感害也。憧憧往來，未光大也。
XIANG-L-31-05.translation: Firm correctness will lead to good fortune, and prevent all cause for regret: there has not yet been any harm from a selfish wish to influence. The person is unsettled in their movements: their power to influence is not yet either brilliant or great.

XIANG-L-31-06.label: Hexagram 31 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-31-06.translation: The person tries to move the flesh along the spine above the heart: their aim is trivial.

XIANG-L-31-07.label: Hexagram 31 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-31-07.translation: The person moves their jaws and tongue: the person only talks with loquacious mouth.

XIANG-L-32-01.label: Hexagram 32 Great Image
XIANG-L-32-01.original: 雷風，恆；君子以立不易方。
XIANG-L-32-01.translation: The trigram representing thunder and that for wind form Hang. The noble person, following this image, stands firm, and does not change their method of operation.

XIANG-L-32-02.label: Hexagram 32 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-32-02.translation: The misfortune attached to the deep desire for long continuance in the person represented by the first line arises from the deep seeking for it at the commencement of things.

XIANG-L-32-03.label: Hexagram 32 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-32-03.translation: All cause for regret? on the part of the person represented by the second firm line, disappears: the person can abide long in the due mean.

XIANG-L-32-04.label: Hexagram 32 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-32-04.translation: The person does not continuously maintain their virtue: nowhere will the person be borne with.

XIANG-L-32-05.label: Hexagram 32 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-32-05.translation: Going for long to what is not their proper place, how can the person get game?

XIANG-L-32-06.label: Hexagram 32 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-32-06.original: 婦人貞吉，從一而終也。夫子制義，從婦凶也。
XIANG-L-32-06.translation: Such steadfastness in a wife will be fortunate: it is hers to the end of life to follow with an unchanged mind. The husband must decide what is right, and lay down the rule accordingly: for them to follow like a wife is misfortune.

XIANG-L-32-07.label: Hexagram 32 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-32-07.translation: The subject of the topmost line is exciting themself to long continuance: far will the person be from achieving merit.

XIANG-L-33-01.label: Hexagram 33 Great Image
XIANG-L-33-01.original: 天下有山，遯；君子以遠小人，不惡而嚴。
XIANG-L-33-01.translation: The trigram representing the sky and below it that for a mountain form Dun. The noble person, following this image, keeps lesser people at a distance, not by showing that the person hates them, but by their own dignified gravity.

XIANG-L-33-02.label: Hexagram 33 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-33-02.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: there is the danger of the position shown by the retiring tail: but if no movement be made, what disaster can there be?

XIANG-L-33-03.label: Hexagram 33 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-33-03.translation: The person holds it*as by a thong from the hide of a yellow ox: their purpose is firm.

XIANG-L-33-04.label: Hexagram 33 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-33-04.original: 系遯之厲，有疾憊也。畜臣妾吉，不可大事也。
XIANG-L-33-04.translation: The danger connected with the case of one retiring, though bound, is due to the consequent distress and exhaustion. If the person were to deal as in nourishing a servant or concubine, it would be fortunate for them: but a great affair cannot be dealt with in this way.

XIANG-L-33-05.label: Hexagram 33 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-33-05.translation: A noble person retires notwithstanding their likings; a petty person cannot attain to this.

XIANG-L-33-06.label: Hexagram 33 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-33-06.translation: The person retires in an admirable way, and with steadfastness this brings good fortune: this is due to the rectitude of their purpose.

XIANG-L-33-07.label: Hexagram 33 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-33-07.translation: The person retires in a noble way, and their doing so will be beneficial in every respect: the person who does so has no doubts about their course.

XIANG-L-34-01.label: Hexagram 34 Great Image
XIANG-L-34-01.original: 雷在天上，大壯；君子以非禮弗履。
XIANG-L-34-01.translation: The trigram representing heaven and above it that for thunder form Ta Tsfwang. The noble person, following this image, does not take a step which is not according to propriety.

XIANG-L-34-02.label: Hexagram 34 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-34-02.translation: The person manifests their vigour in their toes: this will certainly lead to exhaustion.

XIANG-L-34-03.label: Hexagram 34 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-34-03.translation: The second line, undivided, shows that with steadfastness this brings good fortune: this is due to its being in the centre, and its subject exemplifying the due mean.

XIANG-L-34-04.label: Hexagram 34 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-34-04.translation: The petty person uses all their strength; in the case of the noble person it is their rule not to do so.

XIANG-L-34-05.label: Hexagram 34 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-34-05.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the fence is opened and the horns are not entangled: the person represented by the line still advances.

XIANG-L-34-06.label: Hexagram 34 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-34-06.translation: The person loses their ram and hardly perceives it: the person is not in their appropriate place.

XIANG-L-34-07.label: Hexagram 34 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-34-07.original: 不能退，不能遂，不詳也。艱則吉，咎不長也。
XIANG-L-34-07.translation: The person is unable either to retreat or to advance: this is because of their want of care. If the person realise the difficulty of their position, this brings good fortune: their error will not be prolonged.

XIANG-L-35-01.label: Hexagram 35 Great Image
XIANG-L-35-01.original: 明出地上，晉；君子以自昭明德。
XIANG-L-35-01.translation: The trigram representing the earth and that for the bright sun coming forth above it form Jin. The noble person, according to this, gives themself to make more brilliant their bright virtue.

XIANG-L-35-02.label: Hexagram 35 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-35-02.original: 晉如，摧如；獨行正也。裕无咎；未受命也。
XIANG-L-35-02.translation: The person appears wishing to advance, but at the same time being kept back: all-alone the person pursues the correct course. Let them maintain a larofe and generous mind, and there is no blame: the person has not yet received an official charge.

XIANG-L-35-03.label: Hexagram 35 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-35-03.translation: The person will receive this great blessing: for the person is in the central place and the correct position for them.

XIANG-L-35-04.label: Hexagram 35 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-35-04.translation: All around trust them: their common aim is to move upwards and act.

XIANG-L-35-05.label: Hexagram 35 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-35-05.translation: The person advances like a marmot. However steadfast and right the person may be, their position is one of danger: their place is not that appropriate for them.

XIANG-L-35-06.label: Hexagram 35 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-35-06.translation: Let them not concern themself whether the person fails or succeeds: their movement in advance will afford ground for congratulation.

XIANG-L-35-07.label: Hexagram 35 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-35-07.translation: The person uses their horns only to punish the rebellious people of their city: their course of procedure is not yet brilliant.

XIANG-L-36-01.label: Hexagram 36 Great Image
XIANG-L-36-01.original: 明入地中，明夷；君子以蒞眾，用晦而明。
XIANG-L-36-01.translation: The trigram representing the earth and that for the bright sun entering within it form Ming 1. The noble person, following this image, conducts their management of men; the person shows their intelligence by keeping it obscured.

XIANG-L-36-02.label: Hexagram 36 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-36-02.translation: The noble person is revolving their going away: in such a case the person feels it right not to eat.

XIANG-L-36-03.label: Hexagram 36 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-36-03.translation: The good fortune of the person represented by the second yielding line, is due to the proper fashion of their actinor according to their circumstances.

XIANG-L-36-04.label: Hexagram 36 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-36-04.translation: This line or image shows that with the aim represented by hunting in the south a great achievement is accomplished.

XIANG-L-36-05.label: Hexagram 36 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-36-05.translation: The person has just entered into the left side of the belly of the dark land: the person is still able to carry out the idea in their inner mind.

XIANG-L-36-06.label: Hexagram 36 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-36-06.translation: With the steadfastness of the count of Ji their brightness could not be quite extinguished.

XIANG-L-36-07.label: Hexagram 36 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-36-07.original: 初登于天，照四國也。后入于地，失則也。
XIANG-L-36-07.translation: The person had at first ascended to the top of the sky: the person might have enlightened the four quarters of the kingdom. Their future will be to go into the earth: the person has failed to fulfil the model of a ruler.

XIANG-L-37-01.label: Hexagram 37 Great Image
XIANG-L-37-01.original: 風自火出，家人；君子以言有物，而行有恆。
XIANG-L-37-01.translation: The trigram representing fire, and that for wind coming forth from it, form Afia. Zan. The noble person, following this image, orders their words according to the truth of things, and their conduct so that it is uniformly consistent.

XIANG-L-37-02.label: Hexagram 37 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-37-02.translation: The person establishes restrictive regulations in their household: the person does so, before any change has taken place in their wills.

XIANG-L-37-03.label: Hexagram 37 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-37-03.translation: The good fortune attached to the second yielding line, is due to the docility of its subject, operating with humility.

XIANG-L-37-04.label: Hexagram 37 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-37-04.original: 家人嗃嗃，未失也；婦子嘻嘻，失家節也。
XIANG-L-37-04.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: when the members of the household are treated with stern severity, there has been no great failure in the regulation of the family. When wife and children are smirking and chattering, the proper economy of the family has been lost.

XIANG-L-37-05.label: Hexagram 37 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-37-05.translation: This line or image shows that the family is enriched, and there is great good fortune: this is due to the docility belonging to the person represented by the line, and its being in its correct place.

XIANG-L-37-06.label: Hexagram 37 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-37-06.translation: The influence of the king extends to their family: the intercourse between them is that of mutual love.

XIANG-L-37-07.label: Hexagram 37 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-37-07.translation: This line or image shows that the good fortune connected with the display of majesty describes the result of the recovery of the true character.

XIANG-L-38-01.label: Hexagram 38 Great Image
XIANG-L-38-01.original: 上火下澤，睽；君子以同而異。
XIANG-L-38-01.translation: The trigram representing fire above, and that for the waters of a marsh below, form Kui. The noble person, following this image, where there is a general agreement, yet admits diversity.

XIANG-L-38-02.label: Hexagram 38 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-38-02.translation: The person meets with bad men and communicates with them: the person does so, to avoid the misfortune of their condemnation.

XIANG-L-38-03.label: Hexagram 38 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-38-03.translation: The person happens to meet with their lord in a byepassage: but the person has not deviated for this meeting from the proper course.

XIANG-L-38-04.label: Hexagram 38 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-38-04.original: 見輿曳，位不當也。无初有終，遇剛也。
XIANG-L-38-04.translation: their carriage dragged back: this is shown by the inappropriateness of the position of the line.

XIANG-L-38-05.label: Hexagram 38 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-38-05.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: they blend their sincere desires together, and there is no blame: their common aim is carried into effect.

XIANG-L-38-06.label: Hexagram 38 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-38-06.translation: With their hereditary minister the person unites closely and easily as if the person were biting through a piece of skin: their going forward will afford ground for congratulation.

XIANG-L-38-07.label: Hexagram 38 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-38-07.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the good fortune symbolised by meeting with genial rain springs from the passing away of all doubts.

XIANG-L-39-01.label: Hexagram 39 Great Image
XIANG-L-39-01.original: 山上有水，蹇；君子以反身修德。
XIANG-L-39-01.translation: The trigram representing a mountain, and above it that for water, form Jian. The noble person, following this image, turns round and examines themself, and cultivates their virtue.

XIANG-L-39-02.label: Hexagram 39 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-39-02.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: advancing will conduct to greater difficulties, while remaining stationary will afford ground for praise: the proper course is to wait.

XIANG-L-39-03.label: Hexagram 39 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-39-03.translation: The minister of the king struggles with difficulty on difficulty: in the end no blame will be attached to them.

XIANG-L-39-04.label: Hexagram 39 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-39-04.translation: The person advances, but only to greater difficulty; the person remains stationary, and returns to their former associates: they, represented in the inner trigram, rejoice in them.

XIANG-L-39-05.label: Hexagram 39 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-39-05.translation: To advance will only be to encounter greater difficulties; the person remains stationary, and unites with the person represented by the line above: that is in its proper place and has the solidity due to it in that position.

XIANG-L-39-06.label: Hexagram 39 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-39-06.translation: The person struggles with the greatest difficulties, while friends are coming to help them: the person is in the central position, and possesses the requisite virtue.

XIANG-L-39-07.label: Hexagram 39 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-39-07.original: 往蹇來碩，志在內也。利見大人，以從貴也。
XIANG-L-39-07.translation: To advance will only increase the difficulties, while their remaining stationary will be productive of great merit: their aim is to assist the person described by the line inside of them.

XIANG-L-40-01.label: Hexagram 40 Great Image
XIANG-L-40-01.original: 雷雨作，解；君子以赦過宥罪。
XIANG-L-40-01.translation: The trigram representing thunder and that for rain, with these phenomena in a state of manifestation, form Jie. The noble person, following this image, forgives errors, and deals gently with crimes.

XIANG-L-40-02.label: Hexagram 40 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-40-02.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the strong fourth line and the weak line here are in correlation: we judge rightly in saying that its subject will commit no error.

XIANG-L-40-03.label: Hexagram 40 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-40-03.translation: The good fortune springing from the steadfastness of the second firm line, is due to its subject holding the due mean.

XIANG-L-40-04.label: Hexagram 40 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-40-04.original: 負且乘，亦可丑也，自我致戎，又誰咎也。
XIANG-L-40-04.translation: For a porter with their burden to be riding in a carriage is a thing to be ashamed of. It is the person themself that tempts the robbers to come: on whom besides can we lay the blame?

XIANG-L-40-05.label: Hexagram 40 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-40-05.translation: This line or image shows that remove your toes: the places of this line and of the third and first are all inappropriate to them.

XIANG-L-40-06.label: Hexagram 40 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-40-06.translation: When the noble person executes their function of removing whatever is injurious to the idea of the hexagram, lesser people will of themselves retire.

XIANG-L-40-07.label: Hexagram 40 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-40-07.translation: A prince with their bow shoots a falcon: therefore the person removes the promoters of rebellion.

XIANG-L-41-01.label: Hexagram 41 Great Image
XIANG-L-41-01.original: 山下有澤，損；君子以懲忿窒欲。
XIANG-L-41-01.translation: The trigram representing a mountain and beneath it that for the waters of a marsh form Sun. The noble person, following this image, restrains their wrath and represses their desires.

XIANG-L-41-02.label: Hexagram 41 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-41-02.translation: The person suspends their own affairs and hurries away to help the person represented by the fourth line: the subject of that upper line mingles their wishes with their.

XIANG-L-41-03.label: Hexagram 41 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-41-03.translation: It will be beneficial for the person represented by the second firm line, to maintain their steadfastness: their central position gives its character to their aim.

XIANG-L-41-04.label: Hexagram 41 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-41-04.translation: One man, walking, finds their friend: when three are together, doubts rise among them.

XIANG-L-41-05.label: Hexagram 41 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-41-05.translation: The person diminishes the ailment under which the person labours: this is matter for joy.

XIANG-L-41-06.label: Hexagram 41 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-41-06.translation: The great good fortune attached to the fifth yielding line, is due to the blessing from above.

XIANG-L-41-07.label: Hexagram 41 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-41-07.translation: The person gives increase to others without taking from what is their own: the person obtains their wish on a grand scale.

XIANG-L-42-01.label: Hexagram 42 Great Image
XIANG-L-42-01.original: 風雷，益；君子以見善則遷，有過則改。
XIANG-L-42-01.translation: The trigram representing wind and that for thunder form Yi. The noble person, following this image, when the person sees what is good, moves towards it; and when the person sees their errors, the person turns from them.

XIANG-L-42-02.label: Hexagram 42 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-42-02.translation: If the movement be greatly fortunate, no blame will be imputed to them: though it is not for one in so low a position to have to do with great affairs.

XIANG-L-42-03.label: Hexagram 42 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-42-03.translation: Parties add to their stores: they come from beyond their immediate circle to do so.

XIANG-L-42-04.label: Hexagram 42 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-42-04.translation: Increase is given by means of what is misfortune and difficult: as the person has in themself the qualities called forth.

XIANG-L-42-05.label: Hexagram 42 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-42-05.translation: Their advice to their prince is followed: their only object in it being the increase of the general good.

XIANG-L-42-06.label: Hexagram 42 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-42-06.original: 有孚惠心，勿問之矣。惠我德，大得志也。
XIANG-L-42-06.translation: The ruler with sincere heart seeks to benefit all below: there need be no question about the result. All below with sincere heart acknowledge their goodness: the person gets what the person desires on a great scale.

XIANG-L-42-07.label: Hexagram 42 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-42-07.original: 莫益之，偏辭也。或擊之，自外來也。
XIANG-L-42-07.translation: To their increase none will contribute: this expresses but half the result. Many will seek to assail them: they will come from beyond their immediate circle to do so.

XIANG-L-43-01.label: Hexagram 43 Great Image
XIANG-L-43-01.original: 澤上于天，夬；君子以施祿及下，居德則忌。
XIANG-L-43-01.translation: The trigram representing heaven and that for the waters of a marsh mounting above it form Guai. The noble person, following this image, bestows official reward on those below them, and dislikes allowing their gifts to accumulate undispensed.

XIANG-L-43-02.label: Hexagram 43 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-43-02.translation: Without being able to succeed, the person goes forward: this is an error.

XIANG-L-43-03.label: Hexagram 43 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-43-03.translation: Though hostile measures be taken against them, the person need not be anxious: the person pursues the course of the due mean.

XIANG-L-43-04.label: Hexagram 43 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-43-04.translation: This line or image shows that the noble person looks bent on cutting off the culprit: there will in the end be no error.

XIANG-L-43-05.label: Hexagram 43 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-43-05.original: 其行次且，位不當也。聞言不信，聰不明也。
XIANG-L-43-05.translation: The person walks slowly and with difficulty: the person is not in the place appropriate to them.

XIANG-L-43-06.label: Hexagram 43 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-43-06.translation: If their action be in harmony with their central position, there is no blame: but their standing in the due mean is not yet clearly displayed.

XIANG-L-43-07.label: Hexagram 43 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-43-07.translation: There is the misery of having none on whom to call: the end will be that the person cannot continue any longer.

XIANG-L-44-01.label: Hexagram 44 Great Image
XIANG-L-44-01.original: 天下有風，姤；后以施命誥四方。
XIANG-L-44-01.translation: The trigram representing wind and that for the sky above it form Gou. The sovereign, following this image, delivers their charges, and promulgates their announcements throughout the four quarters of the kingdom.

XIANG-L-44-02.label: Hexagram 44 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-44-02.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: tied and fastened to a metal drag: this describes the arrest of the weak line in its advancing course.

XIANG-L-44-03.label: Hexagram 44 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-44-03.translation: The person has a wallet of fish: it is right for them not to allow the person represented by the first line to get to the guests.

XIANG-L-44-04.label: Hexagram 44 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-44-04.translation: The person walks with difficulty: but their steps have not yet been drawn into the course of the first line.

XIANG-L-44-05.label: Hexagram 44 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-44-05.translation: The misfortune shown by there being no fish in the wallet is because of the person represented by the line keeping themself aloof from the people.

XIANG-L-44-06.label: Hexagram 44 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-44-06.original: 九五含章，中正也。有隕自天，志不舍命也。
XIANG-L-44-06.translation: The subject of the fifth firm line, keeps their brilliant qualities concealed: as is shown by their central and correct position.

XIANG-L-44-07.label: Hexagram 44 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-44-07.translation: The person receives others on their horns: the person is exhausted at their greatest height, and this will bring cause for regret.

XIANG-L-45-01.label: Hexagram 45 Great Image
XIANG-L-45-01.original: 澤上于地，萃；君子以除戎器，戒不虞。
XIANG-L-45-01.translation: The trigram representing the earth and that for the waters of a marsh raised above it form Cui. The noble person, following this image, has their weapons of war put in good repair, to be prepared against unforeseen contingencies.

XIANG-L-45-02.label: Hexagram 45 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-45-02.translation: In consequence disorder is brought into the sphere of their union: their mind and aim are thrown into confusion.

XIANG-L-45-03.label: Hexagram 45 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-45-03.translation: The person is led forward; this brings good fortune, and freedom from error: the virtue proper to their central place has not undergone any change.

XIANG-L-45-04.label: Hexagram 45 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-45-04.translation: If the person go forward, the person will not err: in the person represented by the topmost line there is humility and condescension.

XIANG-L-45-05.label: Hexagram 45 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-45-05.translation: If the person be clearly fortunate, the person will receive no blame: this condition is necessary, because their position is not the one proper to them.

XIANG-L-45-06.label: Hexagram 45 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-45-06.translation: There is the union of all under them in the place of dignity: but their mind and aim have not yet been brilliantly displayed.

XIANG-L-45-07.label: Hexagram 45 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-45-07.translation: The person sighs and weeps: the person does not yet rest in their topmost position.

XIANG-L-46-01.label: Hexagram 46 Great Image
XIANG-L-46-01.original: 地中生木，升；君子以順德，積小以高大。
XIANG-L-46-01.translation: The trigram representing wood and that for the earth with the wood growing in the midst of it form Shang. The noble person, following this image, pays careful attention to their virtue, and accumulates the small developments of it till it is high and great.

XIANG-L-46-02.label: Hexagram 46 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-46-02.translation: The person is welcomed in their advance upwards, and this will bring great good fortune: the subjects of the upper trigram are of the same mind with them.

XIANG-L-46-03.label: Hexagram 46 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-46-03.translation: This line or image shows that the sincerity of the second nine brings joy.

XIANG-L-46-04.label: Hexagram 46 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-46-04.translation: The person advances upwards as into an empty city: the person has no doubt or hesitation.

XIANG-L-46-05.label: Hexagram 46 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-46-05.translation: This line or image shows that the king makes an offering at Mount Qi. This means acting in accord with the situation.

XIANG-L-46-06.label: Hexagram 46 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-46-06.translation: The person is firmly correct, and will therefore enjoy good fortune. The person ascends the stairs with all due ceremony: the person clearly succeeds in their aim.

XIANG-L-46-07.label: Hexagram 46 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-46-07.translation: The person blindly advances upwards, and is in the highest place: but there is decay in store for them, and the person will not preserve their riches.

XIANG-L-47-01.label: Hexagram 47 Great Image
XIANG-L-47-01.original: 澤无水，困；君子以致命遂志。
XIANG-L-47-01.translation: The trigram representing a marsh, and below it that for a defile, which has drained the other dry so that there is no water in it, form Kun. The noble person, following this image, will sacrifice their life in order to carry out their purpose.

XIANG-L-47-02.label: Hexagram 47 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-47-02.translation: The person enters a dark valley: so benighted is the person, and without clear vision.

XIANG-L-47-03.label: Hexagram 47 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-47-03.translation: The person is straitened amidst their wine and viands: but their position is central, and this will bring ground for congratulation.

XIANG-L-47-04.label: Hexagram 47 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-47-04.original: 據于蒺藜，乘剛也。入于其宮，不見其妻，不祥也。
XIANG-L-47-04.translation: The person lays hold of thorns: this is suggested by the position of the line above the strong line.

XIANG-L-47-05.label: Hexagram 47 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-47-05.original: 來徐徐，志在下也。雖不當位，有與也。
XIANG-L-47-05.translation: The person proceeds very slowly to help the person represented by the first line: their aim is directed to help that lower line. Although the person is not in their appropriate place, the person and that other will in the end be together.

XIANG-L-47-06.label: Hexagram 47 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-47-06.original: 劓刖，志未得也。乃徐有說，以中直也。利用祭祀，受福也。
XIANG-L-47-06.translation: Their nose and feet are cut off: their aim has not yet been gained.

XIANG-L-47-07.label: Hexagram 47 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-47-07.original: 困于葛藟，未當也。動悔，有悔，吉行也。
XIANG-L-47-07.translation: The person is straitened as if bound with creepers: their spirit and action are unsuitable.

XIANG-L-48-01.label: Hexagram 48 Great Image
XIANG-L-48-01.original: 木上有水，井；君子以勞民勸相。
XIANG-L-48-01.translation: The trigram representing wood and above it that for water form Jing. The noble person, following this image, comforts the people, and stimulates them to mutual helpfulness.

XIANG-L-48-02.label: Hexagram 48 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-48-02.original: 井泥不食，下也。舊井无禽，時舍也。
XIANG-L-48-02.translation: A well so muddy that men will not drink of it: this is shown by the low position of the line.

XIANG-L-48-03.label: Hexagram 48 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-48-03.translation: A well from which by a hole the water escapes, and flows away to the shrimps: the person represented by this second line has none co-operating with them above.

XIANG-L-48-04.label: Hexagram 48 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-48-04.original: 井渫不食，行惻也。求王明，受福也。
XIANG-L-48-04.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the well has been cleared out, but is not used: even passers-by would be sorry for this.

XIANG-L-48-05.label: Hexagram 48 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-48-05.translation: A well the lining of which is well laid. This will bring no error: the well has been put in good repair.

XIANG-L-48-06.label: Hexagram 48 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-48-06.translation: The waters from the cold spring are freely drunk: this is shown by the central and correct position of the line.

XIANG-L-48-07.label: Hexagram 48 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-48-07.translation: This line or image shows that the great good fortune at the topmost place indicates the grand accomplishment of the idea in the hexagram.

XIANG-L-49-01.label: Hexagram 49 Great Image
XIANG-L-49-01.original: 澤中有火，革；君子以治歷明時。
XIANG-L-49-01.translation: The trigram representing the waters of a marsh and that for fire in the midst of them form Ge. The noble person, following this image, regulates their astronomical calculations, and makes clear the seasons and times.

XIANG-L-49-02.label: Hexagram 49 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-49-02.original: 鞏用黃牛，不可以有為也。
XIANG-L-49-02.translation: The person is bound with the skin of a yellow ox: the person should in their circumstances be taking action.

XIANG-L-49-03.label: Hexagram 49 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-49-03.translation: The person makes their changes when some time has passed: what the person does will be matter of admiration.

XIANG-L-49-04.label: Hexagram 49 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-49-04.translation: This line or image shows that the change contemplated has been three times fully discussed: to what else should attention now be directed?

XIANG-L-49-05.label: Hexagram 49 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-49-05.translation: The good fortune consequent on changing existing ordinances is due to the faith reposed in their aims.

XIANG-L-49-06.label: Hexagram 49 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-49-06.translation: The person of mature character produces their changes as the tiger does when the person changes their stripes: their beauty becomes more brilliant.

XIANG-L-49-07.label: Hexagram 49 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-49-07.original: 君子豹變，其文蔚也。小人革面，順以從君也。
XIANG-L-49-07.translation: The noble person produces their changes as the leopard does when the person changes their spots: their beauty becomes more elegant.

XIANG-L-50-01.label: Hexagram 50 Great Image
XIANG-L-50-01.original: 木上有火，鼎；君子以正位凝命。
XIANG-L-50-01.translation: The trigram representing wood and above it that for fire form Ding. The noble person, following this image, keeps their every position correct, and maintains secure the appointment of Heaven.

XIANG-L-50-02.label: Hexagram 50 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-50-02.original: 鼎顛趾，未悖也。利出否，以從貴也。
XIANG-L-50-02.translation: This line or image shows that the cauldron is overturned, and its feet turned upwards: but this is not all contrary to what is right.

XIANG-L-50-03.label: Hexagram 50 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-50-03.original: 鼎有實，慎所之也。我仇有疾，終无尤也。
XIANG-L-50-03.translation: There is the cauldron with the things to be cooked in it: let the person represented by the line be careful where the person goes.

XIANG-L-50-04.label: Hexagram 50 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-50-04.translation: There is the cauldron with the places for its ears changed: its subject has failed in what was required of them in their situation.

XIANG-L-50-05.label: Hexagram 50 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-50-05.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the contents designed for the rulers use are overturned and spilt: how can the person represented by the line be trusted?

XIANG-L-50-06.label: Hexagram 50 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-50-06.translation: This line or image shows that the cauldron has yellow ears: the central position of the line is taken as a proof of the solid virtue of its subject.

XIANG-L-50-07.label: Hexagram 50 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-50-07.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the rings of jade are at the very top: the strong and the weak meet in their due proportions.

XIANG-L-51-01.label: Hexagram 51 Great Image
XIANG-L-51-01.original: 洊雷，震；君子以恐懼修省。
XIANG-L-51-01.translation: The trigram representing thunder, being repeated, forms Zhen. The noble person, following this image, is fearful and cautious, cultivates their virtue, and examines their faults.

XIANG-L-51-02.label: Hexagram 51 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-51-02.original: 震來虩虩，恐致福也。笑言啞啞，后有則也。
XIANG-L-51-02.translation: When the time of movement comes, the person will be found looking out with apprehension: that feeling of dread leads to happiness.

XIANG-L-51-03.label: Hexagram 51 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-51-03.translation: When the movement approaches, the person is in a position of danger: a weak line is mounted on a strong one.

XIANG-L-51-04.label: Hexagram 51 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-51-04.translation: The person is distraught amid the startling movements going on: the third line is in a position unsuitable to it.

XIANG-L-51-05.label: Hexagram 51 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-51-05.translation: Amid the startling movements, the person sinks supinely in the mud: the light in them has not yet been brilliantly developed.

XIANG-L-51-06.label: Hexagram 51 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-51-06.original: 震往來厲，危行也。其事在中，大无喪也。
XIANG-L-51-06.translation: The person goes and comes amid the startling movements, and always in danger: full of risk are their doings.

XIANG-L-51-07.label: Hexagram 51 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-51-07.original: 震索索，中未得也。雖凶无咎，畏鄰戒也。
XIANG-L-51-07.translation: Amid the startling movements the person is in breathless dismay: the person has not found out the course of the due mean.

XIANG-L-52-01.label: Hexagram 52 Great Image
XIANG-L-52-01.original: 兼山，艮；君子以思不出其位。
XIANG-L-52-01.translation: Two trigrams representing a mountain, one over the other, form Kan. The noble person, following this image, does not go in their thoughts beyond the duties of the position in which the person is.

XIANG-L-52-02.label: Hexagram 52 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-52-02.translation: The person keeps their toes at rest: the person does not fail in what is correct according to the idea of the figure.

XIANG-L-52-03.label: Hexagram 52 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-52-03.translation: The person cannot help them whom the person follows: the person whom the person follows will not retreat to listen to them.

XIANG-L-52-04.label: Hexagram 52 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-52-04.translation: The person keeps the loins at rest: the danger from their doing so produces a glowing heat in the heart.

XIANG-L-52-05.label: Hexagram 52 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-52-05.translation: The person keeps the trunk of their body at rest: the person keeps themself free from agitation.

XIANG-L-52-06.label: Hexagram 52 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-52-06.translation: The person keeps their cheek bones at rest: in harmony with their central position the person acts correctly.

XIANG-L-52-07.label: Hexagram 52 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-52-07.translation: There is good fortune through their devotedly maintaining their restfulness: to the end the person shows themself generous and good.

XIANG-L-53-01.label: Hexagram 53 Great Image
XIANG-L-53-01.original: 山上有木，漸；君子以居賢德，善俗。
XIANG-L-53-01.translation: The trigram representing a mountain and above it that for a tree form Kien. The noble person, following this image, attains to and maintains their extraordinary virtue, and makes the manners of the people good.

XIANG-L-53-02.label: Hexagram 53 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-53-02.translation: The danger of a small officer as represented in the first line is because of no fault of their in the matter of what is right.

XIANG-L-53-03.label: Hexagram 53 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-53-03.translation: This line or image shows that they eat and drink joyfully and at ease: but not without having earned their food.

XIANG-L-53-04.label: Hexagram 53 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-53-04.original: 夫征不復，離群丑也。婦孕不育，失其道也。利用禦寇，順相保也。
XIANG-L-53-04.translation: A husband goes and does not return: the person separates themself from their comrades.

XIANG-L-53-05.label: Hexagram 53 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-53-05.translation: This line or image shows that they may light on the flat branches: there is docility in the line going on to flexible penetration.

XIANG-L-53-06.label: Hexagram 53 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-53-06.translation: In the end the natural issue cannot be prevented. This will bring good fortune: the person represented by the line will get what the person desires.

XIANG-L-53-07.label: Hexagram 53 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-53-07.original: 其羽可用為儀，吉；不可亂也。
XIANG-L-53-07.translation: Their feathers can be used as ornaments. This will bring good fortune: the object and character of the person represented by the line cannot be disturbed.

XIANG-L-54-01.label: Hexagram 54 Great Image
XIANG-L-54-01.original: 澤上有雷，歸妹；君子以永終知敝。
XIANG-L-54-01.translation: The trigram representing the waters of a marsh and over it that for thunder form Gui Mei. The noble person, following this image, having regard to the far-distant end, knows the mischief that may be done at the beginning.

XIANG-L-54-02.label: Hexagram 54 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-54-02.original: 歸妹以娣，以恆也。跛能履吉，相承也。
XIANG-L-54-02.translation: This line or image shows that the younger sister is married off in a position ancillary to that of the real wife: it is the constant practice for such a case.

XIANG-L-54-03.label: Hexagram 54 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-54-03.translation: This will bring advantage in maintaining the steadfastness of a solitary widow: the person represented by the line has not changed from the constancy proper to a wife.

XIANG-L-54-04.label: Hexagram 54 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-54-04.translation: This line or image shows that the younger sister who was to be married off is in a mean position: this is shown by the improprieties indicated in the line.

XIANG-L-54-05.label: Hexagram 54 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-54-05.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the purpose in protracting the time is that, after waiting, the thing may be done all the better.

XIANG-L-54-06.label: Hexagram 54 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-54-06.original: 帝乙歸妹，不如其娣之袂良也。其位在中，以貴行也。
XIANG-L-54-06.translation: The sleeves of the younger sister of king Ti-yi, when she was married away, were not equal to those of her half- sister, who accompanied her: such was her noble character, shown by the central position of the line.

XIANG-L-54-07.label: Hexagram 54 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-54-07.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: what is said in the sixth line, divided, about there being nothing in the basket shows that the person represented by it is carrying an empty basket.

XIANG-L-55-01.label: Hexagram 55 Great Image
XIANG-L-55-01.original: 雷電皆至，豐；君子以折獄致刑。
XIANG-L-55-01.translation: The trigrams representing thunder and lightning combine to form Feng. The noble person, following this image, decides cases of litigation, and apportions punishments with exactness.

XIANG-L-55-02.label: Hexagram 55 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-55-02.translation: Though they are both of the same character, there is no blame: if the person represented by this line seek to overpass that similarity, this will bring serious trouble.

XIANG-L-55-03.label: Hexagram 55 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-55-03.translation: Let them cherish their feeling of sincere devotion, that it will appear being put forth: it is by sincerity that the mind is affected.

XIANG-L-55-04.label: Hexagram 55 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-55-04.original: 豐其沛，不可大事也。折其右肱，終不可用也。
XIANG-L-55-04.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: there is an additional screen of a large and thick banner: great things should not be attempted in such circumstances.

XIANG-L-55-05.label: Hexagram 55 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-55-05.original: 豐其蔀，位不當也。日中見斗，幽不明也。遇其夷主，吉；行也。
XIANG-L-55-05.translation: The person is surrounded by a screen large and thick: the position of the line is inappropriate.

XIANG-L-55-06.label: Hexagram 55 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-55-06.translation: The good fortune shown by the fifth yielding line, is the congratulation that is sure to arise.

XIANG-L-55-07.label: Hexagram 55 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-55-07.original: 豐其屋，天際翔也。窺其戶，闃其无人，自藏也。
XIANG-L-55-07.translation: The person has made their house large: the person soars in their pride to the heavens.

XIANG-L-56-01.label: Hexagram 56 Great Image
XIANG-L-56-01.original: 山上有火，旅；君子以明慎用刑，而不留獄。
XIANG-L-56-01.translation: The trigram representing a mountain and above it that for fire form Lu. The noble person, following this image, exerts their wisdom and caution in the use of punishments and not allowing litigations to continue.

XIANG-L-56-02.label: Hexagram 56 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-56-02.translation: The stranger is mean and meanly occupied: their aim is become of the lowest character, and serious trouble will ensue.

XIANG-L-56-03.label: Hexagram 56 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-56-03.translation: The person is provided with good and trusty servants: the person will in the end have nothing of which to complain.

XIANG-L-56-04.label: Hexagram 56 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-56-04.original: 旅焚其次，亦以傷矣。以旅與下，其義喪也。
XIANG-L-56-04.translation: The stranger burns their lodging-house: and the person themself also suffers hurt thereby. When, as a stranger, the person treats those below them as the line indicates, the right relation between them and them is lost.

XIANG-L-56-05.label: Hexagram 56 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-56-05.original: 旅于處，未得位也。得其資斧，心未快也。
XIANG-L-56-05.translation: The stranger is in a resting-place: but the person has not got their proper position.

XIANG-L-56-06.label: Hexagram 56 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-56-06.translation: * In the end the person will obtain praise and a high charge: the person has reached a high place.

XIANG-L-56-07.label: Hexagram 56 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-56-07.original: 以旅在上，其義焚也。喪牛于易，終莫之聞也。
XIANG-L-56-07.translation: Considering that the stranger is here at the very height of distinction, with the spirit that possesses them, it is right the person should be emblemed by a bird burning its nest.

XIANG-L-57-01.label: Hexagram 57 Great Image
XIANG-L-57-01.original: 隨風，巽；君子以申命行事。
XIANG-L-57-01.translation: Two trigrams representing wind, following each other, form Sun. The noble person, following this image, reiterates their orders, and secures the practice of their affairs.

XIANG-L-57-02.label: Hexagram 57 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-57-02.original: 進退，志疑也。利武人之貞，志治也。
XIANG-L-57-02.translation: Now the person advances, now the person recedes: their mind is perplexed.

XIANG-L-57-03.label: Hexagram 57 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-57-03.translation: This line or image shows that the good fortune springing from what borders on confusion is due to the position of the line in the centre.

XIANG-L-57-04.label: Hexagram 57 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-57-04.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the regret arising from the violent and repeated efforts to penetrate shows the exhaustion of the will.

XIANG-L-57-05.label: Hexagram 57 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-57-05.translation: The person takes game in their hunting, enough for the threefold use of it: the person achieves merit.

XIANG-L-57-06.label: Hexagram 57 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-57-06.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the good fortune of the fifth nine comes from its correct and central position.

XIANG-L-57-07.label: Hexagram 57 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-57-07.original: 巽在牀下，上窮也。喪其資斧，正乎凶也。
XIANG-L-57-07.translation: The representative of penetration is beneath a couch: though occupying the topmost place, their powers are exhausted.

XIANG-L-58-01.label: Hexagram 58 Great Image
XIANG-L-58-01.original: 麗澤，兌；君子以朋友講習。
XIANG-L-58-01.translation: Two symbols representing the waters of a marsh, one over the other, form Dui. The noble person, following this image, encourages the conversation of friends and the stimulus of their common practice.

XIANG-L-58-02.label: Hexagram 58 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-58-02.translation: This line or image shows that the good fortune attached to the pleasure of inward harmony arises from there being nothing in the conduct of the person represented by the line to awaken doubt.

XIANG-L-58-03.label: Hexagram 58 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-58-03.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the good fortune attached to the pleasure arising from inward sincerity is due to the confidence felt in the object of the person represented by the line.

XIANG-L-58-04.label: Hexagram 58 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-58-04.translation: The misfortune predicated of one's bringing around themself whatever can give pleasure is shown by the inappropriateness of the place of the line.

XIANG-L-58-05.label: Hexagram 58 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-58-05.translation: The joy in connection with, the person represented by the fourth firm line, is due to the happiness which the person will produce.

XIANG-L-58-06.label: Hexagram 58 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-58-06.translation: The person trusts in one who would injure them: their place is that which is correct and appropriate.

XIANG-L-58-07.label: Hexagram 58 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-58-07.translation: The topmost line, divided, shows the pleasure of its subject in leading and attracting others: their virtue is not yet brilliant.

XIANG-L-59-01.label: Hexagram 59 Great Image
XIANG-L-59-01.original: 風行水上，渙；先王以享于帝立廟。
XIANG-L-59-01.translation: The trigram representing water and that for wind moving above the water form Huan. The ancient kings, following this image, presented offerings to God and established the ancestral temple.

XIANG-L-59-02.label: Hexagram 59 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-59-02.translation: The good fortune attached to the first yielding line, is due to the natural course pursued by its subject.

XIANG-L-59-03.label: Hexagram 59 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-59-03.translation: Amidst the prevailing dispersion, the person hurries to their contrivance for security: the person gets what the person desires.

XIANG-L-59-04.label: Hexagram 59 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-59-04.translation: The person has no regard to their own person: their aim is directed to what is external to themself.

XIANG-L-59-05.label: Hexagram 59 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-59-05.translation: The person scatters the different parties in the state, and there is great good fortune: brilliant and great are their virtue and service.

XIANG-L-59-06.label: Hexagram 59 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-59-06.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the accumulations of the royal granaries are dispersed, and there is no error: this is due to the correctness of the position.

XIANG-L-59-07.label: Hexagram 59 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-59-07.translation: Their bloody wounds are gone: the person is far removed from the danger of injury.

XIANG-L-60-01.label: Hexagram 60 Great Image
XIANG-L-60-01.original: 澤上有水，節；君子以制數度，議德行。
XIANG-L-60-01.translation: The trigram representing a lake, and above it that for water, form Jie. The noble person, following this image, constructs their methods of numbering and measurement, and discusses points of virtue and conduct.

XIANG-L-60-02.label: Hexagram 60 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-60-02.translation: The person does not quit the courtyard outside their door: the person knows when the person has progress and when the person is obstructed.

XIANG-L-60-03.label: Hexagram 60 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-60-03.translation: The person does not quit the courtyard inside their gate. This will bring misfortune: the person loses the time for action to an extreme degree.

XIANG-L-60-04.label: Hexagram 60 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-60-04.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: in the lamentation for not observing the proper regulations, who should there be to blame?

XIANG-L-60-05.label: Hexagram 60 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-60-05.translation: This line or image shows that the progress and success of the quiet and natural attention to all regulations is due to the deference which accepts the ways of the ruler above.

XIANG-L-60-06.label: Hexagram 60 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-60-06.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the good fortune of pleasant restraint comes from occupying the central position.

XIANG-L-60-07.label: Hexagram 60 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-60-07.translation: The regulations are severe and difficult. Even with steadfastness this brings misfortune: the course shown by the hexagram is come to an end.

XIANG-L-61-01.label: Hexagram 61 Great Image
XIANG-L-61-01.original: 澤上有風，中孚；君子以議獄緩死。
XIANG-L-61-01.translation: The trigram representing the waters of a marsh and that for wind above it form Zhong Fu. The noble person, following this image, deliberates about cases of litigation and delays the infliction of death.

XIANG-L-61-02.label: Hexagram 61 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-61-02.translation: The first line, undivided, shows its subject resting in themself. This will bring good fortune: no change has yet come over their purpose.

XIANG-L-61-03.label: Hexagram 61 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-61-03.translation: Her young one's respond to her: from the common wish of the inmost heart.

XIANG-L-61-04.label: Hexagram 61 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-61-04.translation: Now the person beats their drum, and now the person leaves off: the position of the line is the appropriate one for it.

XIANG-L-61-05.label: Hexagram 61 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-61-05.translation: A horse the fellow of which disappears: the person breaks from their former companions, and mounts upwards.

XIANG-L-61-06.label: Hexagram 61 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-61-06.translation: The person is perfectly sincere, and links others to them in closest union: the place of the line is the correct and appropriate one.

XIANG-L-61-07.label: Hexagram 61 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-61-07.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: chanticleer tries to mount to heaven: but how can such an effort continue long?

XIANG-L-62-01.label: Hexagram 62 Great Image
XIANG-L-62-01.original: 山上有雷，小過；君子以行過乎恭，喪過乎哀，用過乎儉。
XIANG-L-62-01.translation: The trigram representing a hill and that for thunder above it form Xiao Guo. The noble person, following this image, in their conduct exceeds in humility, in mourning exceeds in sorrow, and in their expenditure exceeds in economy.

XIANG-L-62-02.label: Hexagram 62 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-62-02.translation: There is a bird flying and ascending till the result is misfortune: nothing can be done to avoid this issue.

XIANG-L-62-03.label: Hexagram 62 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-62-03.translation: The person does not attempt to reach their ruler: a minister should not overpass the distance between their ruler and themself.

XIANG-L-62-04.label: Hexagram 62 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-62-04.translation: Some in consequence find opportunity to assail and injure them. This will bring misfortune: how great will it be!

XIANG-L-62-05.label: Hexagram 62 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-62-05.original: 弗過遇之，位不當也。往厲必戒，終不可長也。
XIANG-L-62-05.translation: The person meets the exigency of their situation, without exceeding the proper course: the person does so, the position being inappropriate for a strong line.

XIANG-L-62-06.label: Hexagram 62 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-62-06.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: there are dense clouds, but no rain: the line is in too high a place.

XIANG-L-62-07.label: Hexagram 62 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-62-07.translation: The person does not meet the exigency of their situation, and exceeds their proper course: the position indicates the habit of domineering.

XIANG-L-63-01.label: Hexagram 63 Great Image
XIANG-L-63-01.original: 水在火上，既濟；君子以思患而豫防之。
XIANG-L-63-01.translation: The trigram representing fire and that for water above it form Ji Ji. The noble person, following this image, thinks of misfortune that may come, and beforehand guards against it.

XIANG-L-63-02.label: Hexagram 63 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-63-02.translation: The person drags back their wheel: as we may rightly judge, there is no mistake.

XIANG-L-63-03.label: Hexagram 63 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-63-03.translation: In seven days she will find it: for the course pursued is that shown by the central position of the line.

XIANG-L-63-04.label: Hexagram 63 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-63-04.translation: The person was three years in subduing it: enough to make them weary.

XIANG-L-63-05.label: Hexagram 63 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-63-05.translation: The person is on their guard all the day: the person is in doubt about something.

XIANG-L-63-06.label: Hexagram 63 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-63-06.original: 東鄰殺牛，不如西鄰之時也；實受其福，吉大來也。
XIANG-L-63-06.translation: This line or image shows that the slaughtering of an ox by the neighbour in the east is not equal to the small sacrifice of the neighbour in the west: because the time in the latter case is more important and fit.

XIANG-L-63-07.label: Hexagram 63 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-63-07.translation: Their head is immersed; the position is dangerous: how could such a state continue long?

XIANG-L-64-01.label: Hexagram 64 Great Image
XIANG-L-64-01.original: 火在水上，未濟；君子以慎辨物居方。
XIANG-L-64-01.translation: The trigram representing water and that for fire above it form Wei Ji. The noble person, following this image, carefully discriminates among the qualities of things, and the different positions they naturally occupy.

XIANG-L-64-02.label: Hexagram 64 Line Image 1
XIANG-L-64-02.translation: Their tail gets immersed: this is the very height of ignorance.

XIANG-L-64-03.label: Hexagram 64 Line Image 2
XIANG-L-64-03.translation: The second line, undivided, shows good fortune arising from being steadfast and right: it is in the central place, and the action of its subject thereby becomes correct.

XIANG-L-64-04.label: Hexagram 64 Line Image 3
XIANG-L-64-04.translation: The state of things is not yet remedied. Advancing will lead to misfortune: the place of the line is not that appropriate for it.

XIANG-L-64-05.label: Hexagram 64 Line Image 4
XIANG-L-64-05.translation: This line or image shows that by steadfastness there is good fortune, and cause for repentance disappears: the aim of the person represented by the line is carried into effect.

XIANG-L-64-06.label: Hexagram 64 Line Image 5
XIANG-L-64-06.translation: The image gives this practical lesson: the brightness of a noble person: the diffusion of that brightness tends to good fortune.

XIANG-L-64-07.label: Hexagram 64 Line Image 6
XIANG-L-64-07.translation: The person drinks and gets their head immersed: the person does not know how to submit to the proper regulations.

WENYAN-01-01.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 1
WENYAN-01-01.original: 元者，善之長也。亨者，嘉之會也。利者，義之和也。貞者，事之幹也。君子體仁足以長人，嘉會足以合禮，利物足以和義，貞固足以幹事。君子行此四德者，故曰：「乾，元、亨、利、貞。」
WENYAN-01-01.translation: What is called under Qian the great and originating is in man the first and chief quality of goodness; what is called the penetrating is the assemblage of excellences; what is called the beneficial is the harmony of all that is right; and what is called the steadfast and principled is the faculty of action. The noble person, embodying benevolence, is fit to preside over men; presenting the assemblage of excellences, the person is fit to show in themself the union of all propriety; benefiting all creatures, the person is fit to exhibit the harmony of all that is right; steadfast and principled, the person is fit to manage all affairs. The fact that the noble person practises these four virtues justifies the application to them of the words; Kfiien represents what is great and originating, penetrating, beneficial, steadfast and principled.

WENYAN-01-02.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 2
WENYAN-01-02.original: 初九曰：「潛龍，勿用。」何謂也？子曰：「龍德而隱者也。不易乎世，不成乎名，遯世无悶，不見是而无悶，樂則行之，憂則違之，確乎其不可拔，潛龍也。」
WENYAN-01-02.translation: What is the meaning of the words under the first line undivided, The dragon lies hid in the deep; it is not the time for active doing? The Master said: There the person is, with the powers of the dragon, and yet lying hid. The influence of the world would make no change in them; the person would do nothing merely to secure their fame. The person can live, withdrawn from the world, without regret; the person can experience disapproval without trouble of mind. Rejoicing in opportunity, the person carries their principles into action; sorrowing for want of opportunity, the person keeps with them in retirement. Yes, the person is not to be torn from their root in themself. This is the dragon lying hid.

WENYAN-01-03.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 3
WENYAN-01-03.original: 九二曰：「見龍在田，利見大人。」何謂也？子曰：「龍德而正中者也。庸言之信，庸行之謹；閑邪存其誠，善世而不伐，德博而化。易曰：『見龍在田，利見大人。』君德也。」
WENYAN-01-03.translation: What is the meaning of the words under the second line, The dragon shows themself and is in the field; it is favorable to see the great person? The Master said: There the person is, with the dragons powers, and occupying exactly the central place. The person is sincere even in their ordinary words, and earnest in their ordinary conduct. Guarding against depravity, the person preserves their sincerity. Their goodness is recognised in the world, but the person does not boast of it. Their virtue is extensively displayed, and transformation ensues. The language of the Yi, The dragon shows themself and is in the field; it is favorable to see the great person," refers to a rulers virtue.

WENYAN-01-04.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 4
WENYAN-01-04.original: 九三曰：「君子終日乾乾，夕惕若，厲，无咎。」何謂也？子曰：「君子進德脩業。忠信，所以進德也；脩辭立其誠，所以居業也。知至至之，可與言幾也。知終終之，可與存義也。是故居上位而不驕，在下位而不憂，故乾乾因其時而惕，雖危无咎矣。」
WENYAN-01-04.translation: What is the meaning of the words under the third line, The noble person is active and vigilant all the day, and in the evening still careful and cautious; the position is dangerous, but there is no mistake? The Master said: The noble person advances in virtue, and cultivates all the sphere of their duty. Their leal-heartedness and good faith are the way by which the person advances in virtue. Their attention to their words and establishinghis sincerity are the way by which the person occupies in their sphere. The person knows the utmost point to be reached, and reaches it, therefore showing themself in accord with the first springs of things; the person knows the end to be rested in, and rests in it, therefore preserving their righteousness in accordance with that end. Therefore the person occupies a high position without pride, and a low position without anxiety. Therefore it is that, being active and vigilant, and careful also and cautious as the time requires, though their position be dangerous, the person will make no mistake.

WENYAN-01-05.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 5
WENYAN-01-05.original: 九四曰：「或躍在淵，无咎。」何謂也？子曰：「上下无常，非為邪也。進退无恒，非離羣也。君子進德脩業，欲及時也。故无咎。」
WENYAN-01-05.translation: What is the meaning of the words under the fourth line, The person is as if the person were leaping up, but still is in the deep; there is no mistake? The Master said: The person finds no permanent place either above or below, but the person does not commit the error of advancing. The person may advance or recede; there is no permanent place for them: but the person does not leave their fellows. The noble person, advancing in virtue and cultivating the sphere of their duty, yet wishes to advance only at the proper time, and therefore there is no mistake.

WENYAN-01-06.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 6
WENYAN-01-06.original: 九五曰：「飛龍在天，利見大人。」何謂也？子曰：「同聲相應，同氣相求；水流濕，火就燥，雲從龍，風從虎；聖人作而萬物覩；本乎天者親上，本乎地者親下，則各從其類也。」
WENYAN-01-06.translation: What is the meaning of the words under the fifth line, The dragon is on the wing in the sky; it is favorable to see the great person? The Master said: Notes of the same key respond to one another; creatures of the same nature seek one another; water flows towards the place that is low and damp; fire rises up towards what is dry; clouds follow the dragon, and winds follow the tiger: so the sage makes their appearance, and all men look to them. Things that draw their origin from heaven move towards what is above; things that draw their origin from the earth cleave to what is below: so does everything follow its kind.

WENYAN-01-07.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 7
WENYAN-01-07.original: 上九曰：「亢龍，有悔。」何謂也？子曰：「貴而无位，高而无民，賢人在下位而无輔，是以動而有悔也。」
WENYAN-01-07.translation: What does “The dragon rises too high; there is regret” mean? The Master said: “The position is honored but carries no office; the person is high but has no people to lead. Capable people are below, but none can provide support. Therefore action brings regret.”.

WENYAN-01-08.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 8
WENYAN-01-08.translation: The passage is saying that the dragon lies hid; it is not the time for active doing: the position is too low.

WENYAN-01-09.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 9
WENYAN-01-09.translation: The dragon shows themself and is in the field: the time requires them still to be unemployed.

WENYAN-01-10.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 10
WENYAN-01-10.translation: All the day active and vigilant: the person now does their proper business.

WENYAN-01-11.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 11
WENYAN-01-11.translation: The person is as if the person were leaping up, but still is in the deep: the person is making trial of themself.

WENYAN-01-12.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 12
WENYAN-01-12.translation: This passage develops the idea in plain terms: the dragon is on the wing in the sky: the person represented by the line is on high and ruling.

WENYAN-01-13.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 13
WENYAN-01-13.translation: The dragon exceeds the proper limit, and this will bring cause for regret: when things have been carried to extremity, serious trouble ensues.

WENYAN-01-14.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 14
WENYAN-01-14.translation: Undivided lines appear in all these representations of the great and originating power denoted by AMien: what follows in the Yao tells us how all in the world this will bring good order.

WENYAN-01-15.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 15
WENYAN-01-15.translation: The passage is saying that the dragon lies hid in the deep; it is not the time for active doing: the energy denoted by the undivided line is laid up and hid away as in the deep.

WENYAN-01-16.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 16
WENYAN-01-16.translation: This passage develops the idea in plain terms: the dragon appears in the field: everyone in the world begins to be adorned and brightened.

WENYAN-01-17.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 17
WENYAN-01-17.translation: All the day active and vigilant: continually, as the time passes and requires, does the person act.

WENYAN-01-18.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 18
WENYAN-01-18.translation: The person is as if the person were leaping up, but still is in the deep: a change is taking place in the method shown by this Khien diagram.

WENYAN-01-19.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 19
WENYAN-01-19.translation: The dragon is on the wing in the sky: this shows that their place is based on their heavenly virtue.

WENYAN-01-20.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 20
WENYAN-01-20.translation: The dragon exceeds the proper limit; this will bring cause for regret: the time is come to an end, and so also is their opportunity.

WENYAN-01-21.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 21
WENYAN-01-21.translation: This passage develops the idea in plain terms: undivided lines appear in all these representations of the great and originating power denoted by Qian: and from what follows in the Yao the model of action afforded by heaven.

WENYAN-01-22.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 22
WENYAN-01-22.original: 乾元者，始而亨者也。利貞者，性情也。乾始能以美利利天下，不言所利，大矣哉！大哉乾元，剛健中正，純粹精也。六爻發揮，旁通情也。時乘六龍，以御天也。雲行雨施，天下平也。
WENYAN-01-22.translation: The passage is saying that the creative origin of Qian means that all things begin and then develop smoothly. “Beneficial and steadfast” describes the nature and proper direction of things. Qian begins the world and benefits everything through what is good, yet it does not claim any particular benefit for itself—how great this is! Great indeed is the creative power of Qian: strong, active, balanced, correct, pure, and refined. Its six lines unfold this meaning and connect it with every situation. At the right time, one rides the six dragons and works with heaven. Clouds move, rain falls, and the world comes into harmony.

WENYAN-01-23.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 23
WENYAN-01-23.original: 君子以成德為行，日可見之行也。潛之為言也，隱而未見，行而未成，是以君子弗用也。
WENYAN-01-23.translation: In the noble person their conduct is the fruit of their perfected virtue, which might be seen therefore in their daily course; but the force of that phrase, lying hid, requires them to keep retired, and not yet show themself, nor proceed to the full development of their course. While this is the case, the noble person knows that it is not the time for active doing-.

WENYAN-01-24.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 24
WENYAN-01-24.original: 君子學以聚之，問以辯之，寬以居之，仁以行之，易曰：「見龍在田，利見大人。」君德也。
