WENYAN-01-24.translation: The noble person learns and accumulates the results of their learning; puts questions, and discriminates among those results; dwells magnanimously and unambitiously in what the person has attained to; and carries it into practice with benevolence. What the Yi says, The dragon appears in the field: it is favorable to meet with the great person, has reference to the virtuous qualities of a ruler as therefore described.

WENYAN-01-25.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 25
WENYAN-01-25.original: 九三，重剛而不中，上不在天，下不在田；故乾乾因其時而惕，雖危，无咎矣。
WENYAN-01-25.translation: In the third line there is a twofold symbol of strength, but the position is not central. Its occupant is not in heaven above, nor is the person in the field beneath. Therefore there must be active vigilance and cautious apprehension as the time requires; and though the position be dangerous, there is no mistake.

WENYAN-01-26.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 26
WENYAN-01-26.original: 九四，重剛而不中，上不在天，下不在田，中不在人，故或之。或之者，疑之也，故无咎。
WENYAN-01-26.translation: In the fourth line there is the symbol of strength, but the position is not central. Its occupant is not in heaven above, nor is the person in the field beneath, nor is the person in the place of man intermediate. Hence the person is in perplexity; and being so, the person has doubts about what should be their movements, and so will give no occasion for blame.

WENYAN-01-27.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 27
WENYAN-01-27.original: 夫大人者，與天地合其德，與日月合其明，與四時合其序，與鬼神合其吉凶；先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時，天且弗違，而況於人乎？況於鬼神乎？
WENYAN-01-27.translation: The person of mature character is the person who is in harmony, in their attributes, with heaven and earth; in their brightness, with the sun and moon; in their orderly procedure, with the four seasons; and in their relation to what is fortunate and what is calamitous, in harmony with the spirit-like operations of Providence. The person may precede Heaven, and Heaven will not act in opposition to them; the person may follow Heaven, but will act only as Heaven at the time would do. If Heaven will not act in opposition to them, how much less will men! how much less will the spirit-like operation of Providence!

WENYAN-01-28.label: Hexagram 01 Words Commentary Unit 28
WENYAN-01-28.original: 亢之為言也，知進而不知退，知存而不知亡，知得而不知喪；其唯聖人乎？知進退存亡而不失其正者，其唯聖人乎！
WENYAN-01-28.translation: The force of that phrase; exceeding the proper limits; indicates the knbecause of advance but not to retire; to maintain but not to let perish; to get but not to lose. The person only is the sage who knows to advance and to retire, to maintain and to let perish; and that without ever acting incorrectly. Yes, the person only is the sage!

WENYAN-02-01.label: Hexagram 02 Words Commentary Unit 1
WENYAN-02-01.original: 坤至柔而動也剛，至靜而德方。後得主而有常，含萬物而化光。坤道其順乎！承天而時行。
WENYAN-02-01.translation: What is shown by Kun is most gentle and weak, but, when put in motion, is hard and strong; it is most still, but is able to give every definite form. By following, it obtains its proper lord, and pursues its regular course. It contains all things in itself, and its transforming power is glorious. Yes, what docility marks the way of Kun! It receives the influences of heaven, and acts at the proper time.

WENYAN-02-02.label: Hexagram 02 Words Commentary Unit 2
WENYAN-02-02.original: 積善之家，必有餘慶；積不善之家，必有餘殃。臣弒其君，子弒其父，非一朝一夕之故，其所由來者漸矣。由辨之不早辨也。易曰：「履霜，堅冰至。」蓋言順也。
WENYAN-02-02.translation: The family that accumulates goodness is sure to have superabundant happiness, and the family that accumulates misfortune is sure to have superabundant misery. The murder of a ruler by their minister, or of their father by a son, is not the result of the events of one morning or one evening. The causes of it have gradually accumulated,; through the absence of early discrimination. The words of the Yi, The person treads on the hoar-frost; the strong ice will come by and by, show the natural issue and growth of things.

WENYAN-02-03.label: Hexagram 02 Words Commentary Unit 3
WENYAN-02-03.original: 直其正也，方其義也。君子敬以直內，義以方外，敬義立而德不孤。「直方大，不習无不利。」則不疑其所行也。
WENYAN-02-03.translation: Straight indicates the correctness of the internal principle, and square, the righteousness of the external act. The noble person, therefore represented, by their self-reverence maintains the inward correctness, and in righteousness adjusts their external acts. Their reverence and righteousness being therefore established, their virtues are not solitary instances or of a single class. Straight, square, and great, working their operations, without repeated efforts, in every respect beneficial: this shows how such a one has no doubts as to what the person does.

WENYAN-02-04.label: Hexagram 02 Words Commentary Unit 4
WENYAN-02-04.original: 陰雖有美，含之。以從王事，弗敢成也。地道也，妻道也，臣道也。地道无成，而代有終也。
WENYAN-02-04.translation: Although the person represented by this divided line has excellent qualities, the person does not display them, but keeps them under restraint. If the person engage with them in the service of the king, and be successful, the person will not claim that success for themself: this is the way of the earth, of a wife, of a minister. The way of the earth is; not to claim the merit of achievement, but on behalf of heaven to bring things to their proper issue.

WENYAN-02-05.label: Hexagram 02 Words Commentary Unit 5
WENYAN-02-05.original: 天地變化，草木蕃；天地閉，賢人隱。易曰：「括囊，无咎，无譽。」蓋言謹也。
WENYAN-02-05.translation: Through the changes and transformations produced by heaven and earth, plants and trees grow luxuriantly. If the reciprocal influence of heaven and earth were shut up and restrained, we should have a state that might suggest to us the case of men of virtue and ability lying in obscurity. The words of the Yi, A sack tied up: this will bring no ground for blame or for praise, are in reality a lesson of caution.

WENYAN-02-06.label: Hexagram 02 Words Commentary Unit 6
WENYAN-02-06.original: 君子黃中通理，正位居體，美在其中，而暢於四支，發於事業，美之至也。
WENYAN-02-06.translation: The noble person emblemed here by the yellow and correct colour, is possessed of comprehension and discrimination. The person occupies the correct position of supremacy, but that emblem is on the lower part of their person. Their excellence is in the centre of their being, but it diffuses a complacency over their four limbs, and is manifested in their conduct of affairs: this is the perfection of excellence.

WENYAN-02-07.label: Hexagram 02 Words Commentary Unit 7
WENYAN-02-07.original: 陰疑於陽必戰，為其嫌於无陽也，故稱龍焉。猶未離其類也，故稱血焉。夫玄黃者，天地之雜也。天玄而地黃。
WENYAN-02-07.translation: The subject of the yin or divided line thinking themself equal to the subject of the yang, or undivided line, there is sure to be a contest As if indignant at there being no acknowledgment of the superiority of the person represented by the yang line, the text uses the term dragons. But still the subject of neither line can leave their class, and therefore we have the blood mentioned. The mention of that as being both azure and yellow indicates the mixture of heaven and earth. Heavens colour is azure and earths is yellow.

XICI-U-01-01.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 1 Unit 1
XICI-U-01-01.original: 天尊地卑，乾坤定矣。卑高以陳，貴賤位矣。動靜有常，剛柔斷矣。方以類聚，物以羣分，吉凶生矣。在天成象，在地成形，變化見矣。是故剛柔相摩，八卦相荡，鼓之以雷霆，潤之以風雨，日月運行，一寒一暑。乾道成男，坤道成女；乾知大始，坤作成物；乾以易知，坤以簡能；易則易知，簡則易從；易知則有親，易從則有功；有親則可久，有功則可大；可久則賢人之德，可大則賢人之業。易簡，而天下之理得矣。天下之理得，而成位乎其中矣。
XICI-U-01-01.translation: Heaven is honored and earth is low; therefore Qian and Kun are determined. As low and high are arranged, noble and humble positions are established. Movement and stillness have their constants; therefore firmness and yielding are distinguished. Directions gather by kind, and things divide into groups; therefore good fortune and misfortune arise. In heaven these become images; on earth they become forms; therefore change and transformation become visible. Firmness and yielding rub against one another, and the eight trigrams stimulate one another. Thunder and lightning stir them; wind and rain moisten them; sun and moon move in their courses; now cold, now heat. The way of Qian forms the male; the way of Kun forms the female. Qian directs the great beginnings, while Kun brings things to completion. Qian knows through ease, and Kun accomplishes through simplicity. What is easy is easy to know; what is simple is easy to follow. What is easy to know gains affinity; what is easy to follow gains achievement. Affinity can endure; achievement can grow great. Endurance is the virtue of the worthy; greatness is the work of the worthy. Through ease and simplicity, the principles of the world are obtained; once those principles are obtained, a place is established amid heaven and earth.

XICI-U-02-01.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 2 Unit 1
XICI-U-02-01.original: 聖人設卦觀象，繫辭焉而明吉凶；剛柔相推而生變化。是故吉凶者，失得之象也。悔吝者，憂虞之象也。變化者，進退之象也。剛柔者，晝夜之象也。六爻之動，三極之道也。是故君子所居而安者，易之序也。所樂而玩者，爻之辭也。是故君子居則觀其象而玩其辭，動則觀其變而玩其占；是以自天祐之，吉无不利。
XICI-U-02-01.translation: The sages established the hexagrams, observed their images, and attached statements to clarify good fortune and misfortune. Firm and yielding lines press upon one another and produce change and transformation. Therefore good fortune and misfortune are images of gain and loss; remorse and regret are images of anxiety and concern; change and transformation are images of advance and retreat; firmness and yielding are images of day and night. The movement of the six lines expresses the way of the Three Powers. Therefore the noble person finds security in the order of the Yi and takes delight in studying the line statements. At rest, the person observes the images and reflects on the words; in action, the person observes the changes and reflects on the prognostications. In this way, “Help comes from heaven; good fortune, nothing unfavorable.”.

XICI-U-03-01.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 3 Unit 1
XICI-U-03-01.original: 彖者，言乎象者也。爻者，言乎變者也。吉凶者，言乎其失得也。悔吝者，言乎其小疵也。无咎者，善補過也。是故列貴賤者存乎位，齊小大者存乎卦，辯吉凶者存乎辭，憂悔吝者存乎介，震无咎者存乎悔。是故卦有小大，辭有險易，辭也者，各指其所之。
XICI-U-03-01.translation: The Judgments speak about the images of the hexagrams; the line statements speak about change. Good fortune and misfortune speak about gain and loss; remorse and regret speak about minor faults; “no blame” means correcting faults well. Therefore the ranking of noble and humble depends on position; the balancing of small and great depends on the hexagram; distinguishing good fortune and misfortune depends on the statements; concern over remorse and regret depends on the boundary between choices; freedom from blame through alarm depends on repentance. Hexagrams therefore differ as small or great, and their statements as dangerous or easy; each statement points to the direction in which the situation is moving.

XICI-U-04-01.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 4 Unit 1
XICI-U-04-01.original: 易與天地準，故能彌綸天地之道。仰以觀於天文，俯以察於地理，是故知幽明之故。原始反終，故知死生之說。精氣為物，遊魂為變，是故知鬼神之情狀。與天地相似，故不違；知周乎萬物，而道濟天下，故不過；旁行而不流，樂天知命，故不憂；安土敦乎仁，故能愛；範圍天地之化而不過，曲成萬物而不遺，通乎晝夜之道而知，故神无方而易无體。
XICI-U-04-01.translation: The Yi accords with heaven and earth and therefore can encompass their way. Looking upward, one observes the patterns of heaven; looking downward, one examines the arrangements of earth, and therefore understands the causes of what is hidden and manifest. Tracing beginnings and returning to endings, one understands the account of life and death. Concentrated vital energy becomes things; the wandering soul produces change, and therefore one understands the conditions of spirits. Because the Yi resembles heaven and earth, it does not oppose them. Its knowledge embraces all things, and its way aids the world, so it does not overstep. It extends in every direction without being swept away; delighting in heaven and understanding destiny, it is free of anxiety. At peace in its place and deep in humaneness, it can love. It frames the transformations of heaven and earth without excess, completes all things without omission, and penetrates the way of day and night. Therefore spirit has no fixed direction and the Yi has no fixed form.

XICI-U-05-01.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 5 Unit 1
XICI-U-05-01.original: 一陰一陽之謂道：繼之者善也，成之者性也；仁者見之謂之仁，知者見之謂之知；百姓日用而不知，故君子之道鮮矣。顯諸仁，藏諸用，鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂，盛德大業至矣哉！富有之謂大業，日新之謂盛德，生生之謂易，成象之謂乾，效法之謂坤，極數知來之謂占，通變之謂事，陰陽不測之謂神。
XICI-U-05-01.translation: In everyday terms, the idea is this: one yin and one yang are called the Way. What continues it is goodness; what completes it is human nature. The humane see it and call it humaneness; the wise see it and call it wisdom. The common people use it every day without knowing it, so the way of the noble person is rarely recognized. It manifests in humaneness and is hidden in its functions; it animates all things without sharing the sages’ anxieties. How complete are its abundant virtue and great work! Rich possession is called great work; daily renewal is called abundant virtue; producing life without end is called change; completing images is called Qian; imitating the model is called Kun; carrying number to its limit to know what is coming is called divination; penetrating change is called undertaking; what cannot be fathomed in yin and yang is called spirit.

XICI-U-06-01.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 6 Unit 1
XICI-U-06-01.original: 夫易，廣矣！大矣！以言乎遠則不禦，以言乎邇則靜而正，以言乎天地之間則備矣！夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。廣大配天地，變通配四時，陰陽之義配日月，易簡之善配至德。
XICI-U-06-01.translation: The passage makes this point: how broad and great the Yi is! Speaking of what is distant, it has no limit; speaking of what is near, it is still and correct; speaking of the space between heaven and earth, it is complete. Qian in stillness is concentrated and in movement is straight; therefore it gives rise to greatness. Kun in stillness is closed and in movement opens; therefore it gives rise to breadth. Breadth and greatness correspond to heaven and earth; change and continuity correspond to the four seasons; the meaning of yin and yang corresponds to sun and moon; and the excellence of ease and simplicity corresponds to the highest virtue.

XICI-U-07-01.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 7 Unit 1
XICI-U-07-01.original: 子曰：「易其至矣乎！夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也，知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。天地設位，而易行乎其中矣。成性存存，道義之門。」
XICI-U-07-01.translation: The Master said: “Has not the Yi reached the highest point? Through it the sages exalted virtue and broadened their work. Knowledge is lofty and ritual is humble: loftiness models heaven, while humility follows earth. Heaven and earth establish their positions, and change moves between them. When one repeatedly preserves and completes one’s nature, the gateway of the Way and righteousness opens.”.

XICI-U-08-01.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 8 Unit 1
XICI-U-08-01.original: 聖人有以見天下之賾，而擬諸其形容，象其物宜，是故謂之象。聖人有以見天下之動，而觀其會通，以行其典禮，繫辭焉以斷其吉凶，是故謂之爻。言天下之至賾而不可惡也，言天下之至動而不可亂也。擬之而後言，議之而後動，擬議以成其變化。
XICI-U-08-01.translation: The passage makes this point: the sages perceived the complexities of the world, represented them through visible forms, and imaged what was appropriate to each thing; therefore these are called images. The sages perceived the movements of the world, observed how they met and communicated, enacted enduring principles and rites, and attached statements to determine good fortune and misfortune; therefore these are called lines. They speak of the world’s utmost complexity without arousing aversion and of its utmost movement without creating disorder. One first models a matter and then speaks, first deliberates and then acts; through modeling and deliberation, change and transformation are completed.

XICI-U-08-02.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 8 Unit 2
XICI-U-08-02.original: 「鳴鶴在陰，其子和之。我有好爵，吾與爾靡之。」子曰：「君子居其室，出其言善，則千里之外應之，況其邇者乎！居其室，出其言不善，則千里之外違之，況其邇者乎！言出乎身加乎民；行發乎邇見乎遠。言行，君子之樞機；樞機之發，榮辱之主也。言行，君子之所以動天地也，可不慎乎！」「同人，先號咷而後笑。」子曰：「君子之道，或出或處，或默或語。二人同心，其利斷金。同心之言，其臭如蘭。」
XICI-U-08-02.translation: “A calling crane is in the shade; its young answers it. I have a fine cup, and I will share it with you.” The Master said: “If a noble person stays in their room and speaks well, people respond from a thousand miles away; how much more those who are near. If the person stays in their room and speaks badly, people oppose them from a thousand miles away; how much more those who are near. Words issue from oneself and reach the people; actions begin nearby and become visible far away. Speech and action are the hinge and trigger of the noble person. When that hinge and trigger move, they govern honor and disgrace. Through speech and action the noble person moves heaven and earth; can the person fail to be careful?” “In Tong Ren, first there is wailing and then laughter.” The Master said: “The way of two noble persons may lead one to serve or withdraw, to remain silent or speak. When two people are of one heart, their sharpness cuts metal; words from united hearts are fragrant like orchids.”.

XICI-U-08-03.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 8 Unit 3
XICI-U-08-03.original: 「初六，藉用白茅，无咎。」子曰：「苟錯諸地而可矣。藉之用茅，何咎之有！慎之至也。夫茅之為物薄而用可重也，慎斯術也以往，其无所失矣。」
XICI-U-08-03.translation: “At the beginning, use white cogon grass as a mat; no blame.” The Master said: “It would have been enough simply to place the offering on the ground. What blame could there be in placing it on grass? This is the utmost care. Cogon grass is a slight thing, yet its use can be weighty. If one proceeds with such care, nothing will be lost.”.

XICI-U-08-04.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 8 Unit 4
XICI-U-08-04.original: 「勞謙，君子有終，吉。」子曰：「勞而不伐，有功而不德，厚之至也；語以其功下人者也。德言盛，禮言恭；謙也者，致恭以存其位者也。」
XICI-U-08-04.translation: “Toiling yet modest, the noble person has a good end: good fortune.” The Master said: “To labor without boasting, to achieve merit without claiming virtue; this is the height of generosity. It means placing oneself below others despite one’s achievements. Virtue speaks of fullness; ritual speaks of reverence. Modesty is carrying reverence to its utmost so as to preserve one’s position.”.

XICI-U-08-05.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 8 Unit 5
XICI-U-08-05.original: 「亢龍有悔。」子曰：「貴而无位，高而无民，賢人在下位而无輔，是以動而有悔也。」
XICI-U-08-05.translation: “The overreaching dragon has regret.” The Master said: “Noble yet without a position, high yet without people, with worthy persons below but no support; therefore action brings regret.”.

XICI-U-08-06.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 8 Unit 6
XICI-U-08-06.original: 「不出戶庭，无咎。」子曰：「亂之所生也，則言語以為階。君不密則失臣，臣不密則失身，幾事不密則害成；是以君子慎密而不出也。」
XICI-U-08-06.translation: “Not going beyond the courtyard, no blame.” The Master said: “Disorder arises when speech becomes its stairway. If a ruler is not discreet, the person loses their minister; if a minister is not discreet, the person loses their life; if incipient affairs are not kept discreet, their completion is harmed. Therefore the noble person is careful about secrecy and does not let words go forth.”.

XICI-U-08-07.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 8 Unit 7
XICI-U-08-07.original: 子曰：「作易者，其知盜乎！易曰：『負且乘，致寇至。』負也者，小人之事也。乘也者，君子之器也。小人而乘君子之器，盜思奪之矣。上慢下暴，盜思伐之矣。慢藏誨盜，冶容誨淫。易曰：『負且乘，致寇至。』盜之招也。」
XICI-U-08-07.translation: The Master said: “Did the makers of the Yi understand how robbers arise? The Yi says, ‘The person bears a burden yet rides in a carriage, thereby bringing robbers upon themself.’ Bearing burdens is the work of a common person; a carriage is the conveyance of a noble person. When a common person rides in a noble person’s carriage, robbers are tempted to seize it. When those above are careless and those below are violent, attackers are tempted to strike. Careless storage teaches theft, and provocative display encourages lust. Therefore the Yi says, ‘The person bears a burden yet rides in a carriage, thereby bringing robbers upon themself.’ It describes how one invites robbers.”.

XICI-U-09-01.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 9 Unit 1
XICI-U-09-01.original: 天一地二，天三地四，天五地六，天七地八，天九地十。天數五，地數五，五位相得而各有合。天數二十有五，地數三十，凡天地之數，五十有五，此所以成變化，而行鬼神也。大衍之數五十，其用四十有九，分而為二以象兩，掛一以象三，揲之以四以象四時，歸奇於扐以象閏，五歲再閏，故再扐而後掛。
XICI-U-09-01.translation: In everyday terms, the idea is this: one belongs to heaven, two to earth; three to heaven, four to earth; five to heaven, six to earth; seven to heaven, eight to earth; nine to heaven, ten to earth. Heaven has five numbers and earth has five numbers. Their five positions correspond and each has its partner. The numbers of heaven total twenty-five and those of earth total thirty; together the numbers of heaven and earth total fifty-five. By these, changes and transformations are completed and the actions of spirits are carried out. The number of the Great Expansion is fifty, of which forty-nine are used. They are divided into two to symbolize the two powers; one is set aside to symbolize the third; they are counted by fours to symbolize the four seasons; the remainders are placed between the fingers to symbolize the intercalary month. In five years there are two intercalary months, so the remainder is taken twice before the next operation.

XICI-U-09-02.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 9 Unit 2
XICI-U-09-02.original: 乾之策，二百一十有六，坤之策，百四十有四，凡三百有六十，當期之日。二篇之策，萬有一千五百二十，當萬物之數也。是故四營而成易，十有八變而成卦，八卦而小成；引而伸之，觸類而長之，天下之能事畢矣。顯道神德行，是故可與酬酢，可與祐神矣。子曰：「知變化之道者，其知神之所為乎！」
XICI-U-09-02.translation: The yarrow stalk numbers for Qian are 216 and for Kun 144, totaling 360, corresponding to the days of the year. The stalk numbers of the two parts total 11,520, corresponding to the number of all things. Therefore four operations complete one change; eighteen changes complete a hexagram; the eight trigrams form the small completion. Extend and develop them, encounter each category and enlarge it, and every possible affair under heaven is encompassed. They reveal the Way and make virtuous conduct spirit-like; therefore they can respond to all circumstances and assist spiritual powers. The Master said: “Whoever knows the way of change and transformation knows what spirit does.”.

XICI-U-10-01.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 10 Unit 1
XICI-U-10-01.original: 易有聖人之道四焉：以言者尚其辭，以動者尚其變，以制器者尚其象，以卜筮者尚其占。是以君子將有為也，將有行也，問焉而以言，其受命也如響，无有遠近幽深，遂知來物。非天下之至精，其孰能與於此！
XICI-U-10-01.translation: The Yi contains four ways of the sages: those who speak value its statements; those who act value its changes; those who make implements value its images; those who divine value its prognostications. Therefore, when a noble person intends to undertake or perform something, the person asks through words. The answer receives their command like an echo; whether far or near, hidden or deep, it enables them to know what is coming. Unless it were the finest essence under heaven, what could participate in this?

XICI-U-10-02.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 10 Unit 2
XICI-U-10-02.original: 參伍以變，錯綜其數，通其變，遂成天下之文，極其數，遂定天下之象；非天下之至變，其孰能與於此！
XICI-U-10-02.translation: The passage makes this point: through repeated comparison, numbers are changed and interwoven. By penetrating their changes, the patterns of the world are formed; by carrying their numbers to the limit, the images of the world are determined. Unless it were the most transformative power under heaven, what could participate in this?

XICI-U-10-03.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 10 Unit 3
XICI-U-10-03.original: 易，无思也，无為也，寂然不動，感而遂通天下之故。非天下之至神，其孰能與於此！
XICI-U-10-03.translation: In everyday terms, the idea is this: the Yi has no thought and takes no action. Silent and unmoving, when stimulated it penetrates the causes of all things under heaven. Unless it were the most spirit-like power under heaven, what could participate in this?

XICI-U-10-04.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 10 Unit 4
XICI-U-10-04.original: 夫易，聖人之所以極深而研幾也！唯深也，故能通天下之志；唯幾也，故能成天下之務；唯神也，故不疾而速，不行而至。
XICI-U-10-04.translation: The passage makes this point: through the Yi the sages reached the deepest and examined the subtlest beginnings. Because it is deep, it can penetrate the intentions of the world; because it attends to subtle beginnings, it can complete the world’s affairs; because it is spirit-like, it is swift without haste and arrives without traveling.

XICI-U-10-05.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 10 Unit 5
XICI-U-10-05.original: 子曰「易有聖人之道四焉」者，此之謂也。
XICI-U-10-05.translation: When the Master said, “The Yi contains four ways of the sages,” this is what the person meant.

XICI-U-11-01.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 11 Unit 1
XICI-U-11-01.original: 子曰：「夫易，何為者也？夫易，開物成務，冒天下之道，如斯而已者也。」是故聖人以通天下之志，以定天下之業，以斷天下之疑。是故蓍之德圓而神，卦之德方以知，六爻之義易以貢；聖人以此洗心，退藏於密，吉凶與民同患，神以知來，知以藏往，其孰能與此哉？古之聦明叡知神武而不殺者夫！是以明於天之道，而察於民之故，是興神物以前民用；聖人以此齊戒以神明其德夫！是故闔戶謂之坤，闢戶謂之乾，一闔一闢謂之變；往來不窮謂之通，見乃謂之象，形乃謂之器，制而用之謂之法，利用出入，民咸用之謂之神。是故易有太極，是生兩儀，兩儀生四象，四象生八卦，八卦定吉凶，吉凶生大業。是故法象莫大乎天地；變通莫大乎四時；縣象著明莫大乎日月；崇高莫大乎富貴；備物致用，立成器以為天下利，莫大乎聖人；探賾索隱，鉤深致遠，以定天下之吉凶，成天下之亹亹者，莫大乎蓍龜。是故天生神物，聖人則之。天地變化，聖人效之。天垂象，見吉凶，聖人象之。河出圖，洛出書，聖人則之。易有四象，所以示也。繫辭焉，所以告也。定之以吉凶，所以斷也。
XICI-U-11-01.translation: The Master said: “What does the Yi do? It opens up things, completes undertakings, and encompasses the ways of everyone in the world; nothing more than this.” Therefore the sages used it to communicate the intentions of the world, establish its undertakings, and resolve its doubts. The virtue of the yarrow stalks is round and spirit-like; the virtue of the hexagrams is square and wise; the meanings of the six lines change so as to provide guidance. With these the sages purified their hearts and withdrew into secrecy, sharing the people’s concerns about good and bad fortune. Through spirit they knew what was coming; through wisdom they stored what had passed. Who could do this except the ancient sages, whose intelligence, insight, spiritual power, and martial strength did not depend on killing? Understanding the way of heaven and examining the conditions of the people, they established the numinous objects to guide the people’s use. The sages purified and disciplined themselves so as to make their virtue spiritually luminous. A closed door is called Kun; an open door is called Qian. One closing and one opening are called change; coming and going without exhaustion are called continuity. What becomes visible is called an image; what takes form is called an implement; what is regulated for use is called a model; what benefits people in going out and coming in and is used by all is called spirit. Therefore the Yi has the Great Ultimate, which produces the Two Forms; the Two Forms produce the Four Images; the Four Images produce the Eight Trigrams. The eight trigrams determine good and bad fortune, and good and bad fortune give rise to great undertakings. No models and images are greater than heaven and earth; no change and continuity are greater than the four seasons; no suspended images shine more clearly than sun and moon; nothing exalted is greater than wealth and rank; in preparing things for use and establishing instruments for the benefit of the world, none are greater than the sages; in probing complexity, seeking the hidden, drawing up what is deep, and reaching what is distant; thereby determining good and bad fortune and completing the world’s endeavors; nothing is greater than the yarrow stalks and tortoise shell. Heaven produced numinous things, and the sages took them as models. Heaven and earth change and transform, and the sages imitated them. Heaven displayed images that revealed good and bad fortune, and the sages represented them. The Yellow River produced the Chart and the Luo River produced the Writing, and the sages took them as models. The Yi has four kinds of images in order to reveal; statements are attached in order to communicate; good and bad fortune are determined in order to decide.

XICI-U-12-01.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 12 Unit 1
XICI-U-12-01.original: 易曰：「自天祐之，吉无不利」。子曰：「祐者，助也。天之所助者，順也。人之所助者，信也。履信思乎順，又以尚賢也，是以『自天祐之，吉无不利。』也。」
XICI-U-12-01.translation: The Yi says, “Help comes from heaven; good fortune, nothing unfavorable.” The Master said: “Help means assistance. Heaven assists those who are compliant; people assist those who are trustworthy. One practices trustworthiness, keeps compliance in mind, and also honors the worthy. Therefore, ‘Help comes from heaven; good fortune, nothing unfavorable.’”.

XICI-U-12-02.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 12 Unit 2
XICI-U-12-02.original: 子曰：「書不盡言，言不盡意。」然則聖人之意，其不可見乎？子曰：「聖人立象以盡意，設卦以盡情偽，繫辭以盡其言，變而通之以盡利，鼓之舞之以盡神。」
XICI-U-12-02.translation: The Master said: “Writing does not exhaust words, and words do not exhaust meaning.” Then can the intentions of the sages not be seen? The Master said: “The sages established images to express meaning fully, set up hexagrams to disclose true and false conditions fully, attached statements to express their words fully, developed change and continuity to realize benefit fully, and stirred and animated them to express spiritual efficacy fully.”.

XICI-U-12-03.label: Appended Statements I Chapter 12 Unit 3
XICI-U-12-03.original: 乾坤，其易之縕邪！乾坤成列，而易立乎其中矣。乾坤毀，則无以見易，易不可見，則乾坤或幾乎息矣。是故形而上者謂之道，形而下者謂之器，化而裁之謂之變，推而行之謂之通，舉而錯之天下之民謂之事業。是故夫象，聖人有以見天下之賾，而擬諸其形容，象其物宜，是故謂之象。聖人有以見天下之動，而觀其會通，以行其典禮，繫辭焉以斷其吉凶，是故謂之爻。極天下之賾者存乎卦；鼓天下之動者存乎辭；化而裁之存乎變；推而行之存乎通；神而明之，存乎其人；默而成之，不言而信，存乎德行。
XICI-U-12-03.translation: Are Qian and Kun not the inner core of the Yi? When Qian and Kun are set in order, the Yi stands between them. If Qian and Kun were destroyed, there would be no means to perceive the Yi; if the Yi could not be perceived, Qian and Kun would nearly cease. Therefore what precedes physical form is called the Way; what follows physical form is called an implement. Transforming and shaping are called change; extending and carrying forward are called continuity; applying them to all people under heaven is called an undertaking. As for images: the sages perceived the complexities of the world, represented them through visible forms, and imaged what was appropriate to each thing; therefore these are called images. The sages perceived the movements of the world, observed how they met and communicated, enacted enduring principles and rites, and attached statements to determine good and bad fortune; therefore these are called lines. What exhausts the world’s complexities resides in the hexagrams; what stirs the world’s movements resides in the statements; shaping transformation resides in change; extending it into action resides in continuity. Making it spiritually clear depends on the person; silently completing it and being trusted without words depend on virtuous conduct.

XICI-L-01-01.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 1 Unit 1
XICI-L-01-01.original: 八卦成列，象在其中矣；因而重之，爻在其中矣；剛柔相推，變在其中矣；繫辭焉而命之，動在其中矣。吉凶悔吝者，生乎動者也。剛柔者，立本者也；變通者，趣時者也；吉凶者，貞勝者也。天地之道，貞觀者也；日月之道，貞明者也；天下之動，貞夫一者也。夫乾，確然示人易矣；夫坤，隤然示人簡矣。爻也者，效此者也；象也者，像此者也。爻象動乎內，吉凶見乎外，功業見乎變，聖人之情見乎辭。天地之大德曰生，聖人之大寶曰位，何以守位曰仁，何以聚人曰財，理財正辭，禁民為非曰義。
XICI-L-01-01.translation: Once the eight trigrams had been set in order, their images were contained within them. By doubling them, the lines of the hexagrams were contained within them. As the firm and yielding lines press upon one another, change is contained within them. By attaching statements and assigning meanings, movement is contained within them. Good fortune, misfortune, remorse, and regret arise from movement. Firmness and yielding establish the foundation; transformation and continuity follow the demands of the time; good and bad fortune are determined by steadfast correctness. The way of heaven and earth is revealed through constancy; the way of the sun and moon is revealed through constant illumination; and all movement under heaven is governed by constancy in the One. Qian clearly shows what is easy, while Kun gently shows what is simple. The lines imitate this, and the images represent it. The lines and images move within; good and bad fortune appear without; achievement becomes visible through change; and the intentions of the sages appear in the statements. The great virtue of heaven and earth is life-giving. The great treasure of the sage is their position. What preserves that position is humaneness; what gathers people is wealth. To manage wealth, rectify words, and prevent wrongdoing among the people is called righteousness.

XICI-L-02-01.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 2 Unit 1
XICI-L-02-01.original: 古者包犧氏之王天下也，仰則觀象於天，俯則觀法於地，觀鳥獸之文，與地之宜，近取諸身，遠取諸物；於是始作八卦，以通神明之德，以類萬物之情。作結繩而為罔罟，以佃以漁，蓋取諸離。
XICI-L-02-01.translation: In ancient times, when Bao Xi ruled the world, the person looked upward and observed the images in heaven; the person looked downward and observed the patterns on earth. The person studied the markings of birds and beasts and the adaptations of each region. Near at hand the person took examples from their own body; farther away the person took examples from other things. The person then created the eight trigrams, in order to comprehend the virtue of spiritual intelligence and to classify the conditions of all things. The person knotted cords and made nets for hunting and fishing, taking the idea from Li.

XICI-L-02-02.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 2 Unit 2
XICI-L-02-02.original: 包犧氏沒，神農氏作，斲木為耜，揉木為耒，耒耨之利，以教天下，蓋取諸益。日中為市，致天下之民，聚天下之貨，交易而退，各得其所，蓋取諸噬嗑。
XICI-L-02-02.translation: After Bao Xi died, Shen Nong arose. The person cut wood to make a ploughshare and bent wood to make a plough handle, teaching the world the benefit of ploughing and weeding; this was taken from Yi. At midday the person established markets, bringing together the people and goods of the world. They exchanged what they had and then withdrew, each obtaining what was appropriate; this was taken from Shi The person.

XICI-L-02-03.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 2 Unit 3
XICI-L-02-03.original: 神農氏沒，黃帝、堯、舜氏作，通其變，使民不倦；神而化之，使民宜之；易窮則變，變則通，通則久；是以自天祐之，吉无不利。黃帝、堯、舜垂衣裳而天下治，蓋取諸乾坤。
XICI-L-02-03.translation: After Shen Nong died, Huang Di, Yao, and Shun arose. They carried change forward so that the people did not grow weary; they transformed things with spirit-like efficacy so that the people found them fitting. When the Yi reaches an extreme, it changes; through change it becomes continuous; through continuity it endures. Therefore, “Help comes from heaven; good fortune, nothing unfavorable.” Huang Di, Yao, and Shun let their upper and lower garments hang down, and the world was brought to order; this was taken from Qian and Kun.

XICI-L-02-04.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 2 Unit 4
XICI-L-02-04.original: 刳木為舟，剡木為楫，舟楫之利以濟不通，致遠以利天下，蓋取諸渙。
XICI-L-02-04.translation: The passage makes this point: they hollowed wood to make boats and shaped wood to make oars. The usefulness of boats and oars opened routes that had been blocked and carried people far away for the benefit of the world; this was taken from Huan.

XICI-L-02-05.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 2 Unit 5
XICI-L-02-05.original: 服牛乘馬，引重致遠以利天下，蓋取諸隨。重門擊柝以待暴客，蓋取諸豫。
XICI-L-02-05.translation: In everyday terms, the idea is this: they yoked oxen and rode horses, drawing heavy loads and reaching distant places for the benefit of the world; this was taken from Sui. They installed double gates and beat clappers to guard against violent intruders; this was taken from Yu.

XICI-L-02-06.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 2 Unit 6
XICI-L-02-06.original: 斷木為杵，掘地為臼，臼杵之利，萬民以濟，蓋取諸小過。
XICI-L-02-06.translation: The passage makes this point: they cut wood to make pestles and dug the ground to make mortars. The usefulness of mortar and pestle benefited the multitude; this was taken from Xiao Guo.

XICI-L-02-07.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 2 Unit 7
XICI-L-02-07.original: 弦木為弧，剡木為矢，弧矢之利，以威天下，蓋取諸睽。
XICI-L-02-07.translation: In everyday terms, the idea is this: they strung wood to make bows and sharpened wood to make arrows. The usefulness of bows and arrows inspired awe throughout the world; this was taken from Kui.

XICI-L-02-08.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 2 Unit 8
XICI-L-02-08.original: 上古穴居而野處，後世聖人易之以宮室，上棟下宇，以待風雨，蓋取諸大壯。
XICI-L-02-08.translation: The passage makes this point: in high antiquity people lived in caves and stayed in the open. Later sages replaced these with houses and rooms, with a ridgepole above and eaves below to shelter them from wind and rain; this was taken from Da Zhuang.

XICI-L-02-09.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 2 Unit 9
XICI-L-02-09.original: 古之葬者，厚衣之以薪，葬之中野，不封不樹，喪期无數，後世聖人易之以棺槨，蓋取諸大過。
XICI-L-02-09.translation: In everyday terms, the idea is this: in ancient burials, the dead were thickly wrapped in firewood and buried in the open country, without mound or planted trees, and there was no fixed mourning period. Later sages replaced this practice with inner and outer coffins; this was taken from Da Guo.

XICI-L-02-10.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 2 Unit 10
XICI-L-02-10.original: 上古結繩而治，後世聖人易之以書契，百官以治，萬民以察，蓋取諸周易/夬。
XICI-L-02-10.translation: In everyday terms, the idea is this: in high antiquity, government was conducted with knotted cords. Later sages replaced them with written documents and tallies, so that officials could govern and the people could understand; this was taken from Guai.

XICI-L-03-01.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 3 Unit 1
XICI-L-03-01.original: 是故易者，象也。象也者，像也。彖者，材也。爻也者，效天下之動者也。是故吉凶生而悔吝著也。
XICI-L-03-01.translation: Therefore the Yi consists of images, and an image is a likeness. The Judgments discuss the material of the hexagrams, while the lines imitate the movements of the world. From these arise good fortune and misfortune, and remorse and regret become manifest.

XICI-L-03-02.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 3 Unit 2
XICI-L-03-02.original: 陽卦多陰，陰卦多陽，其故何也？陽卦奇，陰卦偶。其德行何也？陽一君而二民，君子之道也；陰二君而一民，小人之道也。
XICI-L-03-02.translation: In everyday terms, the idea is this: yang trigrams contain more yin lines, and yin trigrams contain more yang lines. Why is this? A yang trigram is odd, while a yin trigram is even. What does this imply about their conduct? In a yang trigram there is one ruler and two subjects; the way of the noble person. In a yin trigram there are two rulers and one subject; the way of the lesser person.

XICI-L-04-01.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 4 Unit 1
XICI-L-04-01.original: 易曰：「憧憧往來，朋從爾思。」子曰：「天下何思何慮！天下同歸而殊途，一致而百慮，天下何思何慮！日往則月來，月往則日來，日月相推而明生焉。寒往則暑來，暑往則寒來，寒暑相推而歲成焉。往者，屈也；來者，信也。屈信相感而利生焉。尺蠖之屈，以求信也。龍蛇之蟄，以存身也。精義入神，以致用也。利用安身，以崇德也。過此以往，未之或知也。窮神知化，德之盛也。」
XICI-L-04-01.translation: The Yi says, “Restlessly coming and going, your friends follow your thoughts.” The Master said: “What thought or anxiety is there under heaven? Different paths lead to the same destination, and a hundred deliberations arrive at one result. What thought or anxiety is there under heaven? The sun departs and the moon comes; the moon departs and the sun comes. By their mutual succession, light is produced. Cold departs and heat comes; heat departs and cold comes. By their mutual succession, the year is completed. What departs contracts, and what comes expands; through the mutual influence of contraction and expansion, benefit arises. The inchworm contracts in order to extend; dragons and snakes hibernate in order to preserve themselves. Refining principles until they enter the subtle and applying them in practice brings usefulness; making use beneficial and settling oneself securely exalts virtue. Beyond this, perhaps nothing can be known. To exhaust the spiritual and understand transformation is the fullness of virtue.”.

XICI-L-04-02.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 4 Unit 2
XICI-L-04-02.original: 易曰：「困于石，據于蒺蔾，入于其宮，不見其妻，凶。」子曰：「非所困而困焉，名必辱；非所據而據焉，身必危；既辱且危，死期將至，妻其可得見耶！」
XICI-L-04-02.translation: The Yi says, “Oppressed by rocks, the person rests on thorns. The person enters their house and does not see their wife: misfortune.” The Master said: “If one is oppressed by what should not oppress them, their name will surely be disgraced. If the person relies on what the person should not rely on, their person will surely be endangered. Once disgraced and endangered, death is near; how could the person see their wife?”.

XICI-L-04-03.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 4 Unit 3
XICI-L-04-03.original: 易曰：「公用射隼于高墉之上，獲之，无不利。」子曰：「隼者，禽也；弓矢者，器也。射之者，人也。君子藏器於身，待時而動，何不利之有。動而不括，是以出而有獲，語成器而動者也。」
XICI-L-04-03.translation: The Yi says, “The duke shoots a falcon atop a high wall and obtains it; nothing is unfavorable.” The Master said: “The falcon is a bird; the bow and arrow are instruments; the shooter is a person. The noble person keeps the instrument concealed on their person and waits for the proper time to act. How could anything be unfavorable? Because the person acts without obstruction, the person goes forth and obtains their object. This speaks of preparing an instrument and then acting.”.

XICI-L-04-04.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 4 Unit 4
XICI-L-04-04.original: 子曰：「小人不恥不仁，不畏不義，不見利不勸，不威不懲，小懲而大誡，此小人之福也。易曰：『履校滅趾，无咎。』此之謂也。善不積不足以成名，惡不積不足以滅身，小人以小善為无益而弗為也，以小惡為无傷而弗去也；故惡積而不可揜，罪大而不可解。易曰：『何校滅耳，凶。』」
XICI-L-04-04.translation: The Master said: “The lesser person is not ashamed of inhumanity and does not fear unrighteousness. Unless the person sees profit, the person is not encouraged; unless threatened, the person is not corrected. A small punishment that produces a great warning is a blessing for the lesser person. The Yi says, ‘Their feet are placed in the stocks and their toes are destroyed; no blame.’ This is what it means. If good deeds are not accumulated, they are insufficient to establish a reputation; if misfortune deeds are not accumulated, they are insufficient to destroy a person. The lesser person thinks a small good brings no benefit and does not do it; the person thinks a small misfortune causes no harm and does not abandon it. Therefore misfortune accumulates until it cannot be concealed, and guilt grows until it cannot be released. The Yi says, ‘The person wears a cangue and their ears are destroyed: misfortune.’”.

XICI-L-04-05.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 4 Unit 5
XICI-L-04-05.original: 子曰：「危者，安其位者也。亡者，保其存者也。亂者，有其治者也。是故君子安而不忘危，存而不忘亡，治而不忘亂，是以身安而國家可保也。易曰：『其亡其亡，繫于苞桑。』」
XICI-L-04-05.translation: The Master said: “One who keeps danger in mind secures their position; one who keeps ruin in mind preserves what the person possesses; one who keeps disorder in mind maintains good order. Therefore, while safe, the noble person does not forget danger; while secure, the person does not forget ruin; while orderly, the person does not forget disorder. In this way their person is safe and their state and household can be preserved. The Yi says, ‘Will it perish? Will it perish? Bind it to a cluster of mulberry shoots.’”.

XICI-L-04-06.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 4 Unit 6
XICI-L-04-06.original: 子曰：「德薄而位尊，知小而謀大，力小而任重，鮮不及矣。易曰：『鼎折足，覆公餗，其形渥，凶。』言不勝其任也。」
XICI-L-04-06.translation: The Master said: “When virtue is meager but position is honored, knowledge is slight but plans are great, strength is weak but responsibility is heavy, disaster is seldom avoided. The Yi says, ‘The legs of the cauldron break; the duke’s meal is overturned, and their body is soaked: misfortune.’ It means that the person is unequal to their charge.”.

XICI-L-04-07.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 4 Unit 7
XICI-L-04-07.original: 子曰：「知幾其神乎！君子上交不諂，下交不瀆，其知幾乎！幾者，動之微，吉之先見者也。君子見幾而作，不俟終日。易曰：『介于石，不終日，貞吉。』介如石焉，寧用終日，斷可識矣。君子知微知彰，知柔知剛，萬夫之望。」
XICI-L-04-07.translation: The Master said: “Is not the person who knows the subtle beginnings almost spirit-like? In relations with superiors, the noble person does not flatter; in relations with inferiors, the person is not contemptuous. Does the person not understand subtle beginnings? A subtle beginning is the faint start of movement and the earliest appearance of good or bad fortune. The noble person sees it and acts without waiting for the day to end. The Yi says, ‘Firm as a rock, not waiting for the day to end; steadfastness brings good fortune.’ Firm as a rock; why wait for the day to end? The judgment can be known. The noble person knows the hidden and the manifest, the yielding and the firm; the person is the hope of the multitude.”.

XICI-L-04-08.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 4 Unit 8
XICI-L-04-08.original: 子曰：「顏氏之子，其殆庶幾乎！有不善，未嘗不知；知之，未嘗復行也。易曰：『不遠復，无祇悔，元吉。』天地絪縕，萬物化醇；男女構精，萬物化生。易曰：『三人行，則損一人；一人行，則得其友。』言致一也。」
XICI-L-04-08.translation: The Master said: “The son of the Yan family came close indeed! Whenever the person did something wrong, the person always recognized it; once the person recognized it, the person never repeated it. The Yi says, ‘Returning from not far away, without reaching remorse: great good fortune.’ Heaven and earth mingle their vital forces, and all things are transformed and enriched. Male and female unite their essences, and the myriad creatures are transformed and born. The Yi says, ‘When three people travel, one is lost; when one person travels, the person finds a companion.’ This speaks of bringing things to unity.”.

XICI-L-04-09.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 4 Unit 9
XICI-L-04-09.original: 子曰：「君子安其身而後動，易其心而後語，定其交而後求。君子脩此三者，故全也。危以動，則民不與也。懼以語，則民不應也。无交而求，則民不與也。莫之與，則傷之者至矣。易曰：『莫益之，或擊之。立心勿恒，凶。』」
XICI-L-04-09.translation: The Master said: “The noble person settles their own person before taking action, makes their mind easy before speaking, and establishes their relationships before making requests. By cultivating these three things, the noble person remains whole. If the person acts from danger, the people will not join them. If the person speaks from fear, the people will not respond. If the person asks without established relationships, the people will not support them. When no one supports them, those who harm them will arrive. The Yi says, ‘No one benefits them; someone may strike them. The person does not keep their heart constant: misfortune.’”.

XICI-L-05-01.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 5 Unit 1
XICI-L-05-01.original: 子曰：「乾坤，其易之門邪！乾，陽物也；坤，陰物也。陰陽合德，而剛柔有體，以體天地之撰，以通神明之德。」其稱名也，雜而不越，於稽其類，其衰世之意邪！夫易，彰往而察來，而微顯闡幽，開而當名辨物，正言斷辭，則備矣。其稱名也小，其取類也大，其旨遠，其辭文，其言曲而中，其事肆而隱，因貳以濟民行，以明失得之報。
XICI-L-05-01.translation: The Master said: “Are Qian and Kun not the gateway of the Yi? Qian is the yang entity; Kun is the yin entity. Yin and yang unite their powers, while firmness and yielding take form, embodying the operations of heaven and earth and communicating the virtue of spiritual intelligence.” The names used are varied but do not exceed their proper bounds. When their categories are examined, do they not reveal concern about an age of decline? The Yi makes the past manifest and examines what is coming; it makes the subtle visible and discloses what is hidden. It opens things up, assigns fitting names, distinguishes beings, and determines its statements with correct words; therefore it is complete. Its names are small, but the categories it draws upon are great. Its meaning reaches far, its language is refined, its words are indirect yet hit the mark, and its matters are openly set forth yet contain hidden depth. It uses doubt to aid the conduct of the people and to clarify the consequences of loss and gain.

XICI-L-06-01.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 6 Unit 1
XICI-L-06-01.original: 易之興也，其於中古乎！作易者，其有憂患乎！是故：
XICI-L-06-01.translation: The rise of the Yi; was it not in the middle period of antiquity? Did its makers not live with anxiety and distress? Therefore:.

XICI-L-06-02.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 6 Unit 2
XICI-L-06-02.original: 履，德之基也。謙，德之柄也。復，德之本也。恒，德之固也。損，德之脩也。益，德之裕也。困，德之辨也。井，德之地也。巽，德之制也。
XICI-L-06-02.translation: The passage makes this point: lu is the foundation of virtue; Qian is the handle of virtue; Fu is the root of virtue; Heng is the firmness of virtue; Sun is the cultivation of virtue; Yi is the abundance of virtue; Kun is the discernment of virtue; Jing is the ground of virtue; and Xun is the regulation of virtue.

XICI-L-06-03.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 6 Unit 3
XICI-L-06-03.original: 履，和而至。謙，尊而光。復，小而辨於物。恒，雜而不厭。損，先難而後易。益，長裕而不没。困，窮而通。井，居其所而遷。巽，稱而隱。
XICI-L-06-03.translation: In everyday terms, the idea is this: lu is harmonious and reaches its goal. Qian is honored and shines. Fu is small yet distinguishes things. Heng is involved in many circumstances without becoming weary. Sun is difficult first and easy afterward. Yi grows in abundance without contrivance. Kun reaches an extremity yet finds a way through. Jing remains in its place yet conveys benefit. Xun weighs what is fitting while remaining unobtrusive.

XICI-L-06-04.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 6 Unit 4
XICI-L-06-04.original: 履，以和行。謙，以制禮。復，以自知。恒，以一德。損，以遠害。益，以興利。困，以寡怨。井，以辯義。巽，以行權。
XICI-L-06-04.translation: The passage makes this point: lu harmonizes conduct. Qian regulates ritual. Fu enables self-knowledge. Heng unifies virtue. Sun keeps harm at a distance. Yi promotes benefit. Kun reduces resentment. Jing distinguishes what is right. Xun exercises discretion.

XICI-L-07-01.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 7 Unit 1
XICI-L-07-01.original: 易之為書也不可遠，為道也屢遷；變動不居，周流六虛，上下无常，剛柔相易，不可為典要，唯變所適。其出入以度，外內使知懼。又明於憂患與故，无有師保，如臨父母。初率其辭而揆其方，既有典常，苟非其人，道不虛行。
XICI-L-07-01.translation: The Yi as a book must not be kept at a distance, for its way repeatedly changes. Its transformations do not remain in one place but circulate through the six positions. Rising and descending have no fixed rule; the firm and yielding lines exchange places. It cannot be confined to a rigid model, for only change is appropriate. Its coming and going follow measure, causing those outside and within to understand caution. It also clarifies anxiety, serious trouble, and their causes. Though one has no teacher or guardian, it is as if one were approaching one’s parents. At first, follow its words and consider their direction; then its constant principles become evident. Unless there is the right person, however, the way will not operate by itself.

XICI-L-07-02.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 7 Unit 2
XICI-L-07-02.original: 易之為書也，原始要終以為質也。六爻相雜，唯其時物也。其初難知，其上易知，本末也。初辭擬之，卒成之終。若夫雜物撰德，辨是與非，則非其中爻不備。噫，亦要存亡吉凶，則居可知矣。知者觀其彖辭，則思過半矣。
XICI-L-07-02.translation: In everyday terms, the idea is this: the Yi as a book takes the origin as its starting point and the end as its completion. The six lines are intermingled, each according to its time and substance. The first line is difficult to understand, while the top line is easy, for they are beginning and end. The statement for the first line sketches the matter; the final line completes it. To mix the kinds of things, develop their qualities, and distinguish right from wrong cannot be fully accomplished without the middle lines. Ah! If one seeks only to understand survival and ruin, good fortune and misfortune, these can be known from one’s position. A wise person who observes the Judgment will understand more than half.

XICI-L-08-01.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 8 Unit 1
XICI-L-08-01.original: 二與四同功而異位，其善不同：二多譽，四多懼，近也。柔之為道，不利近者，其要無咎，其用柔中也。三與五同功而異位，其遇不同：三多凶，五多功，貴賤之等也。其柔危，其剛勝邪？
XICI-L-08-01.translation: The second and fourth lines have the same function but different positions, so their good qualities differ: the second receives much praise, while the fourth has much fear because it is close to the ruler. The way of the yielding is not beneficial when close; its essential aim is to avoid blame through yielding and centrality. The third and fifth lines have the same function but different positions, so their encounters differ: the third has much misfortune, while the fifth has much achievement, because their ranks are noble and lowly. Is the yielding therefore endangered and the firm victorious?

XICI-L-08-02.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 8 Unit 2
XICI-L-08-02.original: 《易》之為書也，廣大悉備：有天道焉，有人道焉，有地道焉，兼三材而兩之，故六。六者，非它也，三材之道也。道有變動，故曰爻；爻有等，故曰物；物相雜，故曰文；文不當，故吉凶生焉。
XICI-L-08-02.translation: The passage makes this point: the Yi as a book is broad, great, and all-embracing. It contains the way of heaven, the way of humanity, and the way of earth. It combines these Three Powers and doubles them; therefore there are six lines. The six are nothing other than the way of the Three Powers. The way contains change and movement, so the lines are called yao. The lines have ranks, so they are treated as distinct things. The things are intermingled, producing patterns. When a pattern is out of place, good fortune or misfortune arises.

XICI-L-08-03.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 8 Unit 3
XICI-L-08-03.original: 《易》之興也，其當殷之末世，周之盛德邪！當文王與紂之事邪！是故其辭危，危者使平，易者使傾，其道甚大，百物不廢，懼以終始，其要无咎；此之謂易之道也。
XICI-L-08-03.translation: In everyday terms, the idea is this: did the Yi arise at the end of the Shang dynasty, when the virtue of Zhou was flourishing? Did it concern the events of King Wen and the tyrant Zhou? For this reason its statements are filled with danger. Awareness of danger brings peace; complacency leads to collapse. Its way is very great and omits none of all things. Caution at both beginning and end is essential, so that one remains without blame. This is called the way of the Yi.

XICI-L-09-01.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 9 Unit 1
XICI-L-09-01.original: 夫乾，天下之至健也；德行恒易以知險。夫坤，天下之至順也；德行恒簡以知阻。能說諸心，能研諸侯之慮，定天下之吉凶，成天下之亹亹者。是故變化云為，吉事有祥，象事知器，占事知來。
XICI-L-09-01.translation: Qian is the strongest force under heaven; its constant conduct is easy, yet it understands danger. Kun is the most compliant force under heaven; its constant conduct is simple, yet it understands obstruction. They can delight the heart and examine the concerns of those in authority, determine good fortune and misfortune under heaven, and bring the world’s endeavors to completion. Therefore changes, transformations, words, and actions contain signs of fortunate events: by observing images one understands implements, and by divination one understands what is to come.

XICI-L-09-02.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 9 Unit 2
XICI-L-09-02.original: 天地設位，聖人成能；人謀鬼謀，百姓與能。八卦以象告，爻彖以情言，剛柔雜居，而吉凶可見矣。變動以利言，吉凶以情遷。是故愛惡相攻而吉凶生，遠近相取而悔吝生，情偽相感而利害生。凡易之情，近而不相得，則凶或害之，悔且吝。
XICI-L-09-02.translation: Heaven and earth establish their positions, and the sages bring their capacities to completion. Human counsels and counsels sought from spirits allow the people to share in that capacity. The eight trigrams communicate through images; the line statements and Judgments speak through the conditions they express. Firm and yielding lines dwell together, so good fortune and misfortune can be seen. Changes and movements are discussed in terms of benefit; good fortune and misfortune shift according to circumstances. Therefore, when love and hate contend, good fortune and misfortune arise; when what is distant and what is near affect one another, remorse and regret arise; when truth and falsehood influence each other, benefit and harm arise. In every situation shown by the Yi, if things are near yet fail to accord, misfortune or harm follows, together with remorse and regret.

XICI-L-09-03.label: Appended Statements II Chapter 9 Unit 3
XICI-L-09-03.original: 將叛者其辭慚，中心疑者其辭枝；吉人之辭寡，躁人之辭多；誣善之人其辭游，失其守者其辭屈。
XICI-L-09-03.translation: The passage makes this point: the words of one who is about to betray show shame. The words of one whose heart is doubtful are branching and evasive. The words of a fortunate person are few; the words of an agitated person are many. The words of one who falsely accuses the good are wandering; the words of one who has lost integrity are twisted.

SHUOGUA-01-01.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 1 Unit 1
SHUOGUA-01-01.original: 昔者，聖人之作《易》也，幽贊於神明而生蓍。參天兩地而倚數，觀變於陰陽而立卦；發揮於剛柔而生爻；和順於道德而理於義；窮理盡性以至於命。
SHUOGUA-01-01.translation: Anciently, when the sages made the Yi, in order to give mysterious assistance to the spiritual Intelligences, they produced the rules for the use of the divining plant. The number 3 was assigned to heaven, 2 to earth, and from these came the other numbers. They contemplated the changes in the divided and undivided lines by the process of manipulating the stalks, and formed the trigrams; from the movements that took place in the strong and weak lines, they produced their teaching about the separate lines. There ensued a harmonious conformity to the course of duty and to virtue, with a discrimination of what was right in each particular case. They therefore made an exhaustive discrimination of what was right, and effected the complete development of every nature, till they arrived in the Yi at what was appointed for it by Heaven.

SHUOGUA-02-01.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 2 Unit 1
SHUOGUA-02-01.original: 昔者，聖人之作《易》也，將以順性命之理。是以立天之道，曰陰與陽；立地之道，曰柔與剛；立人之道，曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦。分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。
SHUOGUA-02-01.translation: Anciently, when the sages made the Yi, it was with the design that its figures should be in conformity with the principles underlying the natures of men and things, and the ordinances for them appointed by Heaven. With this view they exhibited in them the way of heaven, calling the lines yin and yang; the way of earth, calling them the weak or soft and the strong or hard; and the way of men, under the names of benevolence and righteousness. Each trigram embraced those three Powers; and, being repeated, its full form consisted of six lines. A distinction was made of the places assigned to the yin and yang lines, which were variously occupied, now by the strong and now by the weak forms, and therefore the figure of each hexagram was completed.

SHUOGUA-03-01.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 3 Unit 1
SHUOGUA-03-01.original: 天地定位，山澤通氣，雷風相薄，水火不相射。八卦相錯，數往者順，知來者逆。是故易逆數也。
SHUOGUA-03-01.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: the symbols of heaven and earth received their determinate positions; those for mountains and collections of water interchanged their influences; those for thunder and wind excited each other the more; and those for water and fire did each other no harm. Then among these eight symbols there was a mutual communication. The numbering of the past is a natural process; the knowledge of the coming is anticipation. Therefore in the Yi we have both anticipation and the natural process.

SHUOGUA-04-01.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 4 Unit 1
SHUOGUA-04-01.original: 雷以動之，風以散之，雨以潤之，日以烜之，艮以止之，兌以說之，乾以君之，坤以藏之。
SHUOGUA-04-01.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: thunder sets things in motion; wind disperses them; rain moistens them; the sun warms them; Gen stops them; Dui gives them joy; Qian rules them; and Kun stores them.

SHUOGUA-05-01.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 5 Unit 1
SHUOGUA-05-01.original: 帝出乎震，齊乎巽，相見乎離，致役乎坤，說言乎兌，戰乎乾，勞乎坎，成言乎艮。
SHUOGUA-05-01.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: the divine power comes forth in Zhen, brings all things into order in Xun, makes them visible in Li, receives their service in Kun, brings joy in Dui, struggles in Qian, labors in Kan, and completes them in Gen.

SHUOGUA-05-02.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 5 Unit 2
SHUOGUA-05-02.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: all things emerge in Zhen, which corresponds to the east.

SHUOGUA-05-03.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 5 Unit 3
SHUOGUA-05-03.original: 齊乎巽，巽，東南也，齊也者，言萬物之潔齊也。
SHUOGUA-05-03.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: all things are brought into order in Xun, which corresponds to the southeast. Here, order means that all things become clean and evenly arranged.

SHUOGUA-05-04.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 5 Unit 4
SHUOGUA-05-04.original: 離也者，明也，萬物皆相見，南方之卦也。聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，蓋取諸此也。
SHUOGUA-05-04.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: li means brightness. It is the trigram of the south, where all things become visible to one another. The sage faces south, listens to the world, and governs toward the light; this image comes from Li.

SHUOGUA-05-05.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 5 Unit 5
SHUOGUA-05-05.original: 坤也者，地也，萬物皆致養焉，故曰致役乎坤。
SHUOGUA-05-05.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: kun means earth. All things receive nourishment from it; therefore all things render their service in Kun.

SHUOGUA-05-06.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 5 Unit 6
SHUOGUA-05-06.original: 兌，正秋也。萬物之所說也。故曰說；言乎兌。
SHUOGUA-05-06.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: dui corresponds to autumn, the season when all things rejoice; therefore joy is expressed in Dui.

SHUOGUA-05-07.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 5 Unit 7
SHUOGUA-05-07.original: 戰乎乾，乾，西北之卦也。言陰陽相薄也。
SHUOGUA-05-07.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: the struggle takes place in Qian, the trigram of the northwest, where yin and yang press against each other.

SHUOGUA-05-08.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 5 Unit 8
SHUOGUA-05-08.original: 坎者，水也，正北方之卦也，勞卦也，萬物之所歸也，故曰勞乎坎。
SHUOGUA-05-08.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: kan means water and corresponds to the north. It is the trigram of labor, where all things return; therefore labor is expressed in Kan.

SHUOGUA-05-09.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 5 Unit 9
SHUOGUA-05-09.original: 艮，東北之卦也，萬物之所成，終而所成始也，故曰成言乎艮。
SHUOGUA-05-09.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: gen corresponds to the northeast. There all things complete their ending and begin again; therefore completion is expressed in Gen.

SHUOGUA-06-01.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 6 Unit 1
SHUOGUA-06-01.original: 神也者。妙萬物而為言者也。
SHUOGUA-06-01.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: here, spirit means the subtle power through which all things are transformed and made effective.

SHUOGUA-06-02.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 6 Unit 2
SHUOGUA-06-02.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: nothing moves all things more quickly than thunder.

SHUOGUA-06-03.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 6 Unit 3
SHUOGUA-06-03.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: nothing bends and disperses all things more effectively than wind.

SHUOGUA-06-04.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 6 Unit 4
SHUOGUA-06-04.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: nothing dries all things more thoroughly than fire.

SHUOGUA-06-05.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 6 Unit 5
SHUOGUA-06-05.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: nothing brings greater joy to all things than a lake or marsh.

SHUOGUA-06-06.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 6 Unit 6
SHUOGUA-06-06.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: nothing moistens and enriches all things more fully than water.

SHUOGUA-06-07.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 6 Unit 7
SHUOGUA-06-07.original: 終萬物、始萬物者，莫盛乎艮。
SHUOGUA-06-07.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: nothing completes all things and begins them again more fully than Gen.

SHUOGUA-06-08.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 6 Unit 8
SHUOGUA-06-08.original: 故水火相逮，雷風不相悖，山澤通氣，然後能變化，既成萬物也。
SHUOGUA-06-08.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: water and fire support each other; thunder and wind do not oppose each other; mountain and lake exchange vital energy. Through these relationships, change becomes possible and all things are completed.

SHUOGUA-07-01.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 7 Unit 1
SHUOGUA-07-01.original: 乾，健也。坤，順也。震，動也。巽，入也。坎，陷也。離，麗也。艮，止也。兌，說也。
SHUOGUA-07-01.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: qian means strength; Kun, receptiveness; Zhen, movement; Xun, entering; Kan, danger; Li, attachment and brightness; Gen, stopping; and Dui, joy.

SHUOGUA-08-01.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 8 Unit 1
SHUOGUA-08-01.original: 乾為馬，坤為牛，震為龍，巽為雞，坎為豕，離為雉，艮為狗，兌為羊。
SHUOGUA-08-01.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: qian corresponds to the horse; Kun to the ox; Zhen to the dragon; Xun to the rooster; Kan to the pig; Li to the pheasant; Gen to the dog; and Dui to the sheep.

SHUOGUA-09-01.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 9 Unit 1
SHUOGUA-09-01.original: 乾為首，坤為腹，震為足，巽為股，坎為耳，離為目，艮為手，兌為口。
SHUOGUA-09-01.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: qian corresponds to the head; Kun to the abdomen; Zhen to the feet; Xun to the thighs; Kan to the ears; Li to the eyes; Gen to the hands; and Dui to the mouth.

SHUOGUA-10-01.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 10 Unit 1
SHUOGUA-10-01.original: 乾，天也，故稱乎父；坤，地也，故稱乎母； 震一索而得男，故謂之長男；巽一索而得女，故謂之長女； 坎再索而得男，故謂之中男；離再索而得女，故謂之中女； 艮三索而得男，故謂之少男；兌三索而得女，故謂之少女。
SHUOGUA-10-01.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: qian is heaven and is called the father; Kun is earth and is called the mother. Zhen receives the first yang line and is called the eldest son. Xun receives the first yin line and is called the eldest daughter. Kan receives the second yang line and is called the middle son. Li receives the second yin line and is called the middle daughter. Gen receives the third yang line and is called the youngest son. Dui receives the third yin line and is called the youngest daughter.

SHUOGUA-11-01.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 1
SHUOGUA-11-01.original: 乾為天、為圜、為君、為父、為玉、為金、為寒、為冰、為大赤、為良馬、為老馬、為瘠馬、為駁馬、為木果。
SHUOGUA-11-01.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: qian corresponds to heaven, a circle, a ruler, a father, jade, metal, cold, ice, deep red, a good horse, an old horse, a thin horse, a piebald horse, and tree fruit.

SHUOGUA-11-02.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 2
SHUOGUA-11-02.original: 坤為地、為母、為布、為釜、為吝嗇、為均、為子母牛、為大輿、為文、為眾、為柄。
SHUOGUA-11-02.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: kun corresponds to earth, a mother, cloth, a cooking pot, frugality, evenness, a cow with its calf, a large wagon, pattern, a multitude, and a handle.

SHUOGUA-11-03.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 3
SHUOGUA-11-03.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: among kinds of earth, Kun corresponds to black soil.

SHUOGUA-11-04.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 4
SHUOGUA-11-04.original: 震為雷、為龍、為玄黃、為敷、為大涂、為長子、為決躁、為蒼筤竹、為萑葦。
SHUOGUA-11-04.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: zhen corresponds to thunder, the dragon, dark yellow, spreading growth, a great road, the eldest son, decisiveness and restlessness, young green bamboo, and reeds.

SHUOGUA-11-05.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 5
SHUOGUA-11-05.original: 其於馬也，為善鳴、為馵足，為的顙。
SHUOGUA-11-05.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: among horses, Zhen corresponds to one that neighs well, has a marked hind foot, or has a white forehead.

SHUOGUA-11-06.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 6
SHUOGUA-11-06.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: among crops, Zhen corresponds to plants that return to life.

SHUOGUA-11-07.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 7
SHUOGUA-11-07.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: at its fullest development, Zhen becomes vigorous, lush, and fresh.

SHUOGUA-11-08.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 8
SHUOGUA-11-08.original: 巽為木、為風、為長女、為繩直、為工、為白、為長、為高、為進退、為不果、為臭。
SHUOGUA-11-08.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: xun corresponds to wood, wind, the eldest daughter, a straight cord, craftsmanship, white, length, height, advance and retreat, indecision, and scent.

SHUOGUA-11-09.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 9
SHUOGUA-11-09.original: 其於人也，為寡髮、為廣顙、為多白眼、為近利市三倍。
SHUOGUA-11-09.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: among people, Xun corresponds to sparse hair, a broad forehead, much white in the eyes, and pursuing nearby profit, even seeking threefold gain in the market.

SHUOGUA-11-10.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 10
SHUOGUA-11-10.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: at its fullest development, Xun becomes the trigram of restlessness.

SHUOGUA-11-11.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 11
SHUOGUA-11-11.original: 坎為水、為溝瀆、為隱伏、為矯輮、為弓輪。
SHUOGUA-11-11.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: kan corresponds to water, channels and ditches, concealment, bending and straightening, the bow, and the wheel.

SHUOGUA-11-12.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 12
SHUOGUA-11-12.original: 其於人也，為加憂、為心病、為耳痛、為血卦、為赤。
SHUOGUA-11-12.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: among people, Kan corresponds to increased worry, illness of the heart, ear pain, blood, and the color red.

SHUOGUA-11-13.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 13
SHUOGUA-11-13.original: 其於馬也，為美脊、為亟心、為下首、為薄蹄、為曳。
SHUOGUA-11-13.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: among horses, Kan corresponds to a fine back, an anxious heart, a lowered head, thin hooves, and a dragging gait.

SHUOGUA-11-14.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 14
SHUOGUA-11-14.original: 其於輿也，為多眚、為通、為月、為盜。
SHUOGUA-11-14.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: among vehicles, Kan corresponds to one with many defects. It also corresponds to penetration, the moon, and a thief.

SHUOGUA-11-15.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 15
SHUOGUA-11-15.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: among trees, Kan corresponds to wood that is hard and has much inner pith.

SHUOGUA-11-16.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 16
SHUOGUA-11-16.original: 離為火、為日、為電、為中女、為甲冑、為戈兵。
SHUOGUA-11-16.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: li corresponds to fire, the sun, lightning, the middle daughter, armor and helmets, spears, and weapons.

SHUOGUA-11-17.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 17
SHUOGUA-11-17.original: 其於人也，為大腹、為乾卦、為鱉、為蟹、為蠃、為蚌、為龜。
SHUOGUA-11-17.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: among people and creatures, Li corresponds to a large belly, dryness, the soft-shelled turtle, crab, snail, mussel, and tortoise.

SHUOGUA-11-18.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 18
SHUOGUA-11-18.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: among trees, Li corresponds to a hollow trunk with a dry upper part.

SHUOGUA-11-19.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 19
SHUOGUA-11-19.original: 艮為山、為徑路、為小石、為門闕、為果蓏、為閽寺、為指、為狗、為鼠、為黔喙之屬。
SHUOGUA-11-19.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: gen corresponds to a mountain, a narrow path, a small stone, a gateway, fruits and gourds, a gatekeeper or eunuch, a finger, a dog, a rat, and dark-billed creatures.

SHUOGUA-11-20.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 20
SHUOGUA-11-20.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: among trees, Gen corresponds to wood that is hard and has many joints.

SHUOGUA-11-21.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 21
SHUOGUA-11-21.original: 兌為澤、為少女、為巫、為口舌、為毀折、為附決。
SHUOGUA-11-21.translation: This passage describes the trigrams as follows: dui corresponds to a lake or marsh, the youngest daughter, a ritual medium, the mouth and tongue, breaking and damage, and fruit that is attached but ready to fall.

SHUOGUA-11-22.label: Discussion of Trigrams Chapter 11 Unit 22
SHUOGUA-11-22.original: 其於地也，為剛鹵，為妾、為羊。
SHUOGUA-11-22.translation: The trigrams are described here in this way: among kinds of earth, Dui corresponds to hard salty ground. It also corresponds to a concubine and a sheep.

XUGUA-01-01.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 1
XUGUA-01-01.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: after heaven and earth came into existence, all things were born.

XUGUA-01-02.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 2
XUGUA-01-02.original: 盈天地之間者，唯萬物，故受之以屯；屯者盈也，屯者物之始生也。
XUGUA-01-02.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: what fills the space between heaven and earth is nothing but all things; therefore Zhun follows. Zhun means fullness and is the beginning of things coming to birth.

XUGUA-01-03.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 3
XUGUA-01-03.original: 物生必蒙，故受之以蒙；蒙者蒙也，物之穉也。
XUGUA-01-03.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: things newly born are necessarily immature; therefore Meng follows. Meng means immaturity; the youth of things.

XUGUA-01-04.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 4
XUGUA-01-04.original: 物穉不可不養也，故受之以需；需者飲食之道也。
XUGUA-01-04.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: young things must be nourished; therefore Xu follows. Xu concerns the way of food and drink.

XUGUA-01-05.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 5
XUGUA-01-05.original: 飲食必有訟，故受之以訟。
XUGUA-01-05.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: food and drink inevitably give rise to contention; therefore Song follows.

XUGUA-01-06.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 6
XUGUA-01-06.original: 訟必有眾起，故受之以師；師者眾也。
XUGUA-01-06.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: contention inevitably causes crowds to arise; therefore Shi follows. Shi means a multitude.

XUGUA-01-07.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 7
XUGUA-01-07.original: 眾必有所比，故受之以比；比者比也。
XUGUA-01-07.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: a multitude must have those with whom it associates; therefore Bi follows. Bi means association.

XUGUA-01-08.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 8
XUGUA-01-08.original: 比必有所畜也，故受之以小畜。
XUGUA-01-08.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: association necessarily involves accumulation; therefore Xiao Xu follows.

XUGUA-01-09.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 9
XUGUA-01-09.original: 物畜然後有禮，故受之以履。
XUGUA-01-09.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: after things are accumulated, ritual order becomes possible; therefore Lu follows.

XUGUA-01-10.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 10
XUGUA-01-10.original: 履而泰，然後安，故受之以泰；泰者通也。
XUGUA-01-10.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: by treading the proper way one reaches peace, and then security; therefore Tai follows. Tai means free communication.

XUGUA-01-11.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 11
XUGUA-01-11.original: 物不可以終通，故受之以否。
XUGUA-01-11.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: things cannot remain forever in free communication; therefore Pi follows.

XUGUA-01-12.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 12
XUGUA-01-12.original: 物不可以終否，故受之以同人。
XUGUA-01-12.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: things cannot remain forever obstructed; therefore Tong Ren follows.

XUGUA-01-13.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 13
XUGUA-01-13.original: 與人同者，物必歸焉，故受之以大有。
XUGUA-01-13.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: those who unite with others necessarily attract things to themselves; therefore Da You follows.

XUGUA-01-14.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 14
XUGUA-01-14.original: 有大者不可以盈，故受之以謙。
XUGUA-01-14.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: one who possesses greatness must not let it overflow; therefore Qian follows.

XUGUA-01-15.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 15
XUGUA-01-15.original: 有大而能謙，必豫，故受之以豫。
XUGUA-01-15.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: one who possesses greatness and can remain modest will surely have joy; therefore Yu follows.

XUGUA-01-16.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 16
XUGUA-01-16.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: joy inevitably brings followers; therefore Sui follows.

XUGUA-01-17.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 17
XUGUA-01-17.original: 以喜隨人者，必有事，故受之以蠱；蠱者事也。
XUGUA-01-17.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: one who gladly follows others will necessarily have affairs to manage; therefore Gu follows. Gu means affairs requiring correction.

XUGUA-01-18.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 18
XUGUA-01-18.original: 有事而后可大，故受之以臨；臨者大也。
XUGUA-01-18.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: only after there are affairs to manage can greatness develop; therefore Lin follows. Lin means greatness approaching.

XUGUA-01-19.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 19
XUGUA-01-19.original: 物大然後可觀，故受之以觀。
XUGUA-01-19.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: only after things become great can they be observed; therefore Guan follows.

XUGUA-01-20.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 20
XUGUA-01-20.original: 可觀而后有所合，故受之以噬嗑；嗑者合也。
XUGUA-01-20.translation: After something can be observed, union becomes possible; therefore Shi The person follows. The person means joining.

XUGUA-01-21.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 21
XUGUA-01-21.original: 物不可以苟合而已，故受之以賁；賁者飾也。
XUGUA-01-21.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: things must not merely unite carelessly; therefore Bi follows. Bi means adornment.

XUGUA-01-22.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 22
XUGUA-01-22.original: 致飾然後亨，則盡矣，故受之以剝；剝者剝也。
XUGUA-01-22.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: when adornment is carried to completion, prosperity reaches its limit; therefore Bo follows. Bo means stripping away.

XUGUA-01-23.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 23
XUGUA-01-23.original: 物不可以終盡，剝窮上反下，故受之以復。
XUGUA-01-23.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: things cannot be exhausted forever. When stripping away reaches the top, it returns below; therefore Fu follows.

XUGUA-01-24.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 24
XUGUA-01-24.original: 復則不妄矣，故受之以无妄。
XUGUA-01-24.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: with return, one no longer acts falsely; therefore Wu Wang follows.

XUGUA-01-25.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 25
XUGUA-01-25.original: 有无妄然後可畜，故受之以大畜。
XUGUA-01-25.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: only with freedom from falsehood can there be accumulation; therefore Da Xu follows.

XUGUA-01-26.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 26
XUGUA-01-26.original: 物畜然後可養，故受之以頤；頤者養也。
XUGUA-01-26.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: after things are accumulated, they can be nourished; therefore Yi follows. Yi means nourishment.

XUGUA-01-27.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 27
XUGUA-01-27.original: 不養則不可動，故受之以大過。
XUGUA-01-27.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: without nourishment, there can be no movement; therefore Da Guo follows.

XUGUA-01-28.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 28
XUGUA-01-28.original: 物不可以終過，故受之以坎；坎者陷也。
XUGUA-01-28.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: things cannot remain forever in excess; therefore Kan follows. Kan means a pitfall.

XUGUA-01-29.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 29
XUGUA-01-29.original: 陷必有所麗，故受之以離；離者麗也。
XUGUA-01-29.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: what falls into a pit must attach itself somewhere; therefore Li follows. Li means attachment.

XUGUA-02-01.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 1
XUGUA-02-01.original: 有天地然後有萬物，有萬物然後有男女，有男女然後有夫婦，有夫婦然後有父子，有父子然後有君臣，有君臣然後有上下，有上下然後禮儀有所錯。
XUGUA-02-01.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: after heaven and earth exist, there are all things; after all things, male and female; after male and female, husband and wife; after husband and wife, father and child; after father and child, ruler and minister; after ruler and minister, superior and subordinate. Once superior and subordinate exist, rites and proper conduct have places in which to be arranged.

XUGUA-02-02.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 2
XUGUA-02-02.original: 夫婦之道，不可以不久也，故受之以恆；恆者久也。
XUGUA-02-02.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: the way of husband and wife cannot fail to endure; therefore Heng follows. Heng means duration.

XUGUA-02-03.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 3
XUGUA-02-03.original: 物不可以久居其所，故受之以遯；遯者退也。
XUGUA-02-03.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: things cannot remain forever in the same place; therefore Dun follows. Dun means withdrawal.

XUGUA-02-04.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 4
XUGUA-02-04.original: 物不可終遯，故受之以大壯。
XUGUA-02-04.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: things cannot withdraw forever; therefore Da Zhuang follows.

XUGUA-02-05.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 5
XUGUA-02-05.original: 物不可以終壯，故受之以晉；晉者進也。
XUGUA-02-05.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: things cannot remain forever strong; therefore Jin follows. Jin means advance.

XUGUA-02-06.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 6
XUGUA-02-06.original: 進必有所傷，故受之以明夷；夷者傷也。
XUGUA-02-06.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: advance necessarily brings the possibility of injury; therefore Ming Yi follows. Yi means injury.

XUGUA-02-07.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 7
