XUGUA-02-07.original: 傷於外者，必反其家，故受之以家人。
XUGUA-02-07.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: one who is injured outside necessarily returns home; therefore Jia Ren follows.

XUGUA-02-08.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 8
XUGUA-02-08.original: 家道窮必乖，故受之以睽；睽者乖也。
XUGUA-02-08.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: when the way of the household reaches an impasse, estrangement follows; therefore Kui follows. Kui means estrangement.

XUGUA-02-09.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 9
XUGUA-02-09.original: 乖必有難，故受之以蹇；蹇者難也。
XUGUA-02-09.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: estrangement necessarily brings difficulty; therefore Jian follows. Jian means difficulty.

XUGUA-02-10.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 10
XUGUA-02-10.original: 物不可終難，故受之以解；解者緩也。
XUGUA-02-10.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: things cannot remain forever in difficulty; therefore Xie follows. Xie means release and easing.

XUGUA-02-11.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 11
XUGUA-02-11.original: 緩必有所失，故受之以損。
XUGUA-02-11.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: relaxation necessarily entails some loss; therefore Sun follows.

XUGUA-02-12.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 12
XUGUA-02-12.original: 損而不已，必益，故受之以益。
XUGUA-02-12.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: when decrease continues without stopping, increase necessarily follows; therefore Yi follows.

XUGUA-02-13.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 13
XUGUA-02-13.original: 益而不已，必決，故受之以夬； 夬者決也。
XUGUA-02-13.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: when increase continues without stopping, a decisive break necessarily follows; therefore Guai follows. Guai means decision.

XUGUA-02-14.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 14
XUGUA-02-14.original: 決必有所遇，故受之以姤；姤者遇也。
XUGUA-02-14.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: decision necessarily leads to an encounter; therefore Gou follows. Gou means encounter.

XUGUA-02-15.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 15
XUGUA-02-15.original: 物相遇而后聚，故受之以萃；萃者聚也。
XUGUA-02-15.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: after things encounter one another, they gather; therefore Cui follows. Cui means gathering.

XUGUA-02-16.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 16
XUGUA-02-16.original: 聚而上者，謂之升，故受之以升。
XUGUA-02-16.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: what gathers and rises is called Sheng; therefore Sheng follows.

XUGUA-02-17.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 17
XUGUA-02-17.original: 升而不已，必困，故受之以困。
XUGUA-02-17.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: if rising continues without stopping, exhaustion necessarily follows; therefore Kun follows.

XUGUA-02-18.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 18
XUGUA-02-18.original: 困乎上者，必反下，故受之以井。
XUGUA-02-18.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: what is exhausted above necessarily returns below; therefore Jing follows.

XUGUA-02-19.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 19
XUGUA-02-19.original: 井道不可不革，故受之以革。
XUGUA-02-19.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: the way of the well cannot avoid renewal; therefore Ge follows.

XUGUA-02-20.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 20
XUGUA-02-20.original: 革物者莫若鼎，故受之以鼎。
XUGUA-02-20.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: nothing transforms things better than the cauldron; therefore Ding follows.

XUGUA-02-21.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 21
XUGUA-02-21.original: 主器者莫若長子，故受之以震；震者動也。
XUGUA-02-21.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: no one is better suited to preside over the ritual vessel than the eldest son; therefore Zhen follows. Zhen means movement.

XUGUA-02-22.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 22
XUGUA-02-22.original: 物不可以終動，止之，故受之以艮；艮者止也。
XUGUA-02-22.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: things cannot remain forever in motion; they must be stopped. Therefore Gen follows. Gen means stopping.

XUGUA-02-23.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 23
XUGUA-02-23.original: 物不可以終止，故受之以漸；漸者進也。
XUGUA-02-23.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: things cannot remain forever stopped; therefore Jian follows. Jian means gradual advance.

XUGUA-02-24.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 24
XUGUA-02-24.original: 進必有所歸，故受之以歸妹。
XUGUA-02-24.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: advance necessarily has a destination; therefore Gui Mei follows.

XUGUA-02-25.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 25
XUGUA-02-25.original: 得其所歸者必大，故受之以豐；豐者大也。
XUGUA-02-25.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: one who reaches the place to which one belongs necessarily becomes great; therefore Feng follows. Feng means abundance and greatness.

XUGUA-02-26.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 26
XUGUA-02-26.original: 窮大者必失其居，故受之以旅。
XUGUA-02-26.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: when greatness is exhausted, one necessarily loses one’s dwelling; therefore Lu follows.

XUGUA-02-27.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 27
XUGUA-02-27.original: 旅而無所容，故受之以巽；巽者入也。
XUGUA-02-27.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: a traveler who has nowhere to be received must enter somewhere; therefore Xun follows. Xun means entering.

XUGUA-02-28.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 28
XUGUA-02-28.original: 入而后說之，故受之以兌；兌者說也。
XUGUA-02-28.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: after entering, one rejoices; therefore Dui follows. Dui means joy.

XUGUA-02-29.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 29
XUGUA-02-29.original: 說而后散之，故受之以渙；渙者離也。
XUGUA-02-29.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: after joy, things disperse; therefore Huan follows. Huan means dispersion and separation.

XUGUA-02-30.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 30
XUGUA-02-30.original: 物不可以終離，故受之以節。
XUGUA-02-30.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: things cannot remain forever dispersed; therefore Jie follows.

XUGUA-02-31.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 31
XUGUA-02-31.original: 節而信之，故受之以中孚。
XUGUA-02-31.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: restraint gives rise to trust; therefore Zhong Fu follows.

XUGUA-02-32.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 32
XUGUA-02-32.original: 有其信者，必行之，故受之以小過。
XUGUA-02-32.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: one who possesses trust necessarily puts it into action; therefore Xiao Guo follows.

XUGUA-02-33.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 33
XUGUA-02-33.original: 有過物者，必濟，故受之既濟。
XUGUA-02-33.translation: The sequence moves forward for this reason: one who surpasses things necessarily brings them across; therefore Ji Ji follows.

XUGUA-02-34.label: Sequence of Hexagrams Chapter 2 Unit 34
XUGUA-02-34.original: 物不可窮也，故受之以未濟；終焉。
XUGUA-02-34.translation: This is how the next hexagram follows: things cannot be exhausted; therefore Wei Ji follows, and with it the sequence comes to an end.

ZAGUA-01-01.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 1
ZAGUA-01-01.translation: Qian represents strength, while Kun represents receptiveness. Bi is about closeness and shared joy, while Shi carries the worries of organized conflict.

ZAGUA-01-02.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 2
ZAGUA-01-02.translation: Lin means actively approaching others. Guan means observing, or being looked to as an example.

ZAGUA-01-03.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 3
ZAGUA-01-03.original: 屯見而不失其居，蒙雜而著。
ZAGUA-01-03.translation: Zhun shows new life appearing in a difficult situation without losing its base. Meng shows confusion that can gradually become clear through guidance.

ZAGUA-01-04.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 4
ZAGUA-01-04.translation: Zhen means starting to move. Gen means stopping.

ZAGUA-01-05.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 5
ZAGUA-01-05.translation: The paired hexagrams are contrasted this way: sun and Yi mark the beginnings of decline and growth.

ZAGUA-01-06.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 6
ZAGUA-01-06.translation: Da Xu is about waiting for the right time. Wu Wang warns that unexpected trouble may still occur even when no reckless action has been taken.

ZAGUA-01-07.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 7
ZAGUA-01-07.translation: Cui means people gathering together. Sheng means rising step by step instead of waiting for success to arrive on its own.

ZAGUA-01-08.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 8
ZAGUA-01-08.translation: Qian lowers the self through humility. Yu can become careless when enjoyment turns into complacency.

ZAGUA-01-09.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 9
ZAGUA-01-09.translation: Shi He is like biting through something to remove an obstruction. Bi reaches its highest form when decoration returns to simplicity.

ZAGUA-01-10.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 10
ZAGUA-01-10.translation: Dui shows joy openly. Xun works by entering gently and keeping its force less visible.

ZAGUA-01-11.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 11
ZAGUA-01-11.translation: Sui means adapting to circumstances instead of clinging to old habits. Gu means correcting problems that have built up over time.

ZAGUA-01-12.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 12
ZAGUA-01-12.translation: Bo means gradual stripping away and decay. Fu means returning to the right path.

ZAGUA-01-13.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 13
ZAGUA-01-13.translation: Jin is like daylight advancing in brightness. Ming Yi is light being injured, hidden, or suppressed.

ZAGUA-01-14.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 14
ZAGUA-01-14.translation: Jing connects above and below and supplies everyone. Kun brings several forms of obstruction together.

ZAGUA-01-15.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 15
ZAGUA-01-15.translation: Xian describes a quick response between people. Heng emphasizes lasting commitment.

ZAGUA-01-16.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 16
ZAGUA-01-16.translation: Huan means dispersing and releasing what is blocked. Jie means setting limits and knowing when to stop.

ZAGUA-01-17.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 17
ZAGUA-01-17.translation: Xie means that difficulty is easing. Jian means that the road ahead is hard.

ZAGUA-01-18.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 18
ZAGUA-01-18.translation: Kui emphasizes outward difference and separation. Jia Ren emphasizes order within the family.

ZAGUA-01-19.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 19
ZAGUA-01-19.translation: Pi is blockage, while Tai is free flow. Their situations are opposites.

ZAGUA-01-20.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 20
ZAGUA-01-20.translation: Da Zhuang warns that even great strength must know when to stop. Dun means choosing to withdraw when the time is unfavorable.

ZAGUA-01-21.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 21
ZAGUA-01-21.translation: Da You means abundance and many people gathering in support. Tong Ren means people drawing close and working together.

ZAGUA-01-22.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 22
ZAGUA-01-22.translation: Ge removes an outdated order. Ding establishes a new order and brings the reform into stable use.

ZAGUA-01-23.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 23
ZAGUA-01-23.translation: Xiao Guo permits a small departure from the usual rule. Zhong Fu centers on inner sincerity and trust.

ZAGUA-01-24.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 24
ZAGUA-01-24.translation: Feng contains great abundance, so it also brings many matters to handle. A traveler has few close companions while away from home.

ZAGUA-01-25.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 25
ZAGUA-01-25.translation: The fire of Li moves upward, while the water of Kan moves downward.

ZAGUA-01-26.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 26
ZAGUA-01-26.translation: Xiao Xu gathers strength in small amounts. Lu requires careful movement and does not allow a person simply to sit still.

ZAGUA-01-27.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 27
ZAGUA-01-27.translation: Xu waits before danger instead of rushing forward. Song is conflict, so the parties cannot easily draw close.

ZAGUA-01-28.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 28
ZAGUA-01-28.original: 大過顛也，姤遇也，柔遇剛也。
ZAGUA-01-28.translation: Da Guo carries more weight than the structure can bear and may overturn. Gou is an unexpected meeting in which yielding force encounters firm force.

ZAGUA-01-29.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 29
ZAGUA-01-29.original: 漸女歸待男行也，頤養正也，既濟定也。
ZAGUA-01-29.translation: Jian compares gradual progress to a woman waiting for marriage to proceed in proper order. Yi is about nourishment that follows what is right. Ji Ji means that affairs have largely been brought into order.

ZAGUA-01-30.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 30
ZAGUA-01-30.original: 歸妹女之終也，未濟男之窮也。
ZAGUA-01-30.translation: Gui Mei uses a young woman's marriage to mark the end of one stage. Wei Ji means that the work is still unfinished and available strength has reached a difficult limit.

ZAGUA-01-31.label: Miscellaneous Hexagrams Chapter 1 Unit 31
ZAGUA-01-31.original: 夬決也，剛決柔也。君子道長，小人道消也。
ZAGUA-01-31.translation: Guai means decisively removing an obstruction: firm force pushes out yielding force. The way of the noble person grows, while the way of the petty person fades.
